title: Motherfucker
about:
i just fucking realized and have come to terms with that I have Autism. It makes so much more sense.

And the fact that I was masking all of these years, and that all of my energy has now made sense. And the social anxiety.

This was driven by anger specifically because those around me shamed me for being the way I was, and that fucking sucks like nobody's dick.

Motherfucker.

FUUUUUUUUUUUUUCKKK

I've never played my acoustic this loud. I was fucking mad.

----

I recorded this purely with my iPhone, improv. I came back a bit later to add some compression, EQ, and limiting. Tried using a de-esser, but it made the acoustic too flat sounding. I used only mild compression, I wanted to keep the dynamic intensity that the experience itself had. I was playing insanely loud, and it was for ZERO concern of sound quality. Clipping really didn't fucking matter. I am thankful for lossless Voice Memos. I only used EQ cuts, no adding. The plain sound itself sounded great on it's own, tried to really let it be itself here, as I have been hearing and learning about. It does seem to work great when you hear it just as it sounded, rather than trying to EQ it into sounding different.

This is the first recording with my Yamaha acoustic's new strings! Did it a few weeks ago. Man, I really need to change strings more often. She sounds so great with fresh strings. It makes me sound like I know what I am doing! ha! Very fucking pleased with this song. Just pure rage, and it seemingly sat together perfectly. Fuck yeah.

title: Recreational Outrage: Volume Three
about:
Hello, as of Aug 7, 2026! This album only necessarily started coming to fruition as of the past 5 days. Will elaborate further. Some things started here and there about a month or two ago though, will provide more insights :)

After I make the artwork, this will be published publicly. This isn't available as I am writing this (8:15 PM). I thought it would be funny to get the third album in before the year anniversary of the first one. That wasn't by design, it just worked out that way haha, lol.

Edit: I think this is temporary album art. I have a few other drawing ideas, but I didn't have time before the end of the night. I want to draw a wind-up robot toy walking through a downtown, destroying everything like Godzilla does.

I took a picture of one of my name logo drawings (been wanting to draw a proper artist logo for a long time now), did some editing, turned it into a vector, then I was kind of going for a 70s funk album look. I really like it! Looks like an LP jacket. Looks too much like the special edition Scambot sleeve though, hah! So I probably won't use this one. But I still really like it. I think I was going for something yacht rock-like too.

I think the logo font is reminiscent of Disco Volante, which funnily enough is referenced with "Sleepy Time". Maybe the side of the CD release can use this format, I still really like the font choices and color palette. I wasn't using Keneally for inspiration, it seems like my mind just went to that palette. Aggh! Why does the mind do that? Haha. Well I guess they are pleasing colors.

I think Evelloun might be the best song on the album. Spectator Mode might have some of my best guitar tones yet. If I do make a vinyl of this, maybe this could be the cover. That was a tangent, I was gonna say that if I do make a vinyl, it might omit some of the more obtuse songs. I kind of like that concept actually. The CD can be a bit bigger, and the LP are the essentials. No need to strip back the entire album, they can be distinct things. Might be a thing to try. Separate track lists as well, hmm...

Edit Aug 8:

Already had the feeling, but this is even more solidified. This series is complete. Or maybe the thing I am looking to explain, what the 'goal' of this series was meant to help with, and or was a catalyst to being able to find, has been reached.

The inner critic is no longer in power (the first album was the first example of that, where it specifically was like 'this is what an album would sound like with the reins off'). The second album allowed more vulnerability. It also didn't look for perfection. This album is seemingly the epitome of all of these things. It has vulnerability, flaws (not in a critical/negative sense, just observational), honesty, emotional availability, and it is uncompromising in what it is.

It's not that I don't want to continue this series, I think it's moreso that it's done it's job. It has allowed me to see that I can make these things, that there isn't negative fallout (those who enjoy it will say; those who don't usually don't say anything; those who do critique it, I don't concern myself with that input anymore, it is not conclusive to my internal state of being), and that yes, I don't internally define my own self-worth or emotional state of being by the success/failure (whatever that means) by this project.

So it's not that it's not fun, I think the thing that was scary before, isn't scary anymore, because I have done it now. That's a beautiful thing.

Not that I won't revisit this [style(s)] in the future, whether it be another flavor of my writing for example, but moreso that it isn't coming from the same place anymore, because that place has been refactored, and is stronger now.

And I am also not afraid of this kind of thing either, not that I am going back on having done it, far far far far far from it. It's merely that I am stating that probably any time having been doing it going forward from here, it is merely a tongue in cheek reference to this lovely period of growth in my life.

The track lists we're not intentional in a logical sense, it kind of just came together how it did. It's interesting to me how some of these titles actually lineup to this state of growth. "I Am No Longer Stranger" is very much a literal explanation of all of this.

This album was also more abstract than my 'progress'-based writing was pointing towards. The concept was to have more of a literal character-based reflection of the emotions and negative sentiments that come through one's mind. This song was definitely an interpretation of that, but it's coming from a 'safe' silly point of view, while I want to get to the point of exploring those emotions, feelings, sentiments, and views, as true to how they might be for real, rather than as a silly reference. I think it's because it is merely something very deep still, so it's going to be hard for me. That's okay. That's just a symptom of where I am at currently. So it still managed to come through to the album, that's more than positive. The viewpoints and negative beliefs still are noted in the song too, again, albeit a bit obscured.

There are parts in "Sleepy Time" which are about my journey as well. I will look into denoting a lot of this album with lyrical notes so you can read more about it. It's meant to be obtuse. I think because I am still a bit uncomfortable sharing some of this stuff, since it is very fresh. And I do feel a bit obtuse about the current 'conclusions' (not to say that they are conclusive). I think that's what I worry about. I don't want my *current* perceptions to be taken as objective truth or statements about my current relation and connections to things. I think it's for both, but maybe even moreso for you. Seeing just how ugly some of the internal parts of your mind are, seeing them for what they are, it makes them seem ridiculous. Maybe that's the journey towards that more honest take on things though, that I can see the thoughts for what they are, just those thoughts, than as being 'my thoughts'. I mean, I already realize that. But there still seems to be that connection, as I just mentioned. I think it's making progress. So again, progress is being made. Progress.

"Be Kind to Yourself" is one of the most honest and vulnerable songs I've ever made. I could write a whole write up and or record a video about it. A summary for the time being, woke up in the middle of the night, heavily emotional. It seemed like a real breakthrough. It wasn't by design. I had to record the thoughts and feelings in my head and heart at that moment. I made that song then and there. I was basically seemingly making peace with a bunch of the things internally, and I happened to be awake to catch it. I don't know if that makes any sense, I don't know how to describe it. It's like my emotional speedometer went all the way up, which it hasn't in a very long time.

"Duckling Returns" was just a reference to the track "Duckling Fartek" from Electro Capacitoritor. I think it has a deeper meaning, looking back ('Returns', I mean), to describe me having returned to allowing that open-hearted deep, young part of myself to take part again. Because it's safe. When I was thinking of 'Fartek', I think I was moreso thinking of "Masked Dinosaur", just those funky silly playful GarageBand songs I used to make because that's what was fun, intriguing, and boundary pushing at the time.

"Drymon" is a reference to having gotten reconnected with SpongeBob again, and how much I loved that show as a kid. I think his name stuck in my head after having watched some documentaries on YouTube, just seemed like a cool name.

"Sleepy Time" was just what I preemptively called that song, before having made it. Rather than being asleep in bed, I was up late making weird music on my computer. I think the idea of it being late, and just in that weird focused flow state, and not worrying about outcomes, that's meant to be represented there. That song has a lot of references. I will have to catalog them all. There's moments of SYL "Info Dump" sampled, Mr. Bungle "Mary Go Bye Bye", and a bunch of random and wild YouTube videos.

"Spectator Mode" seemingly was a nice carry-over from the Minecraft references, which also go back to the innocent little kid thing, funnily enough. It's more of a symptom that all of these things coalesced in this way, it was seemingly a more connective thing than an intentional one. Having reconnected with that young fun part of myself, those things are fun again, and they bring me back. And the idea of a live show, being a spectator versus a participant. That seemingly connects to me and how I felt my experience had been, to however that may be taken.

"Contemplative" also is merely just a literal title of the track itself, I feel like that ambient guitar soundscape stuff I do seems to be that kind of mood. It also connects to how I feel like I have related to the world in the past. Rather than having been a participant, I was a spectator, hence being contemplative, and having felt "alone", like was mentioned in the haze of chaos that is "I Am No Longer Stranger".

"I Am No Longer Stranger" is also seemingly the epitome of all of what this album is. Making for the sake of making, not judging it. Saying one's feelings, not judging it. The earnesty is to be cultivated, like I mentioned (not being jokey about serious stuff; making light of it).

"Be Kind to Yourself" seemingly was the title I came up with for that track, after having recorded it. The first title was "Ayahuasca", to represent how I felt people described the awakenings of those experiences. It was more of a way to describe my feeling though, rather than a literal psychedelic experience like that. It was that "coming home" kind of thing which I was trying to articulate. I chose "Be Kind to Yourself" because it felt more fitting like a mission statement, and the truth to the conclusion as to what the experience was lending me towards, rather than the experience itself. It's like the experience was a function, and the return value was 'be kind to yourself'.

"The Race Against Time" was me just describing how I was trying to finish the album, to the extent that I could. I took 5 days off for no-expectations music-exclusive creative time. If "something" came of it, yay. If "nothing", then I still took the effort to try putting myself forward, take focus on my needs, goals, wants, etc. And it was in the effort of trying a new method. That's honestly a bigger win than any music itself that I might gain from the time off anyways. And I still came out ahead in the end, in my opinion. I mean, I didn't intend to come away with this project. I knew it might, it might not. And it's still cooler and more groundbreaking (in all of the ways I've mentioned so far) than I could have done "logically" anyways. I love the character ideas, I still want to do it. But this one is even more unique, and this one is heartfelt too.

This album is uncomfortable. The key that I am attempting to describe though, is that it doesn't make me uncomfortable, anymore. I just see it as progress now. "Sleepy Time" is probably the worst song I've ever made. That wasn't on purpose. It's not conclusive. This album is merely a statement/sentiment of all of this stuff in my head and heart right now. And being able to archive and see that all laid out, it's great. And having spilled my heart out (is that the right expression? That sounds like a negative thing), I am still not worried about how this is perceived.

"Evelloun" was merely the 11th track I recorded, and I wanted to flip the pronunciation around, so I tried to write it the best I could annotate.

"Pasta in Montana" was originally tracked to the project name "Give a Chance on Me". I still like the place it came from. I ended up picking from a conversation at work where someone was taking pasta on a flight to Montana, because their family enjoyed the brand so much. I liked that. I think it was the same day I recorded the song, not totally sure. I could go back through my notes/pictures to find out. I think I likened the "pasta" name because it felt more honest in the sense that it was me, my intrigue, my experience. Coming from a place of interest and heart. The other one feels like it's speaking from a place of lack, begging, being stuck. Because this project is (intended?) coming from a place of truth and heart to my current experience, myself feeling like I am stuck didn't feel truthful to where I am now. I used to be stuck under that other stuff. Now I am not. I chose not to let that thing represent me. It had been my experience, and I am not omitting that. I just don't let it represent me anymore, internally. I am not asking something to let me be heard anymore. Internally, I was asking myself that.

This album is fragmented in the genres and styles because I hypothetically have been wanting to make a "normal" album for a bit now, learning song form, things like that. But omitting the truth for me has been very much a challenge. Having the silly me seemingly has been important to still have a the forefront.

Down to Evelloun even. It might be one of the "best"/"perfect" songs I've made, yet the playing gets unoriginal and sloppy. Maybe that's the odd dilemma too, it's hard for me to be genuine and it not get messy. Hence, why obscuring my messy hasn't been an option for me.

I think I also want to state that this album isn't after having been "living in" this mindset, it has been living by example. Living "as-if". I mean, I believe the positivity more than ever, and I do think I am more capable than I give myself credit for.

So I think this is merely representing both the end/start of these two phases, per se. Not that it's specifically transitional, this is merely mostly representative of being the end of the previous stage, I feel. But it's using verbage from the future phase. And it coming from a place of embodying that future stage as well. So it's not a pho-embodiment. It is indeed real and heartfelt. But the veil to protect the truth is still active, even with the new systems in place. That is the thing which is to be reconstructed. That's why this album is merely also awesome, because even if the songs themselves might not be clear of tongue-in-cheek yet, the statement of the album as a whole, and where it's coming from, those are real. And I mean, seeing how this album represents itself anyways, that is unrelenting, it points to things obviously, whether it literally states the place it's coming from.

It's like if you see a giraffe in a ghost costume. I mean, it might not say it's a giraffe, but you can tell. "I eat trees!!! hahahahah". I mean, it's not wrong, it's just not without a veil. And even then, you can tell it's starting to hangout with other giraffes, so it doesn't matter that it doesn't tell you it is one. Even if it doesn't say it's a giraffe, you can put together that it is one.

Okay, that was good. Talk later :)

Edit a minute later:

I also want to note that the end of the series is merely in the sense that it would no longer be coming from a place as perceiving it in the negative light of itself. Like, if anything, like I mentioned before maybe, it was allowing the work to be what it was, but in the frame that what it was was 'outrageous'. So any references to that going forward, would be explicitly tongue in cheek, because I don't see what I do as outrageous anymore, because it has proved time and time again to be of help to my growth. And again, I don't worry about what others think about it anymore.

I mean, like for the first Recreational Outrage, I was literally doing it as a "okay I am stepping out in the water, the deep end". It wasn't a faux paux in the intent of being boisterous, in of itself. I mean, if that's what it lent itself to being, then that wasn't my problem. I just wasn't letting that critical deciphering run the show anymore. It didn't feel embodied in the way it is now though. Like, I mean, a lot was "at stake" in terms of the unknown, if that makes sense. That's why sharing and fully publishing and CD printing was so keen. I was making a statement, and it was going to be a thing. It's like getting a tattoo. Everything internally was "telling me" it was stupid, outrageous, ridiculous, a waste of time, waste of energy, etc. Now it is merely the exploration of the open-ended part, without all of those voices being present. I mean, I took the wheel to make the album, but they were still shouting at me over my shoulder. Vulnerability wasn't on the table either. That one is a new paradigm, seemingly on it's own timeline. Now is currently the picking up of it. "Deep Dive" was a very hard one for me to do, and to keep on the record for "HARRY". And it was the only honest song, with vulnerability. But that was a huge fucking leap for me. Let alone to put it at the start of the album. Fuck yeah. I was going to put "Be Kind to Yourself" at the start, to do the same thing again. But then, again, I don't need to prove anything anymore. I am merely stating my experience. Doing my thing.

"The Race Against Time" seemingly is a return to Elkosaurus too, which was what I feel is the very start of that kind of state that this project came through in. That one came from a place of working towards that negative thing though (I am going to make the worst album possible), as at the time, that was what felt safer than making something that could be critiqued. This is obvious now. And it was a fantastic loophole.

This also goes back to why I didn't (and maybe don't) consider my work before Elkosaurus to be 'original', 'good', or things like that. It's like I couldn't let myself enjoy it. That is something I am now working on. That is very much the start of my work. I have been embracing that part of me silently, visibly (like the giraffe), I just haven't been able to claim things.

That's the beauty of Recreational Outrage (1). Because it is something I was able to let me take ownership of, it was the first album I was happy to share. Otherwise, I might belittle or take light out of anything I had made before that. And I did, and still view my early catalog that way.

"The Race Against Time" is nominally reflecting how now I have these awarenesses, understandings and viewpoints, and now I have to console how I will live my life, having "lost the first part of it" to this set of things which are struggles. The point is that I don't actually let this part take hold though. It's a concern, but I think I have felt that me merely getting to this point is also part of the journey, and that it's not like it is "lost time". I think this is merely the dilemma that I am presenting, in a literal sense. It's the dilemma, not the conclusion you decide to pick from the scenario itself. "Do I treat my time up until now as something like 'lost time', or 'things weren't right', or do I cram what I didn't have into the 'time I have left'?". I think my current stance as of having written this, is that this is also just a bunch of horseshit, and it's the same mechanism in the first place. They are both glass half empty. My actions (this album being one of them) have been acting like a giraffe. I have been showing myself that making and taking actions is more important than whether you believe in them.

So maybe that's the future. Not that I ignore the tendencies and or voices, I hear them out. I listen to what they might suggest. I learn to understand their perspectives. I don't have to only take their advices though. The most useful thing I think I can take from this is that you calculate what to do based on their outlooks, rather than listening to what they tell you to do.

Recreational Outrage 1 was literally following the thing of "don't do that", and it did that the whole way.

Now that I don't have the "don't do that" voice as present anymore, now I just act, based on the ideas I have. Namely, "Sleepy Time". It doesn't feel as bombastic as it might have in the past. And I think that says something. That's why this album seemingly happened in this way. My possibly weirdest most abstract song, and it doesn't even really bother me or make be critique it or bat and eye. It isn't at the boundary anymore. So it's not edgy like it was. Again, just different scenarios and mental frameworks. Not stating the past was bad, wrong, or things like that. It was just what was needed for the time.

I think the point is that even with the extent of that song, it proves to me and to the mission statement of the project [series] (without having known this was the mission, per se), is that it means I have grown that much. It's like my noise floor for criticism is 24-bit now, rather than 8-bit (audio reference).

Hypothetically, I will release music under my own name, rather than rBnaodn, once in am not under the guise of the cypher-based veil. Again, just a funny correlation. Maybe consequential. Back then, me being my own name wasn't "unique enough". The goal of honest expression, it wasn't the goal. It was merely out of comparison. I mean, it was "play-based fascination" as well, in that I thought cyphers were cool. But to the sentiment that I felt expressing my thoughts through music had to go through a cypher itself, that is merely the same mechanism itself that Elkosaurus operates under.

It is still a tricky thing though, in that I feel like straying away from that part would also be trying to obscure the path. That wouldn't be the goal. It would merely be in favor of honest expression coming from myself truthfully, rather than with a mask or a ghost costume on, as I've mentioned.

But I guess I also feel that maybe the integration part, it can coexist, and things can be messy in that way. That feels like it would be the 'best case scenario'. And internally, that feels fucking messy as fuck. But again, following the logic of "do the thing you don't want to do", it would only make sense for that to be the same one, I feel. Logistically, it would be simpler as well, as I don't want to have to worry about renaming my Bandcamp and stuff.

But again, I think trying to go around under different things without staying under the original thing, might be trying to elude something which I am merely trying to not elude in the first place. I want integration, not to elide the past.

Still work ahead, doing fucking great.

This album is like I am at the end of the series, in that I am nearly to closely reaching a number, but am not quite there. I am essentially on the line though, just not quite there. It's not like I am "there" with this album. It's hard to articulate. Recr 4 will only come from the place of having crossed the line, and is retroactively going back and embodying wha the past was, rather than being in that state itself. Just want to make that clear. The place that these albums are currently coming from is healing, so any further exploration is coming from a place of exploration, rather than first-hand things. Because the nature of this series is about coming from that place of being underneath everything, with those voices on top. But they are almost gone now, in terms of their direct influence to the mainframe. That's what I was trying to articulate with the finish line part.

So the cliffhanger of the final song title is about the statement of pointing towards where things are going.

This reminds me of the likes of the end of Progscapes, with "The Winds of Change", and what that represented for me.

Recreational Outrage was embodying the concept of "I am an artist, I make music". Now I am embodying it myself. I am an artist, I am a musician, I do make music. I am a guitar player. I am a guitar player. I do make mistakes. I did used to criticize my work, because of those old tendencies. Etc. I'm no longer acting as-if, from the idea of "what would I do if I was that kind of person?", because I couldn't let myself become any of those titles. Because qualifying myself as being any of those would have to imply that I am good at it, and that's not an option. Hence why Elkosaurus was a genius loophole. And it's why Recreational Outrage is even more fucking genius. It was taking that loophole, and fucking slamming a brick through it. Essentially, making the worst album possible, but standing behind it, rather than demeaning it and saying it was trying to be the worst album ever (Elkosaurus). And for this album, I am merely releasing it under the premise that it is just like any other day. Because to me, it is. I know it's not for other people, but that's the thing. Now that the shit has hit the fan, or at least, I am being vulnerable for people to be able to see this, now there's possibility for growth. In the sense that me standing behind future works, it is a no-brainer. It is not an as-if thing anymore.

Huge fucking progress. Listening to "Scopes" right now, I love this song. YouTube loudness normalization definitely makes it slightly more tolerable.

I also think I am so used to my "bullshit" (endearing) music, that I forgot just how "fucked" it really is. Hahahaha.

Okay, new premise. I just realized, I know I became aware of my internal critic beliefs. I might have said bullshit in the negative belief sense, back then. Then I became aware and started using positive terms instead. Then I got to be more okay with the play-based endearing usage I just did. I still preface it though, to make it clear. Now I can take the training wheels off. From now on, I am not going to specify it, because it no longer is going to come from the critic. And if it does, I will catch it, and replace it accordingly, with something constructive. But things that come from me in a negative light, that is now the play state, which has recently been under construction. It is safe to use now, yay!!!!!!!!!!!!!! :DDDDDDDDDDDD

Okay, love ya.

Go listen to some Devin Townsend or Strapping Young Lad, you lazy motherfucker!!!!!!!!!!!!!! 👹

To note: I also have loved Dev's humor (and seemingly east-coast humor) because of this brashness, because it was something I was uncomfortable with, because of that internal negative shame/critical sentiment, as I just mentioned. So seeing him use that negative speech, but in a clearly playful way, not as criticism disguised as play, that really has opened my eyes.

Brandon

Edit: Aug 11

Heya! Started working on the artwork for things the other day. Did most of the heavy lifting yesterday. Finished it today, this morning, as of 12:40 or so. It's not as tidy as I thought it might be, I think I used too much sharpie, and some of the colors are a bit meh. But, it's still really cool. So I'm going with it.

Much to the likes of the first album, I initially had help setting up the scene and shapes, with GPT. Then I extrapolated my own parts by using freehand. I colored parts in by what I wanted, rather than what GPT did. I think the long-term goal is to have that mind's eye for how shapes of things could be. That part is still fairly pedestrian for me.

I also was intending to do a title on this one, where it says "Recreational Outrage", then "VOLUME THREE" on a separate line. That didn't seem to find a place on this artwork, it didn't pop out like something natural. So at least for now, it is not on there. Maybe I will add a paper drawing on top, like artwork from the early vinyl days, where printed artwork was aligned then scanned to get that arrangement. It would be instead of me using photo editing to do it, intentionally.

I did do some color correction and hue balancing, it is much more clear as to what the picture consists of, with the extra saturation. It's a bit bleh and messy without it, I feel.

I took the picture with RAW, and I realized after that that means optical image stabilization was turned off, I think that's why it's so much blurrier.

Might do a retake of this, might not. Time will tell. I am open to it though. It is not set in stone like it used to be. I mean, if it feels like this is "it", then I am fine with that. But I just don't feel that way. And I am following that instinct more now, than merely just "all and anything goes". Again, that was by design, with the first album.

I can explain the artwork later on, both with what I understand of it currently, and that it probably means more than I realize currently. The idea was fully mine. It was just arranged by GPT, then I compiled it and did the actual drawing of it, with colors and such.

Edit: Hello from Aug 13!

Retook the album art image, with my old phone. I figured out that my new phone also has a different aperture, so that was also partially why it was blurry, let alone using RAW and not having image stabilization. So that's another interesting trade-off plus with the older cameras. I still love older tech, not because it's older, but because of the trade-offs it allows for. This new image is less in terms of pixels, yet it allows me to take the picture closer to the paper, so it doesn't need to be cropped anyways. 3024x3024 is just right. Just take the picture with square mode, then crop to 3000x3000, and make edits from there. Yes I know I can scan it instead, I intentionally have been going for the 'low-budget' concept with this series. It has intentionally been going by the design of the homemade thing.

I recently made another new headphone EQ, with the pink noise method. So, yet again, now this album is an example of the mix not being reference-quality. I am okay with that. All of my projects have been off in that respect. It just takes time, and I am getting closer. That's why the harshness of the high-end is weird on the opening track for example, my headphones were EQed more tame, hence I missed taming that high end annoyance. And the bass on this album is a bit odd, yet not boomy at least. Compression for this album was also way too hot, in retrospect. But again, kind of representative of what I thought I had just learned. So, all good.

Didn't know that the first album was released on the day of Bikini Atoll, which is inherently tied to Spongebob, Ween, Steven Hillenburg, and Ween. I am going to start listening to Ween. The Mollusk specifically.

Man, I love the honesty on this album.

I had kind of an internal breakdown the other night, now I am better. I am going to move things forward within the next 6 months, as environments permit. Very much excited about my life timeline now. I am now in the next phase. I see where to go, rather than merely only "where I am at". I have let alone deciphered where I am at, but also came to peace with it, and now actively have been moving the ball forwards towards where the map points next. That was what was interesting. Much of the last 5 years or so, I'd say, have been cultivating to this point. I am so happy with this progress. It's not like it's an unexpected "a-ha!" moment, but moreso that the cumulative progress has allowed actionable actions to be made, and it has just naturally progressed. No more shame, no more judgement, no more negative beliefs. Now I just utilize the things I do know how to do, and I have started learning about what frameworks to build next. Again, learning is still in the picture. I merely have "finished learning" about the past, and now I am moving forwards. Not that I am leaving it behind, I feel it has been intergrated.

I had a good way to describe it last night, that much of our personalities and growth are like a git repo. When something positive or negative happens in our life, we might move to a new branch, and the one we were on before doesn't get patch updates until we return to it again. That has been how I feel. And it explains why I can't merely just move forwards (merging those branches) without having done the git merge. It also explains how working on all of the branches little by little, over time, it allows them to converge once again, hence what I feel like I am at now. And not that I need to find out, or that I am able to discern or not, I possibly might not even be back on the main branch again. I might be two or three branches removed, still on patches basically. But still, I have git merged a bunch of stuff, and I am moving back to the main branch. Slowly but surely.

And notably, Normal Bryan does not appear on the back or inside of the case anywhere. Seemingly only the cover, in retrospect. I feel like I don't trust him enough yet, and or I don't know him fully. I have a feeling that he just has a sentiment of wanting to belong, rather than be fully himself. And the rule of the rest of the group has been that being oneself is more important than belonging. So maybe that's why he has never been able to be seen very often.

Carpincho having the broccoli top is the attempt at being Normal Bryan I think. But Normal Bryan is different than that, and I don't think Normal Bryan is known yet. Maybe he doesn't have a face.

tracksInfo.title: Sleepy Time
tracksInfo.about:
Edit Sept 19: Just had this hunch with the research I've been doing about copyright and sampling. Feeling a bit nervous about the stuff I've been making with samples in it. Been being honestly a bit irresponsibly in that regard, not really worrying about what things I use. Thinking about proactively taking things down just in case. Just not worth it. I 100% want the longevity of my music, but losing things to copyright is absolutely not worth it. Note that if things/tracks change, it was because I felt it was a call to make. Take that as you will.

Edit same session, 1:19 AM. Ended up deciding to take down Recr 1 from streaming, I really don't want to flirt with my samples of "Chicken Jockey". The risk is not worth it. Yes it is a bummer, as I wanted the album to be up forever, that was kind of the whole point. But the adult logic part really made the point that being safe is more important with this kind of thing. Going to archive the notes for all of my Bandcamp, and probably will remove the songs that use copyright stuff anyways, even if the odds are low for something to happen. It's the principle, and the possible ramifications that I don't want to flirt with. It's the responsible thing to do.

From YouTube: Aug 7

Okay, so Recreational Outrage 3 has been the focus for the past week or so. This is seemingly the most outrageous of all the creations so far. Lots of inspirations with this one.

The artwork isn't from this project, but I feel like I very well might just combine all of these. Time will tell.

This is not necessarily usually my genre. This is avant-garde, musique concrete, I think? There are moments of Devin Townsend, Strapping Young Lad, Mr. Bungle, Keneally, Marco Minnemann/Mario Brinkmann Normalizer, Maggot Tw*t, things like that. Incubus had done something like this on their Science album too, come to think of it. And actually, that would make sense to be the Bungle influence there.

I used a bunch of samples from different things. This was essentially just a DAW project I just made right now, in the middle of the night. The goal per se, has been to really be okay with the things I make. Just read that on a Devin interview from the 90s or so. It's astounding how much I feel like I relate to him creatively.

Curious what you think of this one. I literally haven't even broke down what it "is". I just felt like this is just so far out there, probably the weirdest and darkest song I've ever made.

Just try it, turn off your brain, and put in a bunch of different things into the project, and follow your gut.

I think I wrote notes for the artwork, I can cover that if you are curious. Lots of references there too, I think that's why it ties in so closely to the aesthetic of this song, more than one might think. I know that probably sounds ridiculous, but I'd be happy to explain it.

No AI, or drugs were used in the making of this. Merely just some samples, myself, and Logic Pro. Thanks a lot to SketchCassette II, TDR Nova (really big thanks, this doesn't sound horrendous because of that), and many other great plugins.

Some of these samples are from random YouTube videos as well. They add to the seemingly abstract and nonsensical story of this.

Paranormal, meets conspiracy theory, meets abstract world perspectives, meets existential dread, meets prog I guess.

This will probably be on Bandcamp soon, and probably CD. Haha.

----

Okay, back to Bandcamp notes:

Just had an aha moment when listening to this track this morning (hello from sept 10 '26), in that unrelated to the name, it really does feel like a dream, in what it's sonic makeup is. I really like that it aptly was named Sleepy Time instinctively. These things weren't on purpose. It does very much seemingly fit the notion of the album a lot, and I fucking love it. It feels like the "keeping things smooth" on the beginning of the album seemingly contrasted with what is going on deep in the psyche, which shows up in the dreams. Coming back 'online' after awaking from the experience, for the rest of the album, you can experience the part of learning how to handle what happened exactly, and how to metabolize it. There's so much deep stuff that it's almost too much to handle, so you can't really 'understand' it. I mean, you can try, but it will run you mad. I think the thing is to merely just trust the way you feel about it, and help that lead your decisions, rather than finding how to be able to handle the understand or experiences themselves. It's what you choose to handle them with after the fact that matters in the long term. I mean, in terms of how life works. Cause and effect is all that matters here. The only thing that remains of you for certain are the implications you affect onto the world, and the butterfly effect that comes from that. People who are no longer here are still heavily influencing us to this day, merely out of habit, structure, and the difficulty of making things change. This is the case for everybody.

And this also seemingly is very interesting in that Track 9 was actually kind of a dream state itself. I mean, I made it when I was awake, but something about my deep existential experience made me wake up, and need to make that song, and all of the emotions and sentiments there were what was going on. So this, again instinctively, not intentionally, because I am just seeing this now, relates very fucking well back to Sleepy Time, in terms of the sequencing. The tracks were written in a bit of a different order, so it didn't pan out exactly like the album sounds. Now I think I am getting a hang of this kind of natural sequencing experience.

Spectator Mode is kind of just being present, and being in the moment. Contemplative is going deep and connecting things again, and in a meditative state. So it also seemingly makes a lot of sense how track 9 comes after, because a lot of times I have meditative relaxing days, I have a lot of big inclinations and things I figured out. Again, none of this is planned. I don't think I even necessarily knew I have been meditating per se. When I listen to ASMR/Reiki videos, I think I am meditating kind of. Sometimes I am drawing, writing, or merely just falling asleep. Having those kinds of videos playing with the screen off when I fall asleep, I sleep so so so great. Heavily recommend. And just a random thing, put your main phone/alarm on the floor under something fabric, like a jacket, it keeps me from getting anxious to wake up, because I don't get jump scared by needing to go turn it off. It still makes me get up to go turn it off, hence helping me wake up, but I am still relaxed. Much better mornings.

Track 10 seemingly is a bit undecided in this pattern. Right now, I would say that it is the response of having come to peace with parts of yourself, and it exemplifies a full circle experience. Not the end of something, but the beginning of something new. I mean, it is the end of an era, but the era is never intended to be left behind, it is cumulative going forwards. So everything in eras experienced will be carried forwards into the new one, being featured as well as embraced and still learned from, but they are accepted as not having to be the only avenue.

I mean, it is rooted in the semi-anxiety that it felt like 'time is running out', in terms of life. Like, the sense of "what am I waiting for? I need to get things moving! Just because people tell me I am young, that doesn't mean to just wait around forever! I have been doing that since I was actually young!".

Post album release, things aren't going as they seemingly were planning to go (in my own life), so while this is a new era, it is looking different than where things were seemingly wanting to go, or could go. I am still pushing the ball forwards, and I have compassion for myself in that it will happen how it happens. The sense of 'the race against time' is settling. Not that I am content with waiting again, but I am not going to rush things if they just aren't meant to be. It's odd, because this ambiguity isn't something I would really ever be okay with. I think it's because it's more of a feeling than a top-down decision. It's a new way of handling things, and a new way of looking at things.

"The Race Against Time" was named because I was literally down to the last few hours of vacation, and I wanted one more track, so I just made that as fast as possible, and it ended up sounding like Elkosaurus, but mixed nicely.

Man, I really am starting to love this album now, looking back after merely just like a month or so. How has it already been a month??? I am glad that this stage of the series has been reached as well. And it's a big fucking statement. Fucking awesome.

I think I also have an interesting feeling that this is a fairly dark album, actually. The first album seemingly was pretty bright. The second album was kind of a sense of being lost, and or cynicism, and the third album is whatever adjectives one might describe for what I've outlined so far. I am still a bit inconclusive to have the words for it. Time will solidify that. I have a few words in mind right now, but I don't feel grounded in the conclusion of them, so I will wait.

Oh yeah, and track 10 seemingly helps bring the brightness back, since leaving it on a heavy note seemingly felt too big. This wasn't meant to represent a downer sentiment, this is a positive thing here. There were just some very deep deep road bumps (dips?), to which the struggles and things to have worked through and overcome have been very fucking awesome, and strong to be able to do. So it's like returning home after having done a huge obstacle course. Track 10 is kind of like a play-fun "fuck you", like after the sincerity of track 9, having just fucking stupid play-fun nonsense just makes me laugh legitimately. Not in only the ridiculousness, but in the pure enjoyment sense. Like, after all of that fucking bull-crap, you can fucking stand up and fuck around. Fucking sick as fuck. I'm laughing!!!

Oh, forgot another thing I was gonna mention. It was the darkness of the album. Some of the songs were made at night, and not literally that it was dark out, while you could say that, but I think the kinds of things I write and or the sentiments and or emotions that tend to come up might gravitate towards these deep darkness things, hence why the album ended up being like that.

When I designed the CD artwork for this album, much like other albums, I listen to it while I made it, to get the vibe to come across. Thinking after the fact, again it was all instinctual in the moment, the darkness very much is present in the outside of the case, with the back artwork. Deep space, introspective penguins (my favorite animals as a little kid, seemingly interesting how it wanted to say that they really like track 9, I think there's a deep correlation there), and the inside of the project shows the brightness of things like track 4, 9, and 10. I feel like the robot is speaking in Sleepy Time, in retrospect. Trying to figure out how that relates to the story. The robot is definitely protecting, so maybe that is the thing. Sleepy Time is definitely inspirative to the chaos on the back cover. Track 3 seemingly comes across with The Angry Cow (on the cover; capitalized because this would be a cool song name). I think the angry cow kind of connects back to "Not Gonna Look..." from "More Alone at Home". I feel like that song has a representation of being part of this album, even if it's not on the CD or the running list. It seemingly is a combination of the angry cow, but also Elkosaurus. Elkosaurus is track 10 here for sure. I thought the Duckling is Elkosaurus, but maybe not. Will look into this. Duckling might be a distinct character. Carpincho might be track 2, 6, and 9, to some extent. Carpincho with the broccoli top haircut is specifically Carpincho embracing themselves and their interests.

The card on the back tells me that the cards that you have are not necessarily the ones that will work. It's up to you to find a new card for the path forwards.

The "FUCK" on the back was just a seemingly random thing, just stupid 'fuck' humor, which is always welcome. But it also seems to be a representation of that looming feeling in the distance that's always there, even when you are at deep peace, namely with Contemplative. Like yes, it is unwavering relaxation and introspection, and you are at peace with the looming presence of "FUCK", but that doesn't mean it isn't there. And part of the journey has been learning that that presence is okay. It's going to be there. It's fine. It could be mortality, time, entropy, aging, things like that. Yeah, angry cow definitely is the line "fuck you and your fucking bullshit" from "Not Gonna Look...". That song felt like a precursor to what this project was though, hence why I didn't have the inclination to include it here. It is part of the module graph, but not part of the program.

I designed the artwork on the back as square on accident, I just spent hours making it so I was going to creatively make it work, even if it looked like shit. Dealing with the speed-dips is all part of the process. I just went with the thing that the dark part is also the spine from the front. That's what I decided. Is it a waste of graphical space? yes. was I lazy? Maybe. Does it matter? No. Am I fine with it? Yes. And that's the growth here. So fuck you and your fucking bullshit!

Oh, I forgot the other part. The front is how the album is trying to be "normal" like everyone else. In retrospect, this is me probably being partly Autistic. I took the test online (again, grain of salt here), and I got a 39 out of 59. Notable is 26 or higher. So, uhh, yeah! And if anything, if this ends up panning out, man I will be more pleased than anything else! I fucking love myself even more for having been 'cope'-ing this whole way, thinking I was the same. Or rather, more truthfully, trying to act and convince myself and others that I was the same.

All I want is peace, please!!!! Internally. World peace is optimistic too, but so cheesy. I mean, I just learned how naive I am and have been, the other day. The definition of the word literally describes me it's FUCKING HILARIOUS!!!!! It gave me reason to understand more of myself from that lens. I am heavily optimistic, yet also driven by logical fact and realism. So the two go together hand and hand for me, always have been. My ideas start out optimistic, I follow them until the aren't able to sustain the real world, then I start building the sustainable versions based on the real-world data that I learn. I am not cynical because that doesn't help. There's plenty of that around me, and logically speaking, I can visibly see how being that way doesn't help with things. You just learned how to be content with status quo. No growth, no chance for new things. Not necessarily peace either, internally I mean. Just existing. So I think that's why the duality of things like this album are so important for me, because the experience of going between all of these facets is the message itself, not a specific one. There's the cynical angry cow, there's the happy go lucky Elkosaurus, there's distraught Carpincho, and there's optimistic Bryan (I don't have a name yet, that just came to mind). Maybe I will make that a new character going forwards. Okay, I think that's it!!! Okay, so the "trying to not be Autistic" straightforward experience character, is Bryan. Maybe a different name will come up. I don't know. He is a cross of Minecraft Steve, but also "normal Spongebob". Moreso "normal Spongebob" than anything else. So when I make my first fully straightforward album, that is essentially me "masking", and trying to inhabit the "normal Spongebob" Bryan character. I think it's been hard to inhabit that character because it is more of an idea, rather than my own self. And I seemingly get irked by trying to mask in music/my creativity itself. Hello hello, back to needing to do everything different, namely artistically, and whatever aspects of my life have been specifically contrarian. So the part of me attempting to embody being "normal" is the other facet. It's hard for me to try to be "normal".

And maybe this is where things will go. My experience of trying to fit in socially, and or emotionally, with relationships, humor, you name it. Maybe my Bryan album can be about me possibly being Autistic, and not knowing. It can be lyrical, truthful, and just "normal", consequentially enough. Song form, chord changes, lyrics, yeah. Without trying to inhabit a character, I've wanted to make an album that's straightforward for a very long time now. None of my characters were top down, I was exploring them, as they were already there.

I think my fear has/had been rooted in the sentiment that exploring one character means leaving the others behind, and that felt wrong and or dangerous to me. Maybe it's only if the character is understood to expect that though. "normal Bryan" (okay, official name) seemingly has the sentiment that he has to take over, and be in place of all of the other characters. So maybe that's why I haven't wanted to inhabit him.

I don't remember if I actually wrote down what I wanted to write ages ago, the album cover is 'normal Bryan'-influenced. The funk stuff, that's Normal Bryan.

title: Pasta in Montana
about: Been reconnecting with my music from about 3 years ago. Really been liking and listening to "Catastrophic Failure as a Human Being", as that time period is what I feel like I have come past, now I am in a 'new era'. I think part of me feels at home at that time period still, too. This song was recorded all today, this afternoon, impromptu, merely recording track onto track, and mixing it after a dinner break. It goes back to a lot of the things I used to do in my songs from back then. This however was all recorded with Logic Pro, and with the electronic drums, rather than GarageBand drums (previously tapped out with my fingers). This is 'real drums' to the extent that I am actually playing. Whether it is creative drumming, that is what I have yet to improve on. I worked hard this time to make sure the mix was okay, as that seems to have been the struggle with the older songs, hence going back and listening to them. I think the ear for this kind of stuff was certainly there, merely just not knowing engineering, mixing, nor mastering, those sorts of things couldn't allow the ideas to flourish like they thankfully can now. I also made sure to adjust my amp settings according to how they sounded in the room, rather than as a reference to how they sound in my (opinionated) MDR-7506s. I recorded the drums as multitracks, that made it easier to EQ, compress accordingly (this track ended up using less edits than I had thought, and they actually made it sound less ideal). So the technique this time was merely to use ''better sources', and to mix with a clean reference. Gain staging for input levels, and mix levels, that's the magic. Mix with an 'opinionated' reference, where all of the other music you like sounds 'right', whatever that means to you. The bass guitar is merely a duplicate preset of the bass amp sim I used from the GarageBand days (copied from a GB project itself), but again, all done in Logic Pro. So it functionally probably sounds the same, but Logic tends to be different at times, so take that as you will. This is Drop D down a half step, the tuning I associate with 2023 seemingly enough, love how this feels to play on my Ibanez, and my bass. So yeah. Whether good or bad, at least in terms of 'objectiveness', whatever that actually is, I like the sound of my amp, and I think it fits in the mix really well, especially when mixed well like here. Especially with double-tracking. It sounds so full. But again, I am biased to the gear I have used since I have started playing. And I associate my Ibanez with the sound of this amp, so yeah. All of the weird intricacies it has, I have come to love them. And I think since maybe like 2022, or yeah 2023, I seemingly have associated it with my "younger self", and or just the sound of my work when I have started out. So it's like the sound of my debut aesthetic if that makes sense. And I actually love the break-up of the chuggy-ness. Maybe it's cheezy, and doesn't sound like real tube-amp break up, I could probably agree. I think I merely just haven't gotten gear which sounds like that yet, so I haven't been biased towards how that sounds yet. It's like my playing style lends itself to that of how this amp works. Whether that's a good or thing or a bad thing, lol. I'd say it's good :)

title: BARKING AT BABIES
about:
Heya! Hello from Aug 14 very early morning. I love this project. It is much more raw and unedited than I initially intended, but coming back to it later, it seems like this aesthetic is what it needed to be, for whatever reason. Not plainly that I am lazy and didn't want to worry about mixing this stuff, since it was recorded a month or two ago, it was not just that. It was also that I feel like I want to re-learn what unmixed stuff sounds like, with these headphones. So I did tweak the demo mixes slightly, but not much.

A note from when I seemingly finished this lineup of songs, on Jul 6, the same night I made the artwork:
This is meant to be a loving reference to "Strapping Young Lad". I am making an album which emphasizes certain emotions driven by an aesthetic similar to that band, so I felt like a tongue in cheek mention to Devin and SYL would be cool. I was just trying to think of things to go on the cover, and maybe it was just my subconscious being too on the nose, but the background is nearly a 'blatant' quote of "Heavy as a Really Heavy Thing", the font is what the band used for their name from the third album onwards, including future remasters of old albums, the alien is kind of an emotional nod to that of the albums from that band, and what the message the music Devin wrote during that time was meant to communicate (me empathizing with that), and also merely just being a nod to the album 'Alien', and the alien is colored like the face on the HAARHT cover art. The cheeseburger was just a random idea, but also very much obviously lines up with the storyline to that of DTP's album Deconstruction. So it ties together as well. I seemingly am in my equivalent phase to what I gather Devin might have been in during Deconstruction, so I think having the two states of progression present at once is also representative of my process and journey of where I am at in the moment.

That was merely about the artwork, but also where the writing for this album is coming from, I think. If I recall, this is when I just bought No Sleep Till Bedtime, hence why I was in a Strapping mood again. I think it also was merely because emotionally that was what I was looking for during this time period, too. It was because of the growth and realizations of the time. I had that recently the other day too.

Another note from Jul 6:
"Barking at Babies" is also a very intriguing title to me. It was from a meme I saw a few years ago, where a random video of a guy making scary faces and barking, was placed next to the video of a baby starting to break out into a cry because of something scary. While it was satire, the nature of the concept itself, if it were to happen in real life, was fascinating to me. Say like someone were so far removed from themselves, and moreso inconsiderate of others, that they would go up to parents say in a store, and bark at their baby in the stroller. It would probably scar the baby for a long time. Very sad. I don't like the feeling of that. I think that sentiment of the feeling of recognizing that, the sense of sadness, disgust, and just distrust of anyone that would do that, the music is kind of inherently tied to that as well. Like the complete negativity of going up to someone else's baby, not even your own, and them being scarred for life, devastating.

This album is from the time period when I decide to try funneling my writing into aesthetic-based folders, where if I felt like a mood, I would write into that folder. I had never done it in that way before. It was before, it felt like because it was all coming from the same place (me..?), it all had to be represented. And previously, I would still write all into one folder, then attempt to separate it out later. That is just a mess, and it makes me feel like I am tearing it apart for no reason.

I do like this new setup. It does make things more difficult in a way, because I don't necessarily want to change concepts or ideas through a song, because the folder is a certain aesthetic. But again, that's kind of a good tool, in retrospect. I think this will ultimately be something I use for when I do the "exploring emotions" and "klishtas" album, I've been talking about. So after coming back to these songs, I very much like how they all have the same sound. But that to me, has been not what I've wanted. But it allowed for a bunch of other things, hence the other sides to these sessions, which I will come back to next. I merely finished this one for publishing first, because it was nearest to being complete. This one doesn't need to be "perfect", in terms of mixes and things, because it is kind of just a very raw feel. I even chopped the tails off of the songs on this one. Just very very quick rapid pace, at least when I came to finish things for this, tonight. Didn't even do EQ or compression on the master bus, just a limiter. That's also part of the experiment I think.

This was also the first time I "properly" worked on an Atmos mix! That is present in the final song, Swimming Upstream. Portajohn for Recreational Outrage 1 was actually mixed in Atmos too, but intentionally downmixed for just plain weirdness, so I won't count that in the same regard.

I think this album initially started as merely just exploring deep negatives and heinous emotions/feelings, in the extent of how they feel I mean, and seeing them out. I ended up doing that same kind of thing on Recreational Outrage: Volume Three, with Sleepy Time. That's why I used this album art for the YouTube video of that song. In theory, that track could have worked on this album too. I made it during the sessions of, and wanted it to appear on Recr 3, though, so it's more to the likes of how this album was featured in that project. I think that series possibly could be like my take on Devin's Empath project, where everything is shown in one place. No worry about critique or things like that. I love Empath so much. So, so, so much.

This project was very unplanned, impromptu-based, and specific in to how it came about. These songs were all made after having feeling like I was in a negative mood. It's not that I sat down and thought (this time at least) "I'm going to make a negative, loud, angry, sad song". No, it was more like the outlet to those feelings, and all of those instances came together in a folder. I then found all of these meanings about it to which I wrote to you here, rather than it having been perceived beforehand.

I think getting to be comfortable with making uncomfortable music/material/lyrics is also part of the goal for this. It kind of lines up with when I used to make those "very outrageous" song titles, a few years back, namely "Trailerpark Lingerie". The ones in this project are definitely a bit angrier, and tied to things like that. They are open to being more abstract, as before I seemingly had to only allow myself to use it if it was silly, or obtuse. I think it had to do with the emotion thing.

I ended up making all of the tracks and album title into all caps, to expand the uncomfortability and blatantness of this project. It wasn't like that or intended to be that way from the beginning. But after having looked at the artwork casing, it does need to be that way. I think seeing them all caps makes it more tied to anger, than to scary unknown edgy-ness. Say like the scary sense you get from the lowercase letters on stuff like Porcupine Tree. That is seemingly more scary than seeing blatantly obtuse uppercase lyrics. Maybe once I go full bore into full scary mode, the reclusive nature of lowercase letters can be present. I feel like this would represent someone yelling, rather than hurting. I feel like people being bad, without emotions, is more scary than people being bad, with emotions. So that's the sense I am going for here. It's not the sketchy emotionless characters, it's the emotion-filled ones. That's the vibe of this project.

This also explains why this project is so short, because between the folders I was making, this would combine to make the length of a full album, if it were all one. So the next time I try this writing method, I will write longer. I think it was a month or two in total for these folder pairs. But yeah, so they were being made at the same time, merely just written into based on the mood I was in. That seemingly works well in tandem with me learning about what mood I was in as well, rather than it being driving the same dial, hence like what I mentioned later on in "Sleepy Time", in retrospect.

And so much of my music, is seemingly stuff that could be trimmed, omitted, and sequenced better possible. I mean, I don't need to release all of this stuff. I mean, it could make a big more expansive project. But so much of it has meaning, and stories to be told, and I have found that to be more important than necessarily making "perfect projects", at this point. Sometimes I have the intent of making nice and clean top-down things, that just isn't always the goal. I started trying to do more of that in the counterpart to this project "The Melancholy Divine" (the 2026 folder. not the 2025 one), and then later on Recr 3. The thing is that my "top-down, perfect" writing seemingly all sounds the same still, to me at least. The same song structures. Same guitar techniques. But hey, that's still getting somewhere. I plan to start listening to mainstream music, just so I can write songs like that too. Not because I want to be mainstream, but because it's another aesthetic to have. Another brush to paint with. I am really happy Recr 3 has moments of that. I love that it's paired with things like "Sleepy Time" too, such a big contrast. I love contrast, as you can probably tell. I can't wait to do a bunch more contrast.

6/24 was when I had the late night emotional breakdown which was documented in the song "Be Kind to Yourself", which ended up being on Recr 3. I seemingly felt like I knew what the concept of Recr 3 was going to be after having had that experience. I made the folder for Be Kind and Recr 3, and later ended up merging 1 into 2. I didn't necessarily start Recr 3 in practice until August 1, a night or two before the time off, if I remember right. Then I made the rest of the songs during the time off. I added Pasta in Montana into the album too, since that was during the timeline of Recr 3. I don't know if it necessarily counts, in retrospect, but I feel like it worked with the track list, and it filled out the start of the album. So, yeah. There were additionally some demos I made with the strat, which I published to YouTube, but didn't feel like I connected with them being on the album. I was debating adding the 'minebeat' song, which I also made available to YouTube too, but I didn't feel like remixing it for the album. It was before I did the new headphone EQ, which is now the additional old headphone EQ. It's all a 'mess'. I could have just included it as is, at this point. But, it's fine. I kind of want to publish PPAP to Bandcamp too, but I don't want to post covers without proper checking of things. I did TV World, but that's an obscure song, and not a very good cover either, so I wouldn't think that one is bad. PPAP is kind of a big song though, so I wouldn't want a takedown for that. One could say I should move this info over to the Recr 3 album info, but it's fine. Meh. No biggie. I'd rather have written this down at all, than worry if it's all in the right place. All of these are tied together in ways anyways, so explaining that is going to be messy regardless.

Edit Aug 22:

WOW! Was going through some of my old meme captures from 2021, and I found the video! I found the original YouTube post too. It was from a JimmyHere video, when I saw it.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tvPetofAfNo

tracksInfo.title: INTO THE NIGHT
tracksInfo.about:
Notes about this track, from when I made the artwork on Jul 6:

I think the name is also meant to explain the depth to the presence of the record. Like, it's an overwhelming darkness in the record, where things are explored that are not comfortable. Like the opening track on the album, "Into the Night", on each side of the stereo, a couple is arguing on the left, and you hear org*sm noises on the other. It is meant to represent the uncomfortability and trade-offs that come with intimacy and partners. You get to "have a hookup friend", but you also have to battle out your inner child, from both sides. Not that it's a black and white "which do you pick?" situation, but it just begs the question, "are you ready for a relationship just because you want to f*ck, or are you ready because you've started your shadow work?"

To me, having those noises seems very ugly, in the sense that it is negative in a sense, but intentional, in that it kind of omits the positives of relationships. But to be fair, I think these are depictions of the klishtas that might be in my mind, where I might not have been first hand to experience the mutual love and care for one another, outside of merely doing things transactionally.

I like this. I will have to make a religion out of this. <bill wurtz reference>

tracksInfo.title: CLAUSTROPHOBIC TIME
tracksInfo.about: This is seemingly about the feeling of being stuck not being able to express your emotions. You are surrounded on all sides, and you have no way out. Other people project onto you, and they ask you to help them with their feelings. You don't get help, and people don't help you.

tracksInfo.title: SWIMMING UPSTREAM (Binaural)
tracksInfo.about:
This could technically tie back into the concepts that were featured on the earlier part of the album, but that is by coincidence. I mean, it is a funny twist around, and I will allow it if it is perceived that way. But the original meaning for the title of this one is seemingly about how one has to overcome the things you are behind on, because of what you didn't get to experienced earlier on.

But, you could also say it's about sperm too, so, yeah. The blatantness of that would fit with the aesthetic of this album, so feel free to decide which one you jive with more. *It's a choose your own adventure! 💅*

title: Left Alone
about:
Made this today, recorded it with my phone, GarageBand, Scarlett, and the new guitar. Mixed it both in headphones, and with speakers, for a cross-reference. Did the mastering in Logic Pro.

Listened to a bunch of music today. Realized that doing or not doing that has both helped and not helped my writing and recording process. Glacier 1985 EP, Quartz Against All Odds, Victim Power Hungry, Marco Minnemann Evil Smiles of Beauty/Sound of Crime, Steve Wilson The Raven That Refused to Sing (The Holy Drinker onwards), Devin Townsend Empath, and started the first two tracks of Groove Collective self titled.

I think having inspiration in your head, rather than ambient music from being out and about, it really does make a difference. I think "Sixdy Seven" was an example of a song where I am doing it more out of habit than by ear. That's kind of why I sat down and listened to so much music today. Being intentional with music is just as important, and having one on one with albums and songs, it really does help a lot with your ear. I used to have more time to do that in the past, in the sense that things naturally provided opportunities to listen to music, like homework or my commute. I am now going to start incorporating intentional music listening into my days, aside from the passive listening I have always had and been doing, regardless of any schedule. I am always listening to music, but a lot of times recently it has been interspersed with being distracted, or not getting to hear albums in full anymore, as I used to do that a lot. Half an album on one half of the commute, another half on the way back, for example.

It's not for the sake of it either, mind you. I miss having intentional listening like that. It just has to be set aside now, rather than being something I already can put into time blocks which necessitate being able to listen to music.

Another thing is that let alone that I don't actually have any less time than I did before, it's just distributed differently. It's not that I need to find access to those ambient activities anymore, say like needing to go drive to listen to an album. I can just set aside time to be present, at home. That seemingly felt uncomfortable before, for whatever reason. It's like the experience of listening to music wasn't something I could constitute as being "productive". That's more a reflection of my discernment being a bit broken, than anything else. If anything, I'd absolutely say that listening to an album is more important to me than watching videos for example. But in the past, I might have reduced them down to the same thing as being "not productive". This was not something I was doing consciously, merely just something running in the background. Relaxing, recovery, reflection, and creativity, these are proper facets to my day now, like food, water, sleep, outdoor time :)

Also wanted to mention how much I just really love those albums, they are attached with great memories from when I found them as well, and getting to know them has been so great. It's one thing to know which albums you like, it's another thing to reconnect with why you love them so much. I think it connects back to that part of having access to connect with the album, ie sitting down and listening without distractions. Hearing it in the same ways you used to hear it, ie not open, it tends to not reconnect with you. Maybe it's after having taken a break from them for some time, or just having also listened to new music since those albums were discovered for me.

title: Sixdy Seven
about:
Ohkay, yah baybey!

This is a crossover of 60s rock, and 2020s meme culture. Hence, 67, and '67. And just my normal lazy mispellings, this is what gave birth to whatever this thing is, which I call music. Beholden to your ears. I did some scatting this time too.

The Fender Strat is rocking it!

Edit: And yes I know that Victrola dates the time period I am referencing, it's another tongue in cheek inside joke with myself to where I reference things by how I associate them, rather than how they actually are. That probably makes no sense. I am picking from specific time periods, consciously kind of (what?). I am playing into the perceived funny of being a Gen Z who doesn't know anything about old-timey music, yet it's the opposite. I am getting more caught up on modern music nowadays, reverse from other people.

But again, to preface, I still have no fucking clue what I am doing. I just enjoy what I am doing. So I am a nobody to anybody. At least not until I am to somebody.

But yeah. Happy with this one. Still not sure what kind of vibe I am getting from the new setup yet.

Oh yeah and this song is mixed in mono, just to make things more aesthetically accurate. This lines up with the work I've been doing in Atmos, it's the complete opposite end to that spectrum. It's funny to me that people would assume albums written for mono would inherently work for something like Atmos. Just the contrast I mean, I am all for doing whatever you want. That's the thing, I am just curious about where intent lies versus where tooling and or production sits.

Again, I probably don't know anything. I'm just rambling because I haven't rambled in a while. It's fun to type and pretend to be one of those keyboard warriors that I really despise. Haha. Or maybe that's my alter ego? Hmm. Neighbourhood Watch my Shadow, yeuo bloughdy wænkeuh!
