title: Fuckton of Shit
about:
Going to work on an album incrementally again. Just made this song, as of posting this. Will add songs as I go.

This is the first time I bounced stems to separate files, as well as mixed with opinionated listening EQ for my headphones. I made a preset for it, which makes my favorite songs from years ago sound like how I remember them sounding, compared to specifically being "flat", or something like that. Just a new way to try things.

111 is a freeway, I always quoted it as a kid when we'd drive by, "111, zipped up the case of jacket". For some reason when making this first track, I thought it should be called 111, to reference that. I didn't know it also has that existential positivity guru association as well. Felt a bit lackluster today, I equated it either to being lacking of sleep, or because people out in the world are just meh. Or I was looking too much into it. Or back from vacation. Or, time to put that sentiment into making new music again, even if I have been doing that for gosh knows how long now. But yeah, some videos online that showed up keep pointing towards being creative as well, rather than passively watching content or things like that.

This first song isn't necessarily new grounds, but again, I am not worrying about that right now. I like the crunchiness that the mix brings to this writing style of mine, so that's all that counts for now. I like it enough, and I have the inclination to make it into something, so here goes!

"111 number meaning" ->

"The 111 number is widely considered a powerful, positive spiritual sign representing new beginnings, manifestation, and alignment with one’s life purpose. Often called an "angel number," it signifies that your thoughts are manifesting into reality, suggesting a need to focus on positive goals. It acts as a green light to take action and pursue opportunities.Key Usage Examples & Interpretations:Manifestation: A sign to focus on positive thoughts, as 111 indicates your ideas are manifesting rapidly.Spiritual Awakening: Interpreted as a direct message of guidance and awareness.New Beginnings/Love: Suggests a fresh start, a new relationship, or a deepened connection is approaching.Career & Opportunity: Prompts taking initiative, embracing leadership, and pursuing a true career calling.Medical (UK/Non-emergency): In the UK, 111 is the NHS phone number for urgent, non-emergency health advice, acting as a direct line for care."

Again, I know it's possibly confirmation bias, I am aware of that. But what does giving it a try really have in the negative? I would just be watching YouTube mindlessly right now anyways, so what good is that? At least I can start working on ANOTHER sub par album (humor, I value what I do!).

And with the strife I have been feeling, and had been feeling today, getting these hints at "it's fine, you fucking got this." That feeling, that's what I am pointing towards.

The project working folder seemed to want to be called "The Pendleton". When uploading this to Bandcamp, it wanted to be called "Fuckton of Shit". Yeah, I don't know either.

I was moving a bunch of previously finished projects over to my archives, and I reencountered the project folder for Ferret Train. I had forgotten that it seemingly consisted of multiple weeks folders' of tracks, to which I picked my favorite from those, and it was a "compilation album" from those few weeks, to some extent. I am open to that happening to this project again. I think having seen that yesterday, and the inclination to record today, that is what sealed the deal to start this.

Been listening to AIC and SYL lately, you can probably tell. I have been wanting to write deep dark lyrics, so I think this project could potentially be beholden to the grounds for that. Essentially, bringing light to the "voices" (not audible, but sentiments rather) that one constructs throughout one's life, which build up over time, consisting of critiques, judgements, things like that. It is meant to be an objective look at them, not dismissing them, not embracing them, just seeing them, as they are, as they are heard.

I realized a week ago or so that I was going to write them out on their own, just to see them, learn them, and see how the effect me. I then also realized that it might be harder to make an album of that kind of intensity if I were to exercise them, without it being in the moment of recognizing them. I mean like, making an album retroactively after having started the process of recognizing them.

This is also paving way for what new entire doors are available to me, which I never perceived of, nor would have felt capable, nor would have embraced or felt comfortable in, before having gotten to where I am now. By that I mean, I think this has been one of the roadblocks for me as a person, period [💅]. And let alone for creative growth, this is a whole new dimension.

The new perspectives I encountered are that my inner critic has been holding me back from doing things I want to in life, because it critiques my inner self, before it can recognize itself, make itself known to the world, or even speak the thoughts. So now it is a more solid pathway.

I used to filter my thoughts before I would even know they were there. Now it's up to me to filter them after having been cognizant of them, not before. This seemingly has been "the death of my personality" [Okay, that has to be a song title, right??]. It wasn't *my* personality mind you though. That's the important part. I now know that, for me at least, my personality is determined by the things I do, not the things I don't do. It's much more open ended than I had realized. Life, I mean (lol? fuck? what the fuck?).

I fucking swear I don't do drugs. I only say that because it's amazing what mindfulness, meditation (I think?), and mental self-awareness can do. It has been astounding. Finding out how to become aware of your own patterns, what are your traits, what others imply onto you, things like that. Find where you are, and they end.

Like I mean I probably would have critiqued this entire writing to hell, if I thought about what was actually "logical" or not. I have plenty of feelings, I have for a long time. I just hadn't been aware that I was allowed to act on them. Or to speak them, as is, without judgement.

That's it! One is judged by their character, not who they are. I think that's a saying of some sort, sounds familiar. Probably a big quote.

Okay, super fucking pumped for this. I love spring. Not that this growth only can happen during spring. I think usually I just get overwhelmed when there are plans and non-free-time available. Cultivating it as much as I feel is healthy, so much room for improvement.

But yeah, having the critic out of the way, I plan to write stories, characters, interactions, and character depictions of these generalizations. Like the things the critic says, each could be described by a story, fictitious, but rooted in "reality", per se. Ok, gotta go! Will talk more later. I think may have covered part of this in Episode 5 of the podcast. Will go over it more once I have a chance. I made a helluva lot of progress, I am proud of that! [speaking of this first song, and all of this writing].

Edit: So yeah, I didn't know inherently that "111" is a "magic number", I just know it was a fun thing I remember from a kid. But it is kind of peculiar that it seemingly is descriptive of the time I am going through on a personal experience right now, in life. But yeah, I know confirmation bias kind of points to that sort of thing. But there are a plenty of other "random magic numbers" which people associate meanings with, and I happened to think of that one. Yeah so I don't believe or not believe in "numerology" (hadn't heard of it before having searched 111 on Google just now), it just seemingly connected the dots of things, you know?

This project is kind of connecting back to Progscapes as well, which was the album before the drinking discovery and or concerns, when I was just about to turn 21. Again, not that it specifically connects or doesn't connect, I don't see the correlation yet. It just is kind of intriguing how I kind of feel like I am returning to some kind of home base, like how I mentioned feeling like I was back in my positivity of my teen years, back to the days of 2019 and earlier, that sort of thing. I seemingly have "disconnected" from the time train that is the incrementing years. Not that I am some self-centered "I will be young forever!", not that. Not that kind of egotistical thing. It's more that, I don't need to follow the trends that come with each year. I am still going to keep in the loop, embrace them for what they are, I just don't have to onboard them for what "my life" is, for me. It's on my terms. Listening to Recreational Outrage 2 right now, and man, it is fucking awesome. I am so happy with how articulate my music has gotten, even if I "don't know what I am doing". That's the thing. I do know, and now I am starting to believe that as well. I can't wait to hear how this project goes. Not that it has expectations, but just that I am excited for what unfolds. So happy to have found all of this creative potential.

I was also talking today about making music videos, where maybe the acting, props, and or visual voicing doesn't match the music. I like the idea of intentionally recording two music videos, for two separate songs, but then intentionally using the video of one song, vice versa. Flipping the video, breaking everything. Seems really neat.

Before listening to RO2/writing this edit, I was listening to 111, and man, I really like the mix/master on it. The EQ with opinionated headphones, it works fucking awesome. I'm curious about any other presets I can make now. It's awesome what a reference can do to help making solid mixes. Both have helped in different ways, I mean, no EQ, flat EQ, opinionated EQ, there's probably even more I can do going forth, which will only further influence the kinds of mixes I make.

Edit: As of Jul 30, this project ended up only having two tracks. I think I ended up feeling like my writing changed concepts, and some other folders came up after this one. There are a lot of cool songs in those, and I think those ended up being their own thing, and this was kind of the intro to it in a way. There might be more from this folder, I don't remember for sure. Going to start Recreational Outrage 3 in a few days, I have 5 days off to just write. Going to see what happens. Even if it doesn't end up being Recreational Outrage 3, whatever works to be honest. I 'intend' (loosely) to write 10 songs a day, then slim down to ones that I enjoy, only. Much to the likes of HARRY, Ferret Train, and so, many, bad, decisions. Again, it could go totally different. If I like all of them, and it's too big for a CD, so be it. It will be digital only.

But yeah. Back to this, I think I was excited with the things I had learned, and that quick rapid-fire release of songs, that was what I was mixing things up from. I still released some quick songs after this, but I think the feeling of going back to iterating a lot, and sorting songs, that is the general consensus which took place after these songs were published.

I was consequently thinking about Ferret Train about a week ago, and yesterday too. I think I already added it, but I don't remember for sure. It's the premise that it's one of my very favorite albums I've ever made. And I think it's actually that it's fairly disjointed in a way. If I "try to write disjointed", that comes across differently than when you just write a bunch of things of varying degrees, sort through them, and pick plain favorites. Recr 1 was peculiar with it's songs, it was the first variant. All and any goes, yet not "intentional" per se. No sequencing, merely just all on board. Elkosaurus was like that too, but in that it had the goal of being "the worst album ever". So while "anything goes", Recr doesn't have a goal.

I think this prefaces how I feel my heart is going from here. I have yet to try it, per se. But I am very very excited. I think Recr 3 is the "conclusion" and or "climax" of the series, because it is essentially when the reins of the critic have been untangled, and while it's still being presented under the critical moniker, I think the journey is going to show that the walls have been torn down, by the end of the record.

I am not merely declaring this is the end of the series though. It is the end of that chapter though, at least in that it's depicting that. I think if and when Recr 4 were and or does come around, it will be about the concept about worrying about what others think of you, rather than your internal critic, or those who put it there. It may be a bit challenging too though, as right now, I merely am not specifically worried about what people think of me. I mean, I guess I do abstain from sharing things because I know people won't get it, but maybe that's because I am making assumptions. I think the point is that now I don't have fear of presenting my works and findings for what they are and what they mean to me. I just know that they are abstract, and not everyone will understand it. It's not that I am preventing to share it out of fear and or of criticism though, at least I don't think that's the case. I mean, I'd love to hear otherwise if you think it still is out of something like that.

But yeah, maybe the depths to which the further records go, will be a bit lighter. Not by intent, but by that because that perspective isn't coming from my own experience, it would be by that of someone else, like a character who is in that experience. That is also part of what I have been learning to get into, writing about others' experiences, even if I haven't experienced them. That was something I have been uncomfortable with for a long time, so I am excited that it isn't troublesome to me to the extent that it was before.

These things could be totally unrelated though, I mean that maybe these concepts may or may not show up in the Recreational series itself, I have yet to see what fits. Everything is up in the air. It's all ambiguous. I am learning to be more okay with that as well. That used to be essentially a non-option for me in the past as well. So yeah, lots of changes.

"Slow progress is still progress" - Devin Townsend

tracksInfo.title: Perspect2ve
tracksInfo.about:
Tried cross-checking both flat EQ and opinionated EQ for my headphones. I also tried to make a clearer mix overall, carving parts out of each, allowing parts of each to make way for one another. The mastering sounds a little odd on my Mac speakers, maybe it's just because it's a single-tracked, and I am used to panning my mixes. So it's probably just that. But I think it is very very clear. Was about to add CHOW tape and SketchCassette onto it, I think as a way to make it sound intentionally analog, but then I thought I should leave it blank this time, since I did all of the mixing stuff.

I recorded it on my phone, with USB-C and the Scarlett, my Line 6 for my guitar, and GarageBand (well, rendered in Logic) for the bass tones. The drums are GarageBand drums, rendered to a WAV file. All mixed in Logic, with my Sony MDR-7506's, thanks to EQ correction with eqMac.

Since I recorded it with GarageBand, that means the resulting Logic project and stems are inherently in 44.1khz. I would want to use 48khz sources ideally, but for recordings done quickly on GB, this is more than plenty okay. Even moreso okay, it's still 24-bit sources, which I very much do value.

This time I bounced to 44.1/24 for the mix, then 44.1/24 for the master, then a final 44.1/16 POWr-2 for the distributable.

I was listening to the demos off of Colloquial Outtakes before this track, an hour of two earlier. I think that's where the inspiration for classic writing came from, once again. This project is going to be along those lines anyways, but it just felt natural again. And my phone was only at 25% battery too, and it didn't die while recording! Sick! The iPad tended to run out quickly. I was going to use that, but then I remembered the phone setup. Might keep using the phone for more projects, I mean, that's why I got it, because of the USB-C and ease of GB recording. So, yeah, that's right! I kind of forgot about that, the video production projects took the spotlight. I still have videos 2 and 3 in the works for Half Awake. The sources for 2 are taken, I haven't made clips or pictures for 3 yet. Can't wait! Just haven't had that "aha" for what 3 should look like yet. I think it should be that night one I was talking about making, originally, before having gotten the new phone. Maybe that can be tonight...

Turns out it had only used 7% battery for the entire recording, considering it was also powering the Scarlett, sick!!

title: Half Awake
about:
[hello on the 17th 👋]

I think I was starting to really get into my head about the ADHD and or AuDHD stuff, and I think doing a lot of thinking and growth at the same time, it led to me feeling like I could relax and just be very peaceful. This was some of the most relaxed I've ever felt in a long time. It was very interesting. I think just being very present all week, namely, having a nice schedule that I was able to stick to, and going for walks before I would go to work in the morning, this closeness to being in the now, fully, and openly, it really helped things click for me. I think these mornings helped put my potential room for growth into perspective as well. It was these mornings that allowed me to trust my instincts, and think through wanting to put more energy into caring for myself. Not coming from a place of lack though, but more from a place of thankfulness, and safety. This album wasn't one I planned to make, nor was it something conscious per se. I really was just very very relaxed while making it, no critic, no hopes, no ambitions. Just that sweet, sweet feeling you get when you are about to fall asleep. I was basically riding that all into the night. This project was record and released on the same night. I made the artwork while listening back to the recordings after the fact. I didn't actually master it in the normal sense, I did the 'mastering' moreso in something like the mix bus, then just did a mastering session merely just for crossfades. I didn't use a lower bitrate nor sample rate, merely because these sonically are very big, so I might as well release the full blown masters. Just thought I'd try that again, as I hadn't done that in a while.

So this came from a state of articulating presence, as well as the internal feeling I was feeling about standing up and doing things for myself. Not in the ego sense, but in the empowered sense. That was the same push that led me to get my new phone. And that's where I am at now. I listened to the impulse, worked through it, trusted it, and now I am going forward after having made a positive decision for myself. So in a way, now looking back, while essentially being just a listener like you, this sounds like it is actually the next part of the story after Ferret Train's song "Integrate". Very cool.

That was an interesting part to this project too, in that it was yes, very instinctual, but also I barely listened back to it at all, other than while making the artwork for it, and doing the crossfades. It was just full presence, documenting it, living with the feelings I was feeling [while making it], and allowing whatever that was to be made public. That is the best thing, and very new to me. That is an amazing facet. I am working on bringing this to more parts of my life. I think in a way, maybe this is a subconscious metaphor utilizing creativity to explain how I am in the process of letting go of what people think of me and what I do, letting loose from that critic that holds so tight. This is the raw manifestation of that. It's one thing to do it blatantly with something like Recreational Outrage, where it is boisterous, kind of proving it's own point by virtue of it's weight. But this, is much more strong, much more subtle. What seems possibly less big, it actually makes it seems insurmountable. When it is that open, there's not much room to critique. I mean in the aspect of insecurity or things like that. Sharing ones feelings and not having to worry about perception, that is a whole different ballgame.

It's like all of my internal self was pointing me in one single direction, and that was towards standing tall, and not being a push over. I would take the steps and leaps for what I needed for me. The names for the songs were all established mid song, and I memorized it to the end to where I would name it that. So there definitely seemed to be a common theme that was building in my head, based on the stuff I was watching at the time. I don't have as many pictures from this time period, as with the project from a few weeks earlier. I think it was because I was trusting the feeling itself, and letting that drive it, rather than it being a certain narrative or thing that was driving the work.

I think while being tired and thinking of what artwork to make for this, I did picture the black pyramids again, the ones I remembered during Carpincho. It seemingly kind of relates to the ones I remember from The Harmony Codex as well, while those are colorful. I think the shape on the cover of this project is kind of like the light being on Impossible Tightrope. I was picturing some kind of thing like that for how I felt with this project.

Yeah, and these were all recorded sequentially, all on the same night. I think they were all played on the night of the 14th, and while barely not falling asleep in bed, I was making the artwork. And hence the name, which also came to right when completing the project, "Half Awake" was the first that came to my head, and it seemed to completely represent what this was.

This project kind of reminds me of Wooden Smoke in a way, to some extent as well. While also being something like Devin Townsend's ambient work as well. Man, loving all of these relaxing inspirations. Having different avenues for things really is a blessing.

The tuning for this was whatever I had tried while going to sit down to record. It always seems to be a similar non-Western open chord, namely not 440hz based. I seem to really like how other-worldly it sounds, and feels. The intervals always seem to work out very cool. Not even that it's specifically feeling like it's from another country, but more just something I am unfamiliar with. There are definitely aspects of it that seem like they are from back east, I just have no experience in that kind of music, so I don't know where my ear for it came from, nor my intrigue with it. The closest might be to that of Devin's work at times, or the ASMR/meditation videos I listen to, those tend to have music somewhat like this.

I think while making the art for this, and doing the crossfades, I was actually listening to ASMR at the same time too, which is a first for me. I think it's because I wanted to get into the feel of the work, rather than the *listening* of it. Hence why the entire project feels other-wordly for me. Very dream-like. I am only listening to it all the way through for the first time, as I type to you now. Yeah I heard parts here and there, but not as a listener yet. This project has so much depth, and it's amazing what presence does. Same with letting go. Trusting. Understanding. Empathizing.

I don't know how to describe the name of the last track, the pronunciation of the name came into my head while I made the track. It's "amoshkha", if I were to try to phonetically spell it in another way. It is supposed to be with a g/k sound, and kind of sounding like "Anneke" at the end. There was another way I spelt it, but that name was already associated with some other stuff that I didn't want to come up when looking for the song, so I changed the spelling a bit. I tend to try and look out for that sort of thing. I don't like when things are hard to search for. Whether it's that you find something you weren't looking for (didn't want to see), or that the name is too common and it makes it hard to find at all. Unique names aren't that hard, relatively speaking. It's that people usually want "normal" names, and unique ones of those are what's hard to come by. And for me and my goals/purposes, having far-fetched names isn't too bad of a trade-off. I enjoy them, and it's easy SEO lol. But that's if Google finds your Bandcamp/YouTube pages at all haha. I promise that sharing more of myself by way of promoting my work, that is absolutely on the horizon. It just takes time. Small baby steps.

I think it's work like this that I absolutely want to make videos for.

As I was thinking over what kinds of things I'd want to record video for, I think that was also part of what inspiration led to making this. It wasn't in knowing that I was going to get a phone, and that I would make videos for these songs in this project specifically, but moreso that thinking of what kinds of songs I'd make videos for, that was what made me want to make music that matched that idea.

So by virtue of having enacted both of these ideas, maybe I should make videos for these songs specifically. I can already picture for Amazjhke that it might be sunsets and sunrises at different mountain views, and it would change between different ones, maybe with each chord I play. It would almost be more of a relaxing meditation kind of video, featuring my music, rather than the other way around. I mean, I did make the music first, but in this case, the video and audio would play off of each other so well. I can't wait.

Oh yeah, the idea I was actually thinking of for the video part, it was similar to how my family and I went up to the mountains, I think during the pandemic, to get night pictures of the comet that was only visible up in those clear night skies. I'd want to do something similar.

This project kind of reminds me of Storm Corrosion in a weird way as well, but in a less abstract scary kind of way, and moreso in that other-worldly place kind of vibe. It's like I haven't been to this place before, and now I have arrived. It's one thing to make ambient music. I don't know what this is. I mean, logically and literally speaking, it is just ambient and or meditation music. But in regards to how it relates to the rest of my catalog, wow. Stark contrast. Love it so much. So so much.

[hello on the 23rd]

Been talking with a friend at work, and I thought of the idea to burn them a DVD with the videos I am making for these tracks. This is going to be the first project I make videos for, afterall. Getting the new camera led way to learning video, once again. Maybe I can make it with Kunaki too :)

tracksInfo.title: Resolute
tracksInfo.about:
[from the music video on YouTube]

I think it was a week or two ago, I had the idea come to mind as I was falling asleep. I thought it would be great to record an ambient guitar project, and to record nature footage in slo-mo, and make that into a music video.

I duly made note of that inclination, as I felt it at the heart, rather than some other metric of "should". I ended up feeling like making a few ambient tracks, so I did, a few nights back. Then I ended up getting a new camera, trusting that instinct. I had this big inclination that I wanted to get into video, as I used to be into it at least like as a kid, for projects and such. I didn't do really any creative work with it yet though, so this is like my true breakthrough into it. It's a whole world of more creative expression that I can't wait to delve into, so, I didn't [wait]!

Been walking around town before work in the very early mornings, and I think the beautiful sunrises really made an effect at my internal peace, if that makes sense. I think the cool air, nice schedule, good sleep, it all made for a very homey, cozy feeling, like I had figured things out, even if just for a little bit. That's kind of why I took the leap, and listened to the inclination.

A lot of my internal experience and creative outlet has felt a bit more open-ended as of lately, whether it's through self-exploration, and or learning habits that do and don't help me. I'm fully aware of how it might be perceived as silly just 'young hippy dippy' as Devin Townsend has called it. For me, it's been a very meditational-like experience, where I feel my best when I am just present with 'being', if that makes sense. That's what this kind of music represents for me, that experience of being here, now, and feeling it to the heart. No expectations, no loud mind. It's like you opened up the back of the computer, and you are dusting off all of the parts that haven't powered up in a while, or something.

Been really contemplating what "adulthood" means. I feel down about how many people I encounter which seem to have lost their spark for life, or just can't let themselves connect to it anymore. This is the very thing I don't want to lose sight of, even if it makes me look silly, immature, or just plain not understood. For me, adulthood is responsibility for those you care for, including yourself. I can't explain how much more grounded I feel when I take care of myself. When I listen to what I need, make note of it, and work on it, it's so much better.

The music for this album 'Half Awake', it was all composed at night. So while the video for this was during the day, I think I envisioned a night video instead. But it's okay, this is the first go-around. That was another thing I really am happy with. I have much less fear in doing it right the first time, because there isn't a "right". I can always make another new song and or video, and I will just learn from what I didn't like about the current one. That's my new mindset, which I've been trying on for size. So while I still picture this music being night-aesthetic in video terms, I enjoyed the video making process for this one, and I like the video itself, so that can be enough, especially since this is the very first one anyways. No need to have a high bar to start out. I already have made a lot of progress jumping into it, so that's what counts as well.

The crow in the video was not planned. I heard it in the bushes, wasn't sure what it was, hopefully not a bobcat or mountain lion, lol. Thankfully it wasn't. It was neat that it flew through the shot later on as well. I think it was the same one at least.

I plan to make a video for each of the three songs for this project. I am going to make a DVD for all of these for a friend as well. We've been talking at work about 'big' life stuff, like all of this deep mind work, and just ways of perceiving the world. I am thankful to have found people like this to connect on about that stuff. Not everyone seems to be open to exploring the existential stuff, so it's nice to have that. I don't think I can forget that that's probably been a big part of the peace in this new feeling of calm, too. I can also rest easy that now I know I am not the only one with this deep perception and or concern. I know I am not the only one, obviously, but having a personable experience has made it solidified. Hearing and watching it is one thing, having the camaraderie is something else.

The music for this project, and the project itself, was 'hastily' done as well, so it would make sense that the video is okay to do so as well. Not in the negative sense, but just that, it's meant to be just a thing, like, just made. No biggie. Taking your inclinations and running with them, I'd say. It's seemingly tied to the ever-growing process of trusting myself, not being afraid of myself anymore. I can go into what that is at some point. I'd love to write music about this too, lyrically speaking. Learning metaphor and song structure are in the cards too.

tracksInfo.title: Pronounce
tracksInfo.about:
[hello from Aug 17!]

This is song two of the EP/album, "Half Awake". I've had the clips recorded for a few months now, getting around to finishing things up! I plan to burn DVDs of these music/video combos. In concept, this could be another Kunaki release as well, the first debut of my video experiments! At least in the creative sense, where the video isn't just a showcase for the music. For me, these videos work really well at exploring the feeling of the music.

The idea for making videos for it was also because I want to share it with a friend, and having a 'thing' to experience the music just seemed natural to me, for this one. Just having the sound itself, is one thing. CDs are cool for that. But for having video too, that's a super fun experience! This one felt like a video-based soundscape. I think it's my mind's eye that wanted to be described with the camera clips I got.

These clips were recorded a few days after when the first video was recorded, this one was on April 27.

tracksInfo.title: Amazjhke
tracksInfo.about:
The third and final installment of "Half Awake", in video form. I think this, at least sonically, is my favorite of the three songs. The depth that this mind journey takes you on, it very much lands at home here, by the third track.

I recorded the footage for this on June 24.

With my current headphone EQ, which has more accurate bass response, the mixing/mastering of these tracks are definitely fairly low-end heavy. But it's what it is. I did all of that on the night that I made those songs (April 15), so I am going to keep the mixes as they are.

Fantastic kudos to ffmpeg for allowing the 2 GB H.264 iMovie video to be reeencoded to a mere 193 MB HEVC. It's moreso that it looks the same quality essentially. HEVC is goated.

title: Variation 6
about:
This is a collaboration album between myself and IndigoBassNotes on YouTube.

They provided the base improvisations/recordinds/ideas, then I added some of my own additions on top. I then mastered and crossfaded the tracks, then made the artwork. They came up with the track names, and I think I came up with the duo name. There were a set of other ideas as to what this project could be, it's a bit more open-ended, not story-based as much as it potentially could have been. I made the artwork, while listening to the songs. That seems to be a great way for my mind to 'draw' how I feel the music sounds. I used Photopea, with a bunch of steps. It's not actually an analog image, it's all digital. You could probably tell though. I like when artwork looks like it had been printed at one point, so I try to emulate that.

One of the image sources I used that I found was called "Variation 6", and that felt like a suited name for this project, for some reason. The ambiguous nature of it seemed intriguing, much like how I feel while listening to the songs. Turns out it's also related to Bach's work, I didn't intend for that reference, that is more of a coincidence seemingly.

Originally the album was going to be called "Atoms with Nervous Energy", but I wasn't sure what the duo would be called.

Seemingly there are other members over at IndigoBassNotes, not sure how to credit them, as it just seems to be one person that manages the channel, and leads the improvisations.

My favorite song is Lullaby :)
I wish Fo was longer, love it too.

Edit:

I'm not sure quite when the source tracks themselves were recorded, but they were sent to me between Apr 2, and Apr 15. And around two weeks ago, May 9, that's when I added my parts to the concepts and did the initial mixes. Last night I did the combined mastering, like with leveling and general EQ fixes, and bouncing to CD specs (encoding-wise I mean, not yet an actual CD, it has been discussed though, for the sake of having something cool :) ).

In general, I tend to take a long time at getting things done. I mean, across the board, in my life, with my goals, with working on things with other people. That has been of interest to me lately. I struggle with having prioritization, outside of mere intrigue, novelty, or plain interest. I seemingly have to have one of those to make something go into action. Or also, curiosity, or wanting to learn how something works.

I am ever so slowly (much like the nature of the issue itself) working towards finding a solution to this. If anything, I've been on the edge of looking for a solution to this for years now, at least a decade, or more to be honest. The recent learnings into ADHD and or similar possibilities, that was one of the facets that seemed to click for me. But I am very wary of confirmation bias, so I have been working to learn more about what "normative" people function like, as that seems foreign to me, because I only know how I work, and how I seem to be lacking, by virtue of how others have mentioned.

I am not bringing this up as a critique to others who mention it, it merely just does connect the dots, whether it's me, my habits, my mind, how I function, whatever the case, something in relation to me seems to be different to how others operate, as it comes up a lot across multiple fields of my life. Even in open-ended interests like music ventures as such, I still "procrastinate". But this time I specifically knew and made clear that it wasn't rooted in avoidance. I think part of what I feel is that I tend to care deeply about what I work on, and if I don't feel at heart like it's what I can work on at the time, I will elide it for a later time. That was the case here. There are other moments of procrastination where it's less discerning than that, but that was the case for this project.

The underlying commonality seems to be that I don't have timelines for how I will feel, I can only place effort into how I feel now, and let that flourish, going through whichever stages it brings later down the road. Yes, very flighty I agree. I wish it didn't work this way. If I try to force work when the interest is not there, I get negative, out of focus, and the work starts to suffer. In my opinion. And I also tend to just want to do it even less, getting to the point of resenting the work or the nature of the work itself. Much along the lines of losing sight of why the work is necessary in the first place. So maybe that's part of it too, the intrigue has to be there because the nature of why I am doing something falls out of focus very quickly, if I am to be in the moment with the work itself.

But yeah. Okay, going to go on a run now. I was starting work on AstroSurfing, doing some crossfades and (re)mastering for the songs from those sessions. It's gonna be like a 2 hour album probably. That set of songs is seemingly similar in creative spirit (of where it comes from, not sonically, necessarily) to the timeframe of "Catastrophic". That springtime balls-to-the-wall-writing, where I just write and write and write. Then after that, I seemingly will write my favorite album of the year.

I am cognizant that it could be hand in hand, rather than causal. I like the spring, so maybe I just tend to write during the spring. Or it's when schedules are open. Whatever the reason, even if multiple at play, those kinds of patterns seem to work out. I haven't had that kind of click this year, per se. It's been kind of a slow burner in my opinion. I think the depth of emotions and growth as a person internally has made it a bit wild this year. The impulsivity of my work is at an all time high, and today I kind of became cognizant of it, it kind of gave me anxiety. But I looked into how the work might be just a representation of what I am going through, so it is what it is. While I might not want to be doing what I am doing, it is where I am at. I just am more excited for the future (yay!) once again, rather than with the present. Not that I don't like the present, but I feel like moreso using the present as a growth period, to help foster where I do want to get to.

I think it might be on of the turnings of the Dunning-Kruger effect too, if I were to shoehorn it, lol. I think (actually, after some talking yesterday, maybe the perspective helped) that the new sight of seeing where I am at, where I've been, where I've been going, where I can go, all of those are (to be fair, always, but not felt always) changing, so I think the arrow is moving directions again.

Programming was an interest for a long time. I still love it, I still utilize it. It hasn't been fun for a while though. I think the novelty wore off, and I learned the things that I wanted to learn based on what I wanted to achieve, and what I needed from it. So it was a success. It just didn't end up where I "thought it could" (aka, a career, or being a "tech bro"). Much of that is identity-based too, which in general, I don't feel I have been very identity-based much of my life. But that's part of the learning of perspective stuff I have been doing too, so that could be something else hooked into that.

While I feel I could potentially be a mixer/mastering engineer, I don't know if identity-wise I am there. Or same with a traveling the world artist. Maybe it's just a phase, as they say. Or maybe this is the kind of "play" that people in their young years do. Maybe that's why it feels foreign to me. It really is open-ended, huh? Ha, interesting.

And much to the likes of how I had trouble saying before if I "was something", aka a guitarist, programmer, mixing engineer, mastering engineer, that sort of thing, I am more able to say that I am those things, even if it's not me on a professional scale.

That's been a big realization as of the last 2 days or so, that your professional outlook isn't what determines if you made it, or what your identity is. I mean, it *can be*, but it doesn't have to be, if you don't want it to be. It's however you want to conclude if you "made it", again, in my opinion, and current perspective.

That was a nice writing session, I think I am back into the other parts of my brain again. What parts of your brain write like that kind of stuff? Is that flow state? This is "logic me" talking again, like without the deep stuff. Man, I love the "deep side", it does get a bit much if you stay there all of the time though. Is that what depression is, come to think of it? Much of the times I feel down, it's that "deep side", but powered by a negative context, lack of belief and or belief in the negative. But the deep side is very powerful as something to act on, regardless. So that's why I think I have been so happy lately, I've been fueling it with positive content, even if that is one-sided. Much like Devin's music, only being one way or the other, that's probably not healthy.

Again, probably my most used word right now, perspective. It's all about perspective, folks!
Brandon

Just changed my Minecraft skin, finally! I made it a few weeks ago. Was going to do more photo work on it, still plan to. But felt the inclination to just start playing the game with it, and find out how I want to edit it that way. I like that it's less of a persona of me, and moreso just like me in real life. I think that could be part of the self-acceptance, *perspective*, and "integrate".

I was going back looking at how my catalog has changed over time, and I think I see a few more stages than I had seen previously. Very neat. I think Critically Wired and or Ferret Train was definitely the start of the new phase, which I think I am currently in, and or possibly in the exit of. Again, no expectations, no plans, just feeling. It's only seen retrospectively, I have tended to find. Jestershit was the end of that period, Potential Self was the next. Critically Wired was kind of the very far end of that period, right on the climax, before going to the next phase. Ferret Train was the descent down the mountain, while still being very high elevation. Then it got very deep in the ocean nearing towards Half Awake. Maybe that's it, Recreational Outrage 1 is an ascending album, while Recreational Outrage 2 is a decending album, in terms of intensity and or emotional state, or something. I don't know. Maybe it has to do with sadness, timelines, a bunch of stuff. Again, this is my initial feeling, looking at it. Much of this could be looked over again in the future. I love learning about myself from my catalog.

Much to the likes of what I was researching about how one may turn to chaos, experimentation, or abstract/absurdist things when times are tough, maybe that's what the link is between things like Elkosaurus, Recreational Outrage, and Ferret Train. It's what the time they were made during was rooted in, in commonality, and the response to how to handle it. The first was the loss and grief of what was/wasn't experienced during the pandemic. The second was dealing with "adult negativity" (having to cope with others who seemingly have pushed down their childhood innocence and hope for the world), and the third is the response to the grief of losing a close influential person in the family, and the ramifications of what that did to my identity as a person. So inherently, that's what also manifested the change in writing style for the albums from then, onto now, same with the experimentation. Again, perspective.

Part of what I had realized was let alone my mortality (like, feeling it, not just knowing it), and realizing how people change to different generational roles, be it child, parent, grandparent. Like, if you lose a grandparent, that means you are closer to being someone who cares for someone else, ie, a parent, than you are to someone who is still cared for, ie a child. So, so much of my self identity and perspective of my own self, my own life, my own goals, ambitions, it was all very much rooted in still perceiving myself as young, ie, lack of perspective of what capabilities were available to me, rather than what I had believed of myself.

Thinking of oneself still as young (self proclaimed associations mind you; incapable, not knowing enough about the world, doesn't trust one's own decisions), that was very much heavily present, whether in habit, or just by way of function. It wasn't that I actually thought or felt that I was young at age, I knew I was an adult, I knew I was out of school. I just didn't believe I was capable. And while I had already been working on not thinking of myself negatively, I also hadn't yet thought of myself positively. And honestly, that's still being constructed as we speak. I am still operating under the terms of "okay, think of myself as if I were to think positively of myself", rather than "I do 100% feel I am worthy". So 1000% progress is being made. I *am* fucking proud of myself, I just have a weight of emotion on top of it keeping me from believing it. Maybe it's because it's hard to find people, in general (regardless of one's outlook to need someone to confirm it), who feel that way about you. I don't want to find people just to have someone to appreciate me. It's not an ego-based thing. It's just very difficult to be the only one who holds myself up, with this new self-belief system. But again, hey, at least I have at least one person holding me up; myself. That's better than before!

And again, not that people don't believe in me, or love me for who I am. I mean, who am I to decide that. It's just that everyone else seems to have this same shadow issue, and they are unable to support me in who I am, because they are in the same boat. They can only support me through their shadow. So maybe that's it, that I long to connect with people who also have done this integration. Much of this sounds like gobbledeygook, but it seems to explain what kinds of things I'm working on, so, so be it. Much like I have mentioned, not that I believe or don't believe that it works, it just seems like it is working though, so results speak for themselves.

And not to discount the magical people I recently have been in contact with, who *have* been on this same wavelength. What. Are. The. Fucking. Odds. Time and place right? Like, it's astounding. Again, it could be a perception thing. Or maybe because I am speaking that language, those kinds of connections are going to flourish. Of course if I wasn't thinking like this, someone else probably wouldn't bring it up. But I know and feel the people I do have deep connections with, those very much are real. So I think part of that is also reminding myself of that. It's easy to slip into that belief of "oh I've never had real friends, or close friends". What is that mindset? I mean, it's not true. I also is very rude to the people who have been kind over the years. But again, if what you are looking for from people hasn't been met, then how does that feeling resolve? If it wasn't lacking (of your specific needs, not the virtue of how they did help), then you wouldn't feel that way, right? And to be honest, I don't know the question to that.

Gonna go listen to music, go on a drive, go for a run. Hell yeah. Keep up the great work, chap [was this monologue to myself?].

"Getting mad at people for what they were unable to provide for you is unfair to them. This can be for friends and family. It is good to be thankful for the lessons and virtues they did teach you, and for how they were there for you in how they knew how to be."

Just thought of something along these lines while having water just as I was leaving. Had to come back and sit down to write it. I think it articulates how I feel about certain connections of mine in life. If anything, it has brought up more empathy and gratitude as well, because it *puts things into perspective*. Getting mad at someone for something they couldn't have changed, that's projecting your grief of "what could have been" onto that person, and it is making it so they have no way to deal with the guilt you put onto them.

So maybe that's [part of] the solution to this. It's not to place the blame back where it "came from". It's to sit with it, and see it as it is, and to live with the roots from which the tree blossomed from.

Like even with the new things to have learned, and conclusions to be made, it has only made me love the people more, because it reminds me just how much they do dearly love me, and care for me. And it also mitigates any of those negative feelings towards them. It's different than it being stuffing those down either. To me, it feels moreso like healing those wounds. Once you tend to yourself, you allow yourself to start to understand them, then you don't have to point the finger of blame at them.

Love is in the world, folks. ❤️

And yeah, it's not pushing your negative feelings down, pushing them away, or negating them for being "wrong". The feelings are feelings. You feel through them, and then they go away. This has helped immensely. I can't believe how peaceful life is after having those worked through. There will always be more hard times, more new things to work through and to learn. But I think nature of what mechanism you choose to handle those occurrences, that's what makes all of the difference. And part of the perspective part, we didn't know we had a choice in how to deal with things. If you only know one way to cope, you internalize it as being the only way. Perspective, perspective, perspective.

Love love love.

title: Jung-L-Gym
about:
Hello, as of the night of Apr 17th!

This was a set of 'demos' I recorded over just about 6 days. It was one of those projects (as of now) where it was just what it was, now looking at it. It wasn't a planned thing, it was just whatever it turned into.

[It was from about Mar 26 through Mar 31; some demos didn't get used, so it was technically shorter; aka the 30th]

The hopes and interest in just writing, simple as that, is now back at play again. Recreational Outrage 2 has been almost complete for a few weeks now, and I think I was getting a bit too overwhelmed and or bored with it. So by the nature of that, I ended up trying out new things again, and these demos were some of the ones that happened.

Whether by intention or not, things are once again not releasing at the time they are done. Not that this was that long ago, but I just released a project a few days ago, which I released as soon as it was done. So while this isn't much further from that, this is a few weeks delayed.

The projects from this were of interest in me wanting to try recording, writing, and demoing from merely just my iPhone again. It even goes back to using my iRig 2 again, now I can very much hear the reduction in capture quality. This time though however, I made sure to use proper gain staging, and at least somewhat tried to make better mixes overall as well. Note that it was all still mixed on my phone, as that's what I wanted to try to do. I think I did a combination of phone speakers and headphones, to cross check a bit. Oh yeah, and it is still GB bass cab tones, GB drums, and back to my Line 6 Spider IV for my classic guitar tones. I think that was the main interest, I wanted to see what I could come up with when using the tech I had used for a very long time, but with my improved production practices/ears. I am happy with how it turned out! I used Logic Pro to crossfade and master the tracks. That helps a ton as well. Even if a mix isn't too great, a master can still go a long way as well. Ideally it would be a great mix too, but if you don't have one, mastering still helps a lot too ☀️

Oh yeah, and this time, I realized I would try to line up all of the tracks to their transients so that everything felt more in line with itself. This is something that much of my early catalog with this recording style suffered from. Even if I were to have played it in time properly, the recording delay, or what have you, that would set the track back or forward a few milliseconds. I hadn't realized that this was the cause, and that a simple moving of the region by such a small amount, that was the only fix, super simple. My internal critic had instead thought that my playing was all over the place (well maybe it was, but that's another thing lol), and thus I hadn't realized it was a (lack of) editing error, rather than a playing or conceptual issue. So this time I played exactly as I normally have and would have, yet after each stem, I made sure that it was on the metronome, just like I had played along with it as I recorded the song. This makes the next tracks more in time as well, as everything before it is much less smeared. Groundbreaking! I think Sigma Freud is the key track here. Really like the vibe. I think it sounds great too. Really starting to feel like I am clicking with what mixing and mastering are. It's like when you mix paint colors, rather than only painting with primary colors. Transitioning between parts of a scene are a key point to the cohesion of the image, that's the same thing with mixing and mastering. You have to paint the background before you paint the foreground. You have to add details afterwards to make everything click. That's my paint-related description. I was trying to picture how Bob Ross did it.

I think I had recently been listening to some of my older albums again too, just out of curiosity. That made me interested in this writing technique again, as it was very much what I used back then, pretty much exclusively. And alongside that, I have and had been doing a lot of self work, merely into personality stuff, and also realizing that I probably (or rather, I am under the assumption/understanding/premise; not conclusive yet!) that I probably have ADHD. Maybe AuDHD? Again, I am only in the learning phase still, so it's not for certain. I am just trying to essentially go through another rework to wire back memories of my past while growing up, with the new lens of looking at it with ADHD being possibly in the picture. So many confusing scenarios and struggles seem to be explained by it now. That alone, that's moreso what leads me to that feeling than anything else. It's not that right now and everything right now means I have ADHD, it's the overwhelming list of things that add up together, in all small yet meaningful ways. That makes it much more concrete than just a guess, I feel. Am going to look into this slowly. My progress thus far and going forward is to operate and learn under the premise as if I do have AuDHD, and see if the work can help me function more. If it does, that seems to be a helpful note as well.

Oh yeah, so about the names and the artwork and stuff. It is kind of a memer way to take the shizz out of all of the deep learning stuff I've been delving into lately. It's like a playful kick in the nuts (what?) to lighten up the mood I think.

Say like inner critic stuff, feeling isolated, all of those things. This is kind of like a portrayal of that, in a third person sense. And under a huge ginormous magnifying glass. So it's pushed to the limits of what it might or might not be, for the sake of the joke. It's like how comedy routines commonly over-exemplify something to where it becomes absurd. That is this, and there are a bunch of different avenues that this is operating under.

This is now appearing to be the "last" album I make on my iPhone 12 mini. Just got the iPhone 15 Pro! I have been really enthused with getting into video production, and or cinematography. I did a bit back in middle school, but haven't returned to it since. Always enjoyed the creative aspect of it. And now having everything like my music projects, and my Mac for editing and saving projects, it seemed like a no brainer to take the leap and get something to get footage going as well. I've been interested in Apple LOG, so that's the main driving factor. And let alone USB-C. Realizing what comes with that, it was show time. I can record onto my iPhone with the Scarlett, without any adapters or power cables! That's great for making my podcasts, as well as recording projects just like this, but with high quality digital audio, rather than with the iffy analog iRig conversion. So I essentially am able to do what I have been doing with my phone all of this time (everything with my iPad mini and earlier), but all with my phone as well. So this means I can have even less barrier of entry for this sort of thing. All the merrier.

Come to think of it, I think this project and realizing the low quality of the iRig, that's actually what made me want to look into the USB-C iPhones. And that's what reminded me of the high quality footage. And since the 15 has been out for a while, I am not a guinea pig for new 3rd party products either, as that's something that I wouldn't want to worry about. Everything's debugged already, so that makes it a no brainer as well. I still didn't want a larger phone, but the cool things that came with the trade off, I thought I would push away my comfort zone, try something new. That's been the goal for the last while now, and this is another step in that direction. I didn't want to regret it later either. I've been wanting to get into it for a while, and not letting that kind of door open itself seemed counter intuitive, now looking through it with those eyes.

So I chose the phone based on the goals I had, what features I needed/didn't need, and went from there. This very much reminds me of the self-investment like I made for myself when I got Logic Pro. And that was one of the best things I did for myself in the last few years. So much learning, so much more fun, so many misconceptions taken down, and now I can articulate myself better than I could before. I now see my "flaws" as just things I hadn't learned yet. That perspective is something I am so thankful for. You can be a smart cookie with the tools you have, yes. But you also need great tools to do your best work. That is important to me.

I also now feel like learning and growing is an investment into my mental health as well. The fact that these 'silly projects' (I see them more than just that, but for those that don't see it as deep as I do, the might think they are silly; I am being humble goarsh danged it!) have helped me build purpose, excitement, intrigued, and a goal system, that's amazing. I can only hope others could find that too, as well as the happiness that comes with accomplishing things. Oh yeah, that's what I was gonna say. The fact that these 'silly projects' can allow me to conduit my feelings, and communicate them openly, that is fantastic. I desperately need and have needed that for a very long time. And I think building this whole world of 'intrigue', it is fucking fantastic. I love it so much. It's like what Minecraft has and does provide for me (moreso back in my school days), but now with this area of creativity, I have more control over things, I get to build the scope to be whatever I want. I can change the rules of the game at any whim. I don't have to worry about other outside aspects of this. Cumulative growth is so great, I so want to teach this to my kids when they become a reality someday.

Okay, so about the artwork, notions of the song titles, and tracking backstories.

I think I was listening to Illegal Aliens again, and that kind of brought me back into the mood of the songs to the like of tracks 3 and 4.

I don't quite remember the place I made track 1, but it seemingly was at night on a day off, after a run (I am going back through pictures). I think I was interested in the idea of making for fun again, I think it was in the music room. Again trying to remember. Then I made track 2 the next morning at work when on break with friends. I was hoping to get them to add some random lyrics or something, they weren't too enthused. I made Gridlock on the 28th. I think I might have named it that because of the region time alignment if I remember right. Might have been traffickey on the way home from work that day too (both..?).

On the 28th I listened to Sunset Mission on the way to a run, that seemingly could have been inspiration for Gridlock, which I recorded later that night.

Okay, yeah, going through the pictures, I was watching a lot of YouTube about the psychology stuff, learning a lot. Dr. K. is goated.

Yeah yeah it's adding up! Listened to Illegal Aliens on break when eating lunch at In-N-Out. That was inspiration for Sigma Freud, sonically. I was off the next day, so in the morning I made Sigma Freud.

Then in the few hours before making Buzzlord Comical FUCK (what?), I had been watching videos about the history of meme culture. That seemed to be the interest of that evening, for whatever reason. So all of that stuff was derived from what seemingly powered the likes of Elkosaurus, which was also rooted in meme culture during it's time.

It's interesting how much of this seemingly accurately came together when making the album art for this, just tonight. I didn't plan any of this beforehand, nor did I document it. But things like picture on my phone, along with dates, and it being relatively recent in memory, you can really build a lot from it. This seems to be a fairly accurate description of how my projects come about.

Okay. And when 'collaborating' (with words, for insight; not for images! I made this all with my own edits, from online sources, using Photopea) with GPT, I wrote out what seemed to be an explanation for what this album is and was. Note that everything I've discussed thus far, that's the actual thing this was rooted in, all of that stuff. And when coming up with what "idea" this album represents, I seemingly came up with this set of conclusions to tie everything together:

[these are my inputs to GPT, after going back and forth to see what conclusions it came up with]

"""
Are there negative connotations with Jung or Freud?


I am trying to shed light on mental health and psychology, through a "memer" lense of some sort, on an album. I am curious whether depicting Jung and Freud on the artwork with MLG Gamer meme era content alongside the psychology focus. Is this bad taste? It is meant to be a meta humor kind of thing again.

Without connotation to the literal words themselves (which I am now less than happy about), I was going to put a flat bill "Supreme"-branded hat on Freud, to make him look like a memer, and maybe with the 8 bit glasses as well. Will this be interpreted like meta humor usage? I don't want to make the statement appear more grandiose than it is, and I don't want to be rude nor display the wrong kind of message. It is meant to be abstract meta humor at best, I just don't want any accidental side connotations to be concluded from it. It should be obviously clear that it is satire and fully a joke.

I was going to call the album "Jung-L-Gym". The artwork makes Freud into the Stonks meme guy, in front of the graph as well. There's going to be Illuminati on it, as well as the sigma symbol. There's a seemingly named 'title track' (while not the name of the album itself; this felt too un-meta), which is called Sigma Freud. It is meant to be a play on words to his name, but also tie itself into the sigma culture phenomenon as well. There's going to be a play at the 'Are Ya Winnin Son?' meme as well.


Okay, I finished the project.
[I sent it to GPT to see what it would reflect from the image]


Great breakdown.

Also, the sigma symbol is related to the sigma male identity online. And the background is a distorted generic image of a Discord mod's gross bedroom.

So it kind of ties in actual shadow progress (the actual root of this project, seemingly), while it also ties into a bunch of other aspects too.

There's a distorted "Are Ya Winnin Son?" in the upper left too, as if the critic is fading away. The capybara is kind of the "high nogood nobody" which also kind of ties into the weed-smoking meta memer that is depicted with Freud. And of course, that Freud is the stonks dude too.


Okay, another set of ways to describe it. We are in a weird paradigm where "nobodys" online are starting to use research from people way back when, and they are trying to contextualize it in the context nowadays, which is totally different. "I want to improve myself as a person", while he sits in his chair, at home, still playing video games, reading conspiracy theories, being a recluse, but because of the online echo chambers, feels like he's making progress. The gym part also relates back to how people look at these "sigma males" who do all but only gym related stuff, because their egos only allow them to get approval from women. So when these "nobody low-lifes" feel bad about themselves, these ego-based people who look for approval from others, that's who these sad people look up to. And all while doing that, feels like he can't progress at all and blames it on the economy. So his will to try is dependent on the ever-changing world which is bound to fail. So, to no avail, that means he will never get any better.

And the real kick in the seat? The psychoanalysis and actual things that can help you, he uses for clout for approval, rather than actually repairing the things that would get him out of this hellhole that is his life. It's like looking for directions to the nearest strip club in the Bible at church.

This is a very bold observation, being hyper-critical of everyone. Think like Idiocracy the movie.


I have to make clear, I should have prefaced the negativity. If anything, it's through the meta lense of not believing in one self. I don't claim those negative feelings about anyone, I don't feel like that myself. That is meant to represent the self hate one may have for oneself, but externalized making it like it's a third-person point of view. Say like you were to say how much you hate yourself, but were to describe it from the third person point of view, as if you somehow were not part of that group in the first place.

I also want to note that I don't feel like this about myself, this is merely a character, and I am entertaining the concept of it. While I have felt down about myself, this is like if you turned up the saturation to 500%, and it started to get very strong, too much.
"""

Part of how I use GPT is to help with lateral thinking tasks. The more inputs I can get, the more I can discern certain conclusions. It's not that GPT has all the answers, if anything, it has a lot of non-answers, but those are useful as well. Sometimes I can find new solutions because of the things it said which don't always fit the scenario at hand. But then it helps me think about it from a new perspective, so I can get into possibly a more productive state to end up getting to the conclusion I do want to get to.

I do want to re-hone again, that the responses above are merely a thought exercise. It's like the ugliest more critical voices, making them into something tangible. They are not my own, and I don't let them take hold over myself. I do notice they are there though, and how fucking strong they are. I can make good use of them, and exemplify why you don't always want to listen to what they have to say.

Hell yeah. Let's fucking go!

Edit: Hello from the 22nd. Felt like moving the release date for this to be when I posted it, rather than when it was 'finished' in terms of writing. I am going to try that out, that way of doing it. I now see that it's okay that I release things in different order than they were written in. That was a big thing for me for the longest time. But now I see that I think maybe the order of it being ready for me, like internally, that might be the metric that I want to order things by. Not sure I will do this for all of the releases, but we'll see. Maybe I'll give it a go, see how it works for me. I only say that because I have a set of songs from 2025 I still haven't released yet, and they merely weren't uploaded because I didn't get around to it, and or I went to work on other things before finishing them. That's the same thing that happened with this project, to which I then went to work on Half Awake before finishing this. That also means that Recreational Outrage will appear after all of these as well, even though it's been in final mastering/sequencing since around just before the start of this project (3/26 or so, roughly speaking? I did a lot of the bulk lifting on the 3/21 it looks like, retroactively going through the file dates). But I feel like having this constant shuffle of moving album releases forwards and backwards, it is a bit jarring. So while it more properly shows when they were written (which I do value, is still crucial, and I will absolutely still make note and annotate), I want the release pattern to be a bit more straightforward. This goes for album art progression, too. Usually I tend to create album art at the end, and I use previous releases as a reference of what I do or don't want to do, and having to fit it in between two existing projects' styles, that's more of a headache as well. I'm happy with how Izalea Afterglow turned out, but that was one example too. I was trying to cater to an existing aesthetic of the surrounding albums that came before, and then eventually after, rather than to completely describe it's aesthetic on it's own. Izalea Afterglow was finalized after Ferret Train, so I think that example of me being more prepared to work on that project, that was because of the overwhelming grandiose-ness of Ferret Train, and I wanted something more simple to work on. I think that aspect of the process is important to note as well. I do like how all of this is explicit with the Bandcamp dates though, as it does track both really nice and easy in the metadata, published date versus release date. So in that regard, I might might might keep the old way. We'll see. Okay yeah that just made me rethink some things. I still don't like magically-appearing previously releases though, that's a bit annoying.

Just to note just in case, the original 'release date' for this was 3/31/26.

tracksInfo.title: Sigma Freud
tracksInfo.about:
This is the "single" for my "latest" "album". All of those are in quotes because this isn't a proper album by intent, I didn't release it in the order I made it (in relation to the other projects on my Bandcamp), and rather than being a single, it's moreso just what I feel is the definitive song for this group of songs, which is called an "album".

Hope that cleared things up (not trying to sound intense, it's just by nature of myself; but actually, yes this description has no meta-intent).

I did a huge description about the times this project was written during. Lots of personal growth and understanding. It covers why the art looks the way it does.

Yeah! So this is one of those in-progress incrementally-released projects of mine. It's where the content is something that felt more significant, not worthy of being glossed over. It also covers some great learning gaps as well, which hint at where I have been, am at, and will be headed into the future (both by recognition in the current moment, as well as reflective after). It seems to be both a step into new directions, a re-kindling with past openness and curiosity, while framing it in the perspective of the new things I've gathered as of the last year or two.

Hope you enjoy! This was one that I feel is very strong, even if not original in terms of my catalog and previous releases I've done. It kind of treads similar waters as past projects, but with a clearer prescription of glasses. But even with that being the case, I totally dig it.

title: Mudflap
about:
Found [a few] plugins on Tone3000, trying them out just to see what happens.

Using Bounce in Place for tracks to help working with stems a bit better. It helps for future mixes, as well as just archival without needing to worry about custom plugins being installed. I now see how this is super helpful.

I am monitoring not with flat EQ, merely just my MDR-7506s, while tracking and making tones. Going to use a separate ear for the mixing step, after going to have lunch.

Not sure the difference yet, but I have Focusrite AIR turned on, trying it out to see if I like it, and or if it does anything different.

I want to try out something along the lines of Keneally’s tone as well.

Oh yeah and this was all done on my Orville. Now about to track bass on my Ibanez SDGR.

I haven’t looked into bass tones on Tone3000 yet, I am curious if they have explored that too. Will have to try. Just been using the GB/Logic tones since forever. I haven’t had the ear for bass yet. Now it is getting there though!

Oh yeah and it’s called Mudflap because I was trying Fender amps and IRs haha.

Hello as of posting this song! Okay, so I had a full mix from using the monitors earlier, it felt a bit too bass heavy, so I adjusted things with my headphones after the fact. I fucking dig this song so much. The second mix/master has better mastering as well, in that the gain reduction is something I ended up looking into. It's more by plain feel as well as numbers, rather than just guesswork. Same with the gain and compression for the mix as well, I was looking more into that. So it has proper gain staging, compression to help each track fit in with one another (and allow it to pop, accordingly; less compression helps it stand out), and things like that. Then for mastering, I just brought up and down aspects of the mix to make it a little brighter and or things like that.

Made the artwork myself, did Photopea editing for it like my other work too. About to go post this to YouTube :D

This song is seemingly inspired by Waiting on Williams, and

Found [a few] plugins on Tone3000, trying them out just to see what happens.

Using Bounce in Place for tracks to help working with stems a bit better. It helps for future mixes, as well as just archival without needing to worry about custom plugins being installed. I now see how this is super helpful.

I am monitoring not with flat EQ, merely just my MDR-7506s, while tracking and making tones. Going to use a separate ear for the mixing step, after going to have lunch.

I want to try out something along the lines of Keneally’s tone as well.

Oh yeah and this was all done on my Orville. Now about to track bass on my Ibanez SDGR.

I haven’t looked into bass tones on Tone3000 yet, I am curious if they have explored that too. Will have to try. Just been using the GB/Logic tones since forever. I haven’t had the ear for bass yet. Now it is getting there though!

Oh yeah and it’s called Mudflap because I was trying Fender amps and IRs haha.

Hello as of posting this song! Okay, so I had a full mix from using the monitors earlier, it felt a bit too bass heavy, so I adjusted things with my headphones after the fact. I fucking dig this song so much. The second mix/master has better mastering as well, in that the gain reduction is something I ended up looking into. It's more by plain feel as well as numbers, rather than just guesswork. Same with the gain and compression for the mix as well, I was looking more into that.
