title: Recreational Outrage 2
about:
Edit Mar 2 '26:

FUCK, I didn't mean to press publish, it's not done yet! Well, whatever I guess lol.

edit: Okay, you can mark it as private again. Crisis averted. Not even that big of a deal, but whatever lol.

[Jan 27 '26]

Hello!

Had the sentiment today (I think the idea came about last night, and I wrote it down to come back to it?) to make a "Recreational Outrage 2". It seemed like something just as fucking funny as the original project itself. I don't like sequels because they seem lazy. So that's exactly why I'd have to make one.

And I think I am reaching something new with this one. It is going to be similar in spirit to the anything goes mentality of the original release, yet I am going to go all out on writing and demoing ideas. I will mix and master each song to the best of it's ability (as far as the piece goes). Then I will try out the tactics again from what I did around the so, many, bad, decisions era, which was to pick which songs made sense for the album, from out of the bunch. So while I am fully open-ended to how this project goes, it also has a slightly higher "standard" for how things will be when completed.

But with that in mind, this also takes a LOT of stress of when recording each track on it's own, because it doesn't need to *absolutely* end up on the final product. It may, or may not, depending on how I feel about the track and how it aligns with sibling tracks which will also be chosen.

I am also going to do this project in more private again, I am still documenting how it goes like I am doing here, but I won't release it on my page until it's finalized. I will make all of these notes as I go, I just won't make the project visible until after it comes together.

And yeah, about the low-stress recording for this, yes I think it could possibly provide more merit to WEIRDER tracks because of not having to make sure that it is something I like from the very beginning. So no "playing it safe" when tracking. That discernment has to occur after everything has been written.

I tracked two songs today. The first song is merely just not a song, and more like, some kind of nightmare. The second is a more straightforward track, which has downtuned guitars, and rhythmically solid too. I want this to be a high-caliber record in terms of production as well. Learned a lot over the last few weeks, and I can't wait to see what I do with all of that knowledge and new reference points, again with taking the guard rails off while using them. I absolutely loved "Recreational Outrage 1" from start to finish. It is so unique, to my feeling at least. The point or points that it expresses really aren't something I've quite covered yet. It's like a fairly obtuse statement that's difficult to discern.

Another interesting part for what's going into this record is that I am very curious about using genres to tell the cohesive "story"/sentiment, this time. I might not have to use that or decide to use that, but the door is open for it. I like the idea of using completely contrasting and "opposite" ideas to convey a certain sentiment of how one feels. Say like if the album opens very quiet, then changes to very loud metal. Then it goes into reggae, then a rap kind of song or something. The point for me at least though is not to have all of these on the album, but to onboard what each of these "musical genre tools" these genres provide, and borrow those to convey the obtusity to the hope of articulating that sentiment, which is hard to convey with a singular emotion.

This underlyingly however is indeed another open-ended record though, so it might not even be "weird". Or it may be only weird. Whatever the result is, there is no expectations going into this. It's a bit scary even, to some extent.

So this isn't really carrying on the story or sentiment from the previous iteration of this nomenclature, instead it is vitalizing figments of what I enjoyed about it, and trying to use those with the new pillars I've been learning. So maybe it's a lack of "critic" album, the first was much like this as well.

Falling asleep, get back to you later.

Oh and I think maybe trying to deal with the stress of world events and emotional strife, this mindset of where the first release came from is something I noticed I could build upon once again, now that things are stressful and out of my control.

I hope that sentence made sense. I am too tried to proofread to comprehend what I was trying to say. See you in the morning.

Edit Apr 25 '26:

["release date: 1/27/26"]

Okay, I am releasing this! Just full sent it. Had a great day outdoors today, I think the happiness and fun times just made me want to finalize this. Note that it's that I am comfortable with what it is, and what it isn't. I mean, if I wanted it to be more than it is, then it would not be done yet. But man, this is going to be another one that's going to be great to reflect back on, to see what worked, and what didn't.

It is much too late, I need to go to bed, should have gone to bed sooner. But this needed to be finalized, completed, bamboozled. I want to see this on vinyl. At least a single one-off copy for myself, at minimum. That was part of wanting to finish this, too, I guess, lol. That's why the running time is a bit shorter, 40 minutes is all Kunaki allows, so I made it work. This album is just as much as surprise to me as it probably is to you.

Note that I mostly "finished" this back in March or so, and I just did all of the final track crossfades and mastering editing tonight on the 25th, hence the release date. I am starting going forwards from now on (not like this is set in stone, but something to be aware of for myself, and to make note of) to make the release dates for projects when I actually release them, rather than when they were completed. I still want to make the distinction now that this was moreso a project from January through to March or so, and now it is representing April. But yeah, now I think it is something to represent something to reflect back on, now being in April (almost May!).

This project was both much easier, and much harder. I could delve into it, but I think I might come back to do such when I have more time available, and when I can reflect back on it again. Maybe I waited to finish this so I could have clearer ears and creative palette to release it. I actually do like that. I am less connected to the songs as I was a month ago. I still very much connect to them, but they aren't a representative state of my "now" experience, like how they are when you just wrote them. So that might be of interest as to what this album represents as well, which I will also go into.

Curious what you think!
Brandon

Edit: May 14

Hello, just wanted to make note of some other new things.

This album was "done writing" on March 15, '26. I have been going back and forth on how I plan to organize my catalog, in terms of when things are released, compared to when they were completed. A few weeks ago I reorganized everything on my Bandcamp from Progscapes onwards to reflect when it was actually posted, rather than when it was completed. I ended up changing it back today, to where things from that time period (then until now basically) to once again show the order that they were written-completed, rather than when they were published. I think it's because my "release drops" aren't completely official, in the literal sense. Say like how I publish albums before they are done, that sort of thing.

So that brings to question, where does that leave this project? I was about to move it back to the period it was written in, rather than when it was published. I like to see the ordering of when the writing occurred, rather than when it was published. But having said that, I absolutely see the necessity of organizing normally like by how things were released in. This was actually finalized, completed, made public, on the date that it's marked as. Hence, April 25, '26. But when looking back at my catalog, I get confused, as I see that Jung-L-Gym happened before the writing of Recr. 2, but that's not the case.

So I think I am just trying to discern that the process is very much very messy, and not congruent. I think I am trying to logically sort things which aren't inherently neat and tidy. And that's okay though.

I think maybe that's it. Going forwards, I will annotate when a release is from, regardless. And depending on the extent of what kinds of editing are done after the end of writing, that will determine when the release date applied is.

But again, any time I try to figure this out, none of it feels right, so fuck it.

Like I think I might even move this before Jung-L-Gym just to make it make sense in my mind, where the progression was. That's kind of part of the point of the work, for me I feel. I think that's been inherently true the entire time. The struggle is that when certain works feel complete, that takes varying durations, and they don't coincide at all. But viewing it outside of the writing order, it very much doesn't make much sense, at least to me. The whole point of what it means to me is the order it was written in. So I think I still will persist that to some extent.

I think I want to fall back into having a more tidy creative and or release schedule as well. I have so many projects up in the air right now, it's ridiculous. It makes it even more confusing how to manage all of this.

I have demos from 2025 from before Recreational Outrage, which span from after Compass, to Open Ears. I released a few singles around then, because I felt like sharing those ideas was paramount to that process. Now as a sorting of the catalog thing, I am curious whether to leave those there, and or just release the entire suite of projects as-is, leaving the singles there, and or, what do I put for the release date? I plan to use artwork I made that May as well, so that's not new either. I think I will use the historic release date that time, even though I just said I will try not to do that. The music is done, I am not fixing the mixes, it is merely like a stepping stone of a bunch of projects and ideas which were what led to Recr. 1.

Just sharing my ideas, it gets frustrating, overwhelming, and confusing. But that's okay. Much like one of the demos itself, I mentioned to myself that I don't have to explain what I am doing, I don't have to worry about what I am or am not doing, I just work out what will work best, then trust that path. That demo speaks real so much. There's even a song in there called "Perspective", which has been my favorite word as of the last few weeks. Amazing. It's like the past year has been filled with all of this hard work and growth. Doing so fucking well.

And it's gonna be called "AstroSurfing". It was an artwork I made while having a Moscow Mule on vacation, lol. I guess that's what that seemingly creative (AuDHD? idk) brain of mine does while drunk. I love the artwork. Haven't gotten to using it yet.

I haven't decided whether it will strictly be perceived as merely a compilation album, or if I should try to make it into a deliberate album. I don't want to fall into the trap I did with Catastrophic. I am feeling like this project is that if I am not careful. So I am actually thankful to have fallen into this "trap" again. I think there is definitely a fine line with under-baking and album, as well as over-baking. It has been all over the place for me. Recr. 2 kind of feels under-baked, but that's okay. Recr. 1 was just the right amount, chef's kiss. I think it's because I knew it was allowed to be under-baked going into it, so the ingredients really spiced things up. This one is a little lack-luster. But again, it's a sequel, and those are never as good as the first. And who fucking gives a crap anyways, it's not like anyone listens to my music anyways, right? (this sentence paves way for another project I am mentally working on, which needs more runway. So fucking excited for it. Note that the previous sentence I am not taking seriously, it is merely just one of the answers my brain spat out. Make Klishtas your Bitchtas, as they say; do they though? lol).

Edit: Turns out it was before the big road trip, there's a set of demos from around then. Those are separate to the trip. Then it was after the trip that the perspective changed, and that was what gave birth (wow a bit of an overstatement right? lol) to the growth that happened after that. So there's a seemingly unnamed group of songs from early April, then from May, June, and early July, those are what AstroSurfing is. I keep wanting to call it AstroSurfer, but the artwork says AstroSurfing. agh.

Edit Jul 12 '26:

Was having a crazy awesome concept discussion with GPT. The idea is about much of my work, and my relationship to it. The cliffs notes, to which more of this concept will be described and or articulated and embodied with future releases (whether intentional or not, that's also kind of the point), it's that we are trying to articulate our internal state as people, without the ability to access our minds, which are always changing, in a world where things are always changing, context plays a role in a perspective anyways, we are not "perfect" at conveying these things anyways, let alone if we could understand them in the first place. And we don't even know how to do things that would articulate the idea cleanly either, even if we knew what it was. And even then, it isn't going to be received or interpreted the same by other people, because of their difference of life experience, as well as what they are or aren't capable of understanding, both in themselves and in you and what your perspective might be. Let alone that they might understand something about you that you don't, which is a whole other layer too. So this release is actually fucking awesome, even if I thought it wasn't as good. Because it is the other side of the coin, how I "intentionally" sequenced the tracks, and "mixed it better". It's the same paradigm. "The point of this exercise is to accentuate the cheesier parts" to quote Devin Townsend, with my perspective now, whether I am intentional, learned more, didn't learn anything, all of this is still wildly inaccurate. There are always obstacles in the way, in that line of thinking. But the point of my goal here is actually to emphasize that this is all actually the point of my work, both in this series, and other facets of what I do. It's the awareness that we are only ever as good as we are and are able to be in that moment. So it's not that I am merely "doing whatever because that's what I can do", it's because it's the only thing I can do. I can only ever do what I can do. I can only ever understand what I understand. My goal with these projects is to emphasize that this is itself, perfect. Like, in the sense that that's exactly the experience. I am exactly what I can ever or will ever be or not be. That probably makes no sense. I swear it's like you can understand something, and not be able to describe it. I actually just fucking said that a few sentences ago, fuck. My work is the description of this state, that we are all living in. It's that the "now" is only ever what it can be. But what you arrange for future nows, in the now, that's what makes future nows different than current nows. But it's only ever now. I don't know how to describe this thing in my own words other than the concept of "here's the sound of someone who doesn't know how to record", "here's someone that tries to remix an album that they think could merely be fixed from the mix", "here's someone that writes an album thinking that they've figured it all out", "here's an album where someone has accepted that they can show their world exactly as it is, no matter what they do, whether they like it or not". I mean, we are doing that anyways, whether we are aware of it or not. I mean, like me writing this is implicitly telling of what I have been pondering. It implies how much sex I haven't had. That previous sentence implies that I am more okay with using words now. I don't judge myself anymore. That means the next album is going to be fucking bat shit fucking awesome. This series is the metacognative exploration of the understanding of what the scope is that we live our lives through, and that what we do or don't do merely exemplifies exactly what we are or aren't, again, whether we like it or not. And on top of that, "it's a moving target", so even the artistic expression of this scope, is inaccurate, because the visibility of this scope is always missing pieces. And our views about this scope change, as well as are ability to articulate those views, that also fluctuates. And the people who look at this interpretation are going through their own lenses as well, which are also always imperfect and fluctuating. But that's the point of this exercise. The explanation of that thing. We both have that same fluctuating lens. This is the same thing with how I view opinions and politics. Whoever anyone is, potentially one could say that they want the best of something, I would assume. They always want conclusion, peace, whether for themselves, for others, etc. If it's at the expense of other people, or of themselves, that's the changing of the lenses. The point is that getting to that state of 'conclusion' is seemingly the goal. Again, figuratively, people on opposing sides of a policy, they both want the country to get better. They just have different ways of viewing how that should be achieved. But again, they also have different objectives for what "better" is in the first place. So what would be a good conclusion for one person, is a different conclusion for another. And all of that goes back down to the perspective that they themselves uniquely have. So the point of empathy I hold myself to, in terms of navigating with people, is that everyone would empathize that we are all living through that lens experience, that's the common thing. It's not that the lenses are the same by any means, far from it. But the fact that we all have a specific lens, that's exactly the same. That's why I am so curious about others' viewpoints and perspectives, because so many different life paths and starting points, occurrences, biases, all of that is at play. The common thread is that we are all observing this experience of the universe. And even with things like animals, and people who have passed, ancestors, people we have never met. Empathize with them in that they are also "people"/"beings"/"eyes" who view the universe, and by that I mean experience.

Maybe I am just spiritual and I didn't know it, I don't fucking know. Lol. I was about to mention how we are just cameras living through meat sacks (Devin Townsend reference I think?) decorated with lights which sprinkle our influence all over the world. It's like we are cameras walking through a field, and we pick up a meat sack which influences how we see the experience. We didn't get to pick that meat sack. We then run through a field of pollen and thorns, picking up all and any of which cross our paths. And the ones we did or didn't miss also eat away at us, because we see the ones that others did or didn't pick up as well. But we can never truly look at ourselves through the eyes of others. Whenever a "mirror" is presented, say like reading our writing, looking at pictures of us, we only see us through our eyes. The point I am trying to make is that we are all cameras. Whether I decide to let my meat sack, pollen, thorns, or mirrors decide what I do, that is where I think the true you lies. I guess.

What the fuck was that.

I listened to Normalizer 2 all of the way through today. Fucking outstanding album. I already have loved Evidence of Humanity since about 2020 or 2021, so this is a long time coming. I think I did know that I wasn't quite ready for it yet, so I am glad I waited. Recreational Outrage 3 will be heavily inspired by the things I have been learning lately, this "camera"/lens based thing, as well as the push and pull of Normalizer 2, and how that kind of articulation describes things. But again, remember, I am not aware of myself fully, nor am I able to articulate it perfectly, nor am I able to mix it perfectly, and even then, it was still just a snapshot in time for a certain version of me. So, good luck with that fuckers. And you won't be able to get it anyways, because it's from my perspective. That was tongue in cheek by the way haha. I am getting so much more comfortable talking out of my ass! Yay!

"But everybody in the world's different point of view, could never see the world the same" -Devin Townsend

"
Not:
"I intentionally leave flaws."
More:
"I acknowledge that the work can never escape the conditions under which it was made."
" -Chat GPT

And on top of that, connecting back to being able to talk out of my ass, I am going to seemingly take things which I made from the first two albums, which felt too honest at the time, uncomfortable for me, and the things which were too absurd/out of place, and that will also be part of Recreational Outrage 3. Part of me tells me that's lazy. The other part says "remember, that's the rule. If it makes you uncomfortable, that's why you have to do it". I like that part of me. It's fucking right.

It's not that I'm lazy for using extra things. The fact that I would be uncomfortable doing it, that's also even the point of this project. Doing the very thing you are uncomfortable with. That's why I love this project so much as well, because it's always just out of my range. But that's why it keeps growing as well. And that's why I am so excited for it. It is breaking all of the rules. And even if it doesn't break the rules, it explains with satire that I am doing them anyways, in the face that breaking the rules because that's what you are supposed to do, that is also cliche. The whole fucking thing is cliche. Back down to the lens thing again.

Okay I am done talking, hope you have a night. Because a good night would be too much of a projection on my part. I am just talking out of my ass again. No joke, listen to some "intuitive energy healing", and lay down for sleep. It's the best fucking sleep I've had in years. Totally recommend it.

Brandon (formerly known as Mousecop)

tracksInfo.title: We Believe In Our Own Bullshit
Vata Kapha (Doctor's Orders)
tracksInfo.about:
[from the YouTube video I posted tonight on Feb 26, same day I made the seemingly final mix and master for this song; I am adding this song to the Bandcamp on the 26th as well]

Been working on what will eventually be Recreational Outrage 2, this is seemingly the first "complete song" that I have, which I am posting merely as some sort of single, or progress update. The song is kind of boring to be honest, definitely dark, and random.

I absolutely love the mix on this. Used my new headphones, in addition to virtual room monitoring as well. I think it helped be able to clear up some colliding frequencies. It sounds sick on a 5.1 system ('upscaled' of course).

This album has a LOT in store for it. This likely will be a transition song, maybe to reset the tone after something more taxing. I don't have a dedicated track order yet, I specifically want to do that when the album writing is seemingly done. I have 30 projects in the folder so far. Usually when writing in bulk like this (this is going back to how I used to write for HARRY, and prior), only 2/3 or 1/2 of the songs get used. Time will tell.

The name was randomly what I thought of while making it. I made it with GarageBand iOS, bounced the MIDI tracks to stems there, then did the mix and master in Logic.

This song reminds me of something from around 2023 I think, and something from Elkosaurus too, I can't quite put my finger on it. Let me know if your ear can figure it out. I think just using the samples I used to write with tends to elicit that kind of memory of the past. The glockenspiel reminds me of Carpincho, and the bass synth reminds me of Flatlands. So this song is kind of like a mishmash of songs from the past. Kind of neat. Now I want to write more GarageBand songs again, it's low-effort, and really fun. Even if it's not regular music, nor "good", it seems to really produce things which I remember and want to listen to again.

I used stereo panning for the panned instruments as well, I think that made it more sonically pleasing/realistic as well. I love the super light compression, and the gain staging feels really tight this time around. Really happy with the clarity yet dynamics at the same time. And I don't know if my ears are highly sensitive to certain tones, but 1khz and 3khz are handled nicely, they don't sting my ears when listening in the car. That seems to be a problem with big songs I love, as well as my earlier work as well. So maybe it's just a reference problem, maybe my car is specific at not handling those clashing frequencies well or something. And listening to this with a flat EQ curve helps too. Not that it's necessary, but I would come to presume that most music might sound better with it? Don't know where I sit with that yet. And I should have checked this song in mono, on my phone it seems to be a bit harsh, and maybe even clipping somehow, unless the stem bounces were like that, and maybe the mastering brought it to the forefront or something.

I worked on final mixing adjustments to set up for mastering, by adjusting levels by monitoring with a compressor. I didn't bounce with it, I merely mixed to ensure that nothing was too over-powered once compressed. That was a huge help here. The drums (hi-hat/cymbals) were a bit too prominent, so cutting that in EQ in the mixing phase helped a lot, specifically for mastering. I am trying to make more even mixes too, as I think I have tended to favor whatever instruments I just recorded last, rather than listening to the mix as an entire "thing". Some of the guitar tracks in other songs really benefitted from that, as of recent mixes.

Can't wait to see this release come to fruition! It's gonna be a bold one for sure. How can you really make a second Recreational Outrage? Must be pretty bold then, lol, heh.

The album doesn't have an intended release date, nor writing duration. It is open ended in how it will come about. It is the only thing I am working on right now though, so again, anything goes. This time, not everything has to get used though. And if it has to be a double album, so be it. But only if it warrants being one. I have been wanting to take like a year or two to make an album some time, as usually I work honestly probably too fast at it. But to each their own. I just want to try to make a solid statement sometime, in that it is heavily thought through. I don't know if I need that, but I want to try it. I don't know if it would be a straightforward album, or what. This is probably the longest duration project I've done in the last two years. I think Catastrophic took the longest, in practice. Well, maybe Elkosaurus. Just depends what metrics I guess. Elkosaurus was fragmented, it went and did whatever, much like this release probably and kind of intends to. Catastrophic was merely hoping to be just a guitar album, within reason. Eventually I want to get back into that again, I think the open-creativeness bug is still very much present though, so it's here to stay for the time being. But as the pendulum swings, the way I am writing this one is already closer to being a guitar album than the previous ones have been so far.

tracksInfo.title: Skyline
tracksInfo.about:
[from YouTube, Mar 2 '26, 4pm]

Okay, the latest installment of what's to come for Recreational Outrage 2. This one seemingly sounds kind of like early Porcupine Tree to me, reminds me of something off of Yellow Hedgerow Dreamscape in a way, at least that's kind of what the beat and composition kind of turned into. I just got Zappa/Beefheart/Mothers "Bongo Fury" today too, so I think that is already having an impression on me. Now I think I am starting to "get" Zappa. I admired the humor and the amount of people who love his work, I just didn't quite "get" it. Now it makes sense. At least with what I have gathered from it. The documentary from 2020 really helped a lot. Can't wait to check out more of his work, I'm only just getting started. I definitely hear where Keneally gets his inspirations from now. Much of what I gathered from Keneally was what he gathered from Zappa, I now see. I am thankful for both of them.

This is another installment of some of the songs I am making with my new Yamaha PSR-EW320. I love Marco Minnemann's "The Green Mindbomb", so I think part of wanting to get the keyboard was in relation to loving that album, too.

Thanks to Sketch Cassette II for really honing in to make things sound 80s. I wasn't planning for that out of the gate, but now I totally dig the aesthetic. Now I am very curious about maybe making my own synths which emulate something to the likes of mellotrons, merely because of the tape mystique. I could play just regular choir sounds, and put it through Sketch Cassette, then sample those, and use that as a keyboard in Logic Pro, for example. I could even use my Yamaha as the MIDI controller for it.

This song is the first that I have fully made with the keyboard. I didn't really have the best of times mixing it, I think because I don't know how the EQ and compression would work for each layer quite yet. That's alright, now I have come to really dig it. I intentionally didn't time-align things, while I could have, potentially, I wanted to practice playing in-time again, as I love that kind of writing.

I use the keyboard while hooked into Logic Pro, so I am monitoring the Mac from the keyboard speakers itself. I normalize the regions after I record them. Loopback is turned off, make sure to do that, or you accidentally record the metronome in the take itself, very intriguing, and could be very useful for certain applications, maybe like karaoke or something? I'd probably want to record stems if it were me, but maybe that's overkill lol. It probably is.

Then I mixed it with my Beyerdynamic DT 990 Pro 250 OHMs again, with the headphone imaging plugin from their website. It does help to hear it in a monitor-like setup. I am merely just trying to practice that, I haven't quite got the hang of it just yet, but man it does sound good for the first few tries. This and the previous song were done with them. I went and remixed a few others as well, those aren't up yet.

I wanted to share this one because I felt like making artwork for it, it felt like one of those classic-looking 'no-man'-esque 'Lasse Hoile'-style artwork would be applicable here. Hence, the sans-serif font as well.

As of the last few projects [albums], I also have been doing mastering separate from mixing, that has been helpful, as you use your ears more than your eyes. It also has made it crucial to understand what makes for a good mix. I haven't had the ear for that too much, so it's getting better. Today's mix could be a little better, but maybe that's why I ended up putting Sketch Cassette on it, to kind of hone in the demo kind of sound it has, whether intentional or not.

[edit after adding this to the w.i.p. Bandcamp]

This is also inspired by the industrial finds as of lately, namely Godflesh and Grotus to some extent. I listened to Streetcleaner more than anything else as of lately though, between the two. Grotus was neat, still deciding whether to get Streetcleaner. I like "Like Rats", the depth of the tone is sick as fuck. I don't like the remastered version as much, to each their own. I have been intrigued to find original masters of things as well, as I want to hear the closest version of what each artist had influence and ears around, to learn what they intentionally chose with it. I don't want to hear someone else's interpretation. Maybe once I get to know the album, that's one thing. I decided the same for Bongo Fury too, namely that I wanted to hear what Zappa heard it as. It is remastered from 2012, but I'll take what I can get. I would love to get to know the new Atmos one releasing on the 20th of this month, I just want to get familiar with what already has existed as well. That's how I connected with Bongo Fury specifically, I saw the mention about the 50th anniversary releasing this month.

My friend described this song as "glip gloopy", I love that. Great set of words to describe it. I fully agree, and stand by it. The source image for the demo art seemed to want to be called "sendoniso", I don't know why. So this song might end up being called "Sendoniso", or it might stay as "Skyline". I called it Skyline because I looked out at the window and saw a cool cloud while I was making this. It was around 1pm I think. Very nice say out, now it's kind of cloudy. I like that both of these two songs seem to be kind of trance-like, I keep playing them on loop and I don't get tired of them, I don't know why. Back to the PT reference, Skyline is kind of a neat reference to PT too, namely "We lost the skyline" the lyric. So that could be a cool nod to it as well.

Yeah so that British electronic-rooted trip hop, and industrial metal facets, that seems to be what this is rooted in, in one way or another. And the ending is having just listened to Bongo Fury, probably.

[edit 4:30 pm]

I totally dig no-man Wild Opera, so that's probably what this is kind of relating too as well. Let alone PT Signify, The Sky Moves Sideways (another sky reference lol), yeah. And I love Up The Downstair, this isn't in the same space kind of vibe as that though. Oh yeah and Orbit Orbit. Somehow that relates to this too, I heard Steven Wilson likes them too, so that's also a neat crossover. I found Orbit Orbit for $1 at a local book store, got it because of the artwork and liner notes, went in blind, it was a success. That was last spring just about.

tracksInfo.title: Kånoff
tracksInfo.about:
[Also from the YouTube video made for this. I posted the demo mix as-is from GarageBand. Hello from the night of March the 3rd! Almost sounds like a holiday in some regard. It's just a date]

Literally just hot off the press. Back to trying out using plainly just GarageBand iOS with my Scarlett, and Line 6 Spider IV. Yes, might be cheesy by some, but I actually kind of like the sound, I think production matters more than tone, in a lot of cases.

With that in mind, this hasn't been mixed at all, other than with my MDR-7506s without any EQ correction for monitoring. So the actual mix will be done in Logic Pro, and the drums will be rendered there as well. This is merely bounced directly from iOS at "Highest Quality" (256 kbps). I didn't even upscale to 48khz before muxing the video with ffmpeg (🥸). So YouTube probably reencoded the audio. Whatevz.

I think this is the first time I publicly shared the artwork for this project. It has already been done, maybe even before I started writing any of the songs. I think it's the first time I made artwork and concept before having written the music itself. The thing that makes that okay for a project like this, is that the scope of it is to allow it to be whatever it is, so with that being the only objective, it really isn't bad if it goes in ways that aren't predictable.

The Devin Townsend Podcast for Z2 today was great, go join dvn.fm if you haven't already! Listening to him again really makes me want to start recording some of those again. I think my head is in a better place now, merely in productive thinking, rather than bleak or negative thinking. It's trying to learn and understand the world, rather than critique it. Things are the way they are because that's how it came about, simple as that. If it were able to come about in some other way, it would have. But it didn't. So that's that. Now what are we to do about it going forward? Now that is the question, my friends.

Go listen to Bongo Fury, it's life changing! I got the standard edition from the regular 1975 masters, as I wanted to learn what Zappa's ear wanted to lead the album towards. Once I am familiar with that, then maybe I'd be open to checking out the new release coming out on the 20th.

With all of that in mind, I still want to get into mixing in Atmos and or 5.1 surround. It would be a whole new avenue to be creative in, can't wait! Even if it's just for mere sillyness, it would be awesome to make something like Elkosaurus, and or combined with something like Captain Beefheart, but in surround. Just complete wildness. And some kind of Bungle as well.

I have a slide whistle, and I still haven't properly used it on a record yet. I think when lyrics are fully involved, that's the same time the slide whistle comes out. Maybe the slide whistle can be an object that moves around the surround field when in Atmos. I think I know where my life's goals are heading now, it's all beginning to come clear now.

"I have a slide whistle, and I'm not afraid to use it!"
- Brandon Bennett

The song name is made up, I wanted to make something that looked and sounded Scandinavian, but didn't actually mean anything. I think it turned out well.
