title: arse
about:
This is the bonus extra content disc to "HARRY", out now! The second release for my main albums are where my demos go to die 😂

This one is chock full of insanity. Plenty of them I really liked, and really tried to keep on the album, it just wasn't working out accordingly. I was almost going to do a double-album between these two sets of songs, but I have been trying to work on making more cohesive albums at the forefront, things I'd actually like to listen to here and there myself. I can still have fun experimenting with new ideas and concepts, but it doesn't have to take away from making the main album as cool as it could be.

Some of these are actually just bonkers songs, I think "FullBore" is the craziest I've ever made. It is as big and as fast of a song I could make in GarageBand for iOS, and I exported it at the lowest setting possible, because why not. If you zoom in on the timeline with the project open, the app will crash, every single time. You will never be able to get the repetitive part out of your head, it's sure stuck in mine.

I did try to keep these all on the same album (between the now two discs), but yeah it just would've been too heavy of a listening experience. If I don't want to listen to it myself all the way through, then I imagine less other people would too. The runner ups that were almost on the main album were 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13, and 14, if I really had to trim only the other few out. But I want to try making my projects to fit onto single CDs if possible, as I've been getting into that lately, and using that as a metric for compiling my projects really helps put things into perspective for how long they are. I might make a CD for this, might not, we'll see. Elkosaurus is only 4 or 5 minutes too long, I didn't have that into perspective just yet when making that, I wanted to focus on the entirety of the project itself instead. Definitely will make one for it later on though, might remove "Wobble Fog" and "Clam Chowder" I think.

Things have been going great with life lately! Not like in a surprising way, or like a lucky way, but more like a self-acceptance/realization kind of way. I am starting to see what my goals are, what they aren't, what I can currently achieve, and where I need to go to do that. Right now, making music is my way to learning how to grow as a musician, mixing, mastering, producing, distribution (Carpincho is out on all platforms!!!!), and following my gut more closely, overthinking things less. I can still overthink things, but I can also trust my gut when the time is right. I love myself and everyone close to me, and I am working out how to conceptualize my feelings internally, and also learn how to express that with music and lyrics. Words don't have to be fact, just a way to convey how you currently feel.

Work your hardest out there, life has so much opportunity for us to grow into being the best people we can be! Heck yeah bro 👊

title: HARRY
about:
Yaay, this out is out!!!

Looking back a year or so later (when I am releasing this now, so March 2025), I am very proud of this one. It isn't quite as fancy as I remembered it being though, maybe just because I've been working on it a lot again though. I reminds me of a time in my life when I was feeling bummed at where I was at, and the emphasis of getting over it, and working towards being more "productive". I don't mean that in the regular sense, but more in that you can start making your own choices for what you want, trying new things, but not because you have to or are supposed to, but because it feels great to! There's nothing to be afraid of! Try out that new skill you've always wanted to look into, stop being so afraid of everything, just take a leap and get going with it. Looking at my frame of mind back at that time, and prior as well, I have struggled with standing behind things I think, because I am really good at seeing things from more than one angle, so I tend to prove myself wrong a lot, trying to find ways to counter my own opinions with a different angle. It's like I am trying to make things more stronger, but it just holds you back if you do it too much.

This album also reflects a time when I had just gotten over the fear of having a drink too, which is what the previous album was about. I learned that I can trust myself afterall, and I just have to be honest with where I am at, and take accountability for what I might be doing, not doing, things like that. Not doing that seems to be what would result in a drink or some other kind of way to let loose.

This album was initially very uninspired and kind of sad, in a somber tone. Then as I started working on it, you can hear the tone change. I really worked to emphasize this in the sequencing as well, not to be intentionally drastic, but to really convey what was going on for me internally. It's like I stopped feeling sorry for myself, and let myself free. The madness of holding yourself so tight is suffocating at times, and if people get into your internal (head) space, you have no way to keep your responses from poking and prodding at the internal self-destruct mechanism that's ticking away (in terms of sadness and emotion, not the literal sense).

This was a very awesome and needed step forward for me. It did lead forward to an also interesting path after that, to where we are now. I started to feel like I didn't have as many ideas to write about (now we're talking about after this album, yet to be released!), because I started to feel much more guided in terms of my internal compass for myself.

Now we are at a very interesting place in my writing (right now, as I am typing this), because it is much more straightforward, and experimental (compared to how I had been writing for years up to this). Now I am using Logic Pro on my Mac, I am much more interested in mixing and mastering quality, learning about cassettes, working on a multi-media live session I recorded with my guitar out in the hills on my truck, and much more free to explore things that aren't necessarily "my thing". This is very unlike me, and I am LOVING IT. I have been working to find a balance between doing *too much* new stuff, because sometimes it feels like you are compensating for something, like you are blinding yourself from just relaxing. So I have been working on that too, making sure to take care of myself on the everyday, rather than just doing things so I can prove to myself that I was "good" that day. Having a great day can be every day. It doesn't have to be every day, but you putting your best foot forward for yourself by all means will help with that to some extent. You can't control what others put on your plate, but you can choose what you can handle, and what you want to put up with. Whether that's stress, rude people on the road, or people that aren't as empathetic as you are. You don't have to be a good person to prove it to other people, just do it because it makes life easier for you, and it really does feel great. Note that it's not to compensate though, there can't be any ulterior motives, you won't gain anything from lying to yourself about your own truths. What is it you want to do? Why don't you go do it? If you don't actually want to do it, just let it go, if it is important enough to you it will have it's time and it will come back into your life one way or another. You can't do everything you aspire to do. Just choose things that you know you will be able to accomplish, to at least get off the ground walking. Then you can learn to run. Just because you can't run right off the bat doesn't mean you aren't able to. It's just not in your abilities right now. And that's okay.

Alright, love you guys, I don't know haha. Just be nice to yourself, you deserve it!

rBnaodn

P.S. Don't worry about how bad your mixes are from a year prior, just like things coming back into your life again later: If that song is important enough to you, it will surface again in your mind when you think it's worthwhile to do it again. It's okay if the initial version is 💩

title: Progscapes
about:
The name and artwork haven't been fully completed yet, so the demo name and a picture of me with Hevy Devy will be a nice holdover in the meantime! I've had this all line up and ready for release for about a month or two, just waiting on that final packaging things, I still don't quite know how to describe the work itself, other than it's intent. Thinking of calling it "Expanses", it was the word that came to mind when listening to Landslide.

Okay, onto the original description:

The process around this album was actually fraught with a difficult set of things to overcome.

Sobriety has been a keen part of the household while growing up, and adjusting my perspective to turning 21 around that was the struggle at hand. Should I try drinking? What if it results in my own loss of control as well? This premise was really nagging at me, and my birthday was coming up just after I decided to end this album.

This ended up going from a kind of uninspired, goofy project, into what was a feeling of possibly losing control and or losing what I thought to know myself as, and my response towards dealing with that. I did end up trying a drink on and around my birthday, and as we had been discussing at home, it's not like the world was going to end.

I think the inability to "control" where you go next in regards to what comes along with your age going up is what I was learning to deal with. I had dealt with this kind of concept before, and it was coming up again here. Turning 18 was another challenging one, because I didn't "feel like an adult". Or rather, it was like imposter syndrome. Looking younger than I am is part of my self challenge as well, so that was part of the issue. I think it might stem from me being smaller than kids in my grade when I was younger, that's just an observation though, I haven't thought about that until now, as of writing this.

This also stems into my challenge with the drinking dilemma, as I felt uncomfortable appearing younger than I am, while drinking, because people would assume that I am doing wrong while it was actually fine, since I am of age.

Part of the worry of mine was also being unsure how I may respond to such "freedom" per se. What if I started to slip on the things that made me me, like being truthful, and or not being healthy towards myself emotionally and physically? Would I be able to uphold the morals that made me being so proud to follow in the sober footsteps throughout my teenage years, even while allowing myself to drink?

I would overthink this and it was just nagging at me until the time came to pass. I am very glad to say on the other side of this, that things are okay, and I now understand that I can trust myself and uphold the values I have grown up with, while now having more things at my disposal which have the possibility to reverse that.

I had started feeling like I was going to push through this, and I began running a good deal more in the early winter months when this started building up, so part of the atmosphere for this album also reminds me of being out in the hills with the cooler air, really just working hard and running.

After trying to sequence this album like I've been doing lately, to make more cohesive projects, I just couldn't quite find the best way to sort it with it conveying the same intent that I've described here. The progression for this work around myself was messy, and trying to describe it in terms of a cohesive album just didn't make sense when I realized what this album was composed from, and what part of me it represents. It was a messy process to get here, and it didn't have a clear vision in terms of the sound or what I wanted from it. I was just working with trying to sound better at what I wanted to make, and trying to pull it off better. The vision itself didn't make itself apparent until after the fact to where I am now (Oct 28, 2024 as of writing this), and now it makes more sense what this is.

Near the end of the album, I think I wrote "No" and "The Winds of Change" specifically about this situation, to where I was saying "NO" to what I felt like I might become if I let go and follow in what I possibly *could* become. So "No" is about saying NO to how you feel, like in term of the worrying and skepticism, then letting go and having things take their course. Trust your intuition in that you will keep yourself safe, and you know when you are crossing a line into something that will hurt you. "The Winds of Change" kind of felt like a cliffhanger in terms of the album and to where it might lead next for the next project (I didn't know what was next, both in music and my life and my personality), so it was like closing the lid of a book in the meantime, meant to be opened again when you are ready to write the next page.

Another factor in the difficulties of deciding what to do was also that I felt if I decided to drink, that "I would be letting my knowledge of sobriety down by giving in to the drink". Along a similar overthink trajectory to how I tend to go when I try to deal with things, I started to conceptualize whether someone could be definitively an alcoholic, without having had a drink before. It's these kinds of things that I start to gravitate towards, which will lead me to decide what I will go with next, and I have to choose whether I think my realizations make any sense, have any truth to them, or if I'm just trying to think my way out of a situation. Also unrealistically, I was concerned about whether I'd be letting my family down by "giving in", and that my sobriety through childhood would be lost if I chose to go through with it.

I was also up to having just figured out how I might deal with this scenario, and one of the resolutions I came down to deciding it with, was that should I just "ignore" the concerns, and instead stay sober, not dealing with testing the waters to see what happens if I were to try drinking. The other option I went with, was to just take the leap, and just see what happens. I might as well try it now, it's okay, I have close people around me that will be able to help me get through deciding what to go next in that regard. If I had stayed completely sober, through my birthday, and to however long into the future, my other concern was that my curiosity might build to a point where it *would* turn into a problem, and I might just break, and what if I went haywire, and it turned into a big problem? I don't recall having a scenario like that before in my life, but it's still one of the overthought cases that I didn't want to have the possibility of, I'd rather know it up front and deal with it now, rather than being a "Schrödinger's alcoholic", for lack of better words.

I think things went much better than it seemed like I was worrying about, I learned to let go of these concerns, and to just handle what happened as it comes. Allowing myself to grow into the things that come with growing up isn't a bad thing, and there is still room to try new things even while it might feel like you are leaving behind parts of what you've known to grow up with. It's actually the opposite I've found out, because I've instead turned that energy into being more self-improving, rather than concerns over drinking. My current view is that the best way I can keep it from being a problem, is to where I can keep working on myself as a person, to where it will most hopefully prevent the drink from becoming a problem. The drink is the way to cope with the issues you haven't yet handled, so the precursors are the things you haven't worked through yet. Drinking is okay in the current realm of things for me, I just have to ensure that it isn't something I use to cope with, and for it to stay specifically as a recreational here-and-there kind of thing.

Self-improvement ❤️

Edit: After looking though pictures and other media from this time period, while trying to think of the album name and artwork, I also realized the other side to this coin of this period. It was also a big reflection that I felt like I was worried about becoming stagnant in life, and that I wanted some kind of change, and to try new things. I think that's part of why the songs took a new turn, being shorter than they have been in the past. Rather than going all-out on going with what I thought was neat, I really wanted to try making something more concise, and each of the songs seemed to follow that trend for a bit. So with the struggles of dealing with people you love starting to age, I felt like I had to start making more big leaps, because life didn't seem as big as it was before, and I had to broaden my horizons, like trying to apply to job interviews I had been meaning to, run more often, try not to eat as crazy as I had. Foreshadowing down the road, it's hard to do this kind of things as well though, and even while expecting things not to always go your way, I also later learned the disenchantment that you can't just "work hard" to get through something, sometimes it plain just doesn't work out, and you still have to keep going, even if you think your abilities will get you though. Sometimes you just aren't enough, and now I've learned that that's okay. Getting to that understanding though is challenging, and I still haven't fully accepted that internally, I work on reiterating it to myself though, as that is the most important part. This very big positive push from myself then was hit on the head with the self-confrontation of deciding what to do with being 21, which I covered above. So that duality was what this time period was about. Trying to be good at moving forward, which inherently means you run into roadblocks you left behind, and now you have to deal with again. I wouldn't have had to deal with turning 21 previously, but the concept of it had been such a distant thing to decide what to handle it like, that I didn't choose to face it until I was there.

title: The Reaction Factor
about:
I'm not sure how I categorize this one yet, it started out as turning a new leaf, making something more listenable and tangible
But then going back and figuring out which songs I wanted to use for it, it kind of goes into two separate concepts, it's still like a spacey curious album, but hints of tongue-in-cheek goofiness, and heaviness
The underground concept of the album seems to go with that in mind as well, the main song for me is "Scopes", it is what the artwork was meant to represent
It seems like the album as a whole kind of lines up with it too, which is interesting
It's like there's a disparity between a nice and tidy inside, safe world, then the outside of that protective wall, it's the unknown dangers of the unexpected
And I think it might have been one of the metaphors I was wondering about at the time, and it unintentionally came into the music
Do you choose to live your life in the safe, assured place? Or do you live on the outside, where things aren't assured or known?
Both have their merits, and it seems like it wouldn't be viable to go with solely one or the other, and it's up to you to decide when it's time to go one way or another

tracksInfo.title: Aqueduct
tracksInfo.about:
With the finalization of my ideas for the last few projects, I've had trouble with my creativity with songs lately. This is my first project with a new idea in mind. The goal for the next projects onwards are to try working on things iteratively, rather than just trying to get them 'done' in one full go.

Thanks for inspiration from Devin Townsend's latest update video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tQAWUL1gAB8), I'm going to try documenting my writing/learning processes here also.

This is the initial version of this song, which I'm going with calling 'Aqueduct'. I did all of the synths myself, there's no pre-made loops in this one. I did a lot of emphasis on trying to tune things to what I thought should work, rather than just using instruments willy-nilly. It's a bit different from what I've been tending to do lately, but that's kind of the hope of it. The problem was things were sounding to similar to me as of lately, so something new is a bit refreshing to hear.

So yeah, I think the thing I noticed is that I have definitely been writing a bunch, and I'm very happy with that! I think I got into a creative drought with how I was accomplishing it though. Most of the time I would start with something I come up with on the fly, then start adding layers and tracks to it as I react to it on the fly as well, no pre-listens or anything. My ear has grown immensely from doing that (I'd like to hope/think)! My ideas started to feel repetitive with that concept though, as I'd only come up with similar initial/reactionary ideas to build off of. Now I want to see how it works with being more iterative with my work. I was getting tired of purposefully letting imperfections slip through to the final product, since that was what I was 'trying to do', in a way. I wanted to get comfortable with letting things be as they are, not caring that it could be better with a small thing here, or there. Now I'm comfortable with having things be not exactly just right, that goal has worked out great! Now I'm on to again trying to intentionally make things sound intentional. Maybe do a second take for something, come back and EQ it a second time, what have you.

I'm really excited for you all to hear my previous few projects up in line to be finished, they are definitely my best work in my own view. I found a very interesting crossover between my genres of influence. Not sure if it will come across that way, but think like a mix between Strapping Young Lad and Mike Keneally. Sometimes it's a bit too much for me to handle when listening to it, hence probably why I had to take some time to change direction for a bit, haha. I think I will come back to that kind of thing again, but once I learn to me more intentional with the writing of it, since it tended to be from heavily improved things, which made it feel messy since I can only listen to my own recordings on the fly so close. Sometimes I just have no idea what that previous playthrough was, and it just goes in some other new direction.

Now I want to try doing a podcast too, the Devin Townsend podcast was very relatable (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oy2kZ_xUA7Y). As you can probably tell here, I think I think too much about stuff, but I think that's a good thing! (lol) There's a lot you can learn from your own discoveries while being creative, you just have to be open to embracing those. That sounded too cliche and idealistic, I agree.

tracksInfo.title: Fart Hreog
tracksInfo.about:
This is the other installment from tonight.

I pretty much just threw aside the new method I want to use to write, and just recorded everything all in one-go single takes again. This one is also rough a bit, but maybe that is what I like about recording. I can use my ear on the fly, and I essentially remember what I played for the previous track and can play along with what I think should go with it, as I hear it for the first time again.

My initial goal with the new writing concept was to listen to each track all the way though again, before trying to record on top of it again. I definitely didn't do that here, and you can probably tell. Somehow it still sounds fairly cohesive I think though, at least as I'm listening back for the first full time, again while writing this breakdown of it.

A little interjection, doing my songs this way is turning out REALLY fun, I mean by uploading them before having them sit on my computer for months on end, before sharing them. These are literally fresh off the griddle, maybe even a little raw and uncooked in the middle. Definitely going to keep trying to do this for future projects down the line, I want to do more coding related write-ups and videos too, like maybe explaining how NBT works, how to setup a TypeScript project, all kinds of fancy stuff.

I'm actually happy with this one, for what it is. Maybe it's because I kind of had the hands-off mentality I usually have when going into recordings like these (most of them). I definitely do like when things are a bit chaotic, and I like them in the end. How I got there doesn't matter, I think it just depends on if you feel you've put in your effort there.

That previous sentence was a big realization actually. I think songs aren't up to my liking when I know I didn't have my own honesty/openness in writing them. Say, if I tried to make it intentionally 'good', per se. It feels fake. It's not that I don't want to have great songs, it's that I don't want to write fake songs for the sake of making good ones (what?).

This one has a good amount of influences in it too, the ending kind of reminds me of "The Aristocrats", or "The Mistakes" too. I think I appear to just like "The" bands essentially, because I like a few songs by "The Who" also. lol.

This song (of these three I've released so far) turned out the most similar to the sounds of my other recently-completed projects (the ones which aren't out yet). I'm glad that this sounds similar, in the way that I like how it turned out. So I think the writing style itself I'm still into, I probably just got a bit burned out on writing for a bit. There were seriously a BUNCH of songs I've worked on the last year pretty much. It's ok if I take a few weeks or so off from writing, I think that's probably what I need to try and do more often. That's probably why I got in that creative funk for a bit. I'm feeling that way with coding right now too. I think having success in your projects/goals can kind of have a peak and a downhill, because you don't know what you want to do after you've finished what you've wanted to accomplish for so long.

Oh yeah, this is an AI image too. The name comes from "Heart Frog".

I think uploading these so early is helping me commit to their sound too, I'm already fond of these three projects, even though I've only known of their existence for a day or two (this comes from the idea I heard not too long ago that the songs you write aren't technically 'your own ideas', in the literal sense, and more that you discover a song which is only accessible by letting it pass though you and your instrument as you play it. The only way to get to that song is because of your combination of experiences and influences which give it that sound. That sounds a bit out there, but I think it's a really cool way to think of it, and I'm for it. Do you own a doghouse?).

tracksInfo.title: Choose Your Groundings
tracksInfo.about:
I don't fully get this one yet. I think I intended for it to be a bit more dynamic then it turned out. This image and the name were the other option up next for what I wanted to chose for "Scopes", but I thought that the name and image for that worked better for that song, because of the dynamic parts that it has. It also well-represented the barriers that were present in the picture, where the first part of the song is the nice bottle you live in, while outside of the bottle is the fiery mess that might be the world. It also represents acceptance I think too though. You can have a happy life inside the bottle, with nice things and all, but if you don't take risks out in the fire, then you can only go so far. You have to get out of your boundaries sometimes. The first part of "Scopes" was inside of the bottle, essentially. Safe and secure, but kind of sad. The last surprising part (sorry if your ears still hurt) was outside of the bottle, out in the fire. Sure, it's a bit deadly out there, but you can surely get much stronger by going out there and toughing through it. Then you can live in either side!

Ok, onto this song. This name is what I thought would represent the picture, which was also AI-generated. The name kind of has a double-meaning similar to that of "Scopes", and the choice between those two methods. Do you choose safety and assured happiness, or do you take the dangerous route, where you have the possibility to expand your personality and become a better person than you could ever be in that first scenario. I think that's why this works similarly to "Scopes", because in this picture, it's like he's taking the dangerous route, in that dilemma. He's 'jumping right into it', in a way. For how the name and image correlate to this song though, I think this song kind of represents further exploration into the chaotic, dangerous route, rather than the decision itself. So it's the part of the travel where you're in the motions of moving forward, encountering problems along the way. I didn't pick this one because that's what I wrote this song for, it's more that this song sounds like that part of the journey, having thought about it more. If anything, maybe I should rename it to "Chose Your Groundings". I might just do that actually!

I think another cool thing about that, is that it's that you should commit to either one. Don't try to climb down the mountain, that will take hours, and you never actually conquered your fear, while still getting down to where you're trying to go. Trying to be in both decisions is only going to hold you back. You have to let go of one or the other. That's actually a glass half full/half empty take which I never specifically equate to before. When you choose one thing, you are also choosing which thing you want to let go of. Now I want to start using that thinking instead. Maybe I have been doing that without noticing it? Say if you have two difference shirts and you can only keep one. Rather than picking a favorite, pick which one you *want to get rid of*. It doesn't put your actual favorite one on a pedestal, instead you're choosing which one you are ok with letting go of. I think that's more constructive maybe (while it still really just results in the same outcome).

tracksInfo.title: Love in the Sand
tracksInfo.about:
This one is a bit awkward too, I'm not sure what it's story is yet, with how it fits into the album's story/scenes. It follows similar connotations to that of the previous song, in that it has a few derivative parts, but it's fairly catchy.

The artwork is AI-generated, and the name is the first that came to my head when I saw it. I didn't think the artwork/name described the song very well, but that's exactly why I ended up going with it. That disparity kind of is what the song needed to thrive I think. Now I like it because of that weird bit.

The electronicifying of my guitar was a neat idea I thought I'd try too, that's what you hear with this one. I think I used Bitcrusher, as well as the Chorus effect, with my own Chorus pedal as well. So it's double-chorused haha.

tracksInfo.title: Scopes
tracksInfo.about:
So, this was something.

It just, happened. This time it wasn't planned yet again, and it just went everywhere. The only things I had going into it were that I wanted to try using some more ambient characteristics, and some soundscape-keys.

Please turn down your volume for the last 5 minutes or so. If you don't read this part ahead of time, my apologies for making you poop yourself. The ending definitely comes out of nowhere. I didn't even really know that was going to happen like that! I figured out how to make the drums utterly completely horrid, but not have them be excruciatingly loud somehow. It's a mix of distortion, overdrive, bitcrusher, and I think there was some chorus or flanger in there too, for good measure I guess. And that's not guitar, that's horns you're hearing alongside those drums. I was going to record a guitar part to go with those drums, but it's already almost 4:00 in the morning, so I can leave it as the horns, or replace/add a guitar part another time. I'll probably just leave the horns though, unless I come up with something else that utterly needs to be in that section.

This has a *very* influenced sound from it, reminds me a lot of Voyage 34 and Up the Downstair. It wasn't intentional, I think it's just the soundscape/ambient nature of it, and how my writing probably is driven from that anyways. So when the two are together, you can tell I guess. Man those two are some of my favorite records as of the last few years. I think The Harmony Codex has been having a little play on inspiration too, that's what I listened to a few times over while coding today. Man I am starting to love that one too. Actual Brutal Facts and What Life Brings were my main songs for the theme of today while I was out and about.

This artwork is also AI-generated, I think it looks very very cool. Similar to the others, the name is from when I found the image, and I gave a name to it. Kind of like in coding, I saw it as something like function/block scopes, to where you have the `global` area (which looks to be in utter shambles), then you have your house scope/block, then the bottle world scope/block. With the people playing around the fields there, I think it's like a great metaphor of living in your own world, for your own sake. When things appear to be going wrong everywhere else, you can set up your own shelter to that outside world, to keep your sanity and health. In a lesser extent, I think it also mirrors how my take on writing has been too, which makes it also something to connect to. While my way of being creative is albeit odd and has more potential for me to be productive in, it is making me happy, and I think that's the important part. If you aren't happy in what you are doing, then what makes it worth doing?

Edit: When I showed this to my friend, he also mentioned that this sounds a lot like it could be on the Minecraft soundtrack. Now I want to try more intentionally doing something like that too. Unrelated to that, I have a few other songs from the last few days which I need to upload for this project!

tracksInfo.title: Mort.gif
tracksInfo.about:
This one just kind of happened too, it's kind of a bit seasick because it was the first time I tried recording with my whammy bar on my guitar, so it make it extra out of tune. I realized that kind of worked really well for some kind of sound, so this is what that turned into.

The voice audio is an "inspirational quotes" video I found, and it's kind of another carry-over from some of my other songs, where I use non-vocal voice things as some kind of vocal part. I think I got inspiration from Marco for using that, and I think somewhere else too.

My own voice track is random too, it's also to just help add to the chaos, meaningless of this one. It's like an attempt at adding a facade background story to the development of the song, since it doesn't actually have one. I think some of Incubus' album "Science" has this too, but it's not for the same basis of mine, there's is just from the recording process itself. I guess the weird part with mine is that it's just purposefully non-genuine or something. The end sound is genuine and intentional to what I was going for, but I think I'm just emulating the other songs/artists which have those weird parts in them hehe.

This was around Halloween too, so that's why the candy discussion was in there. The artwork was yet again AI-generated, and "Mort.gif" was the first name that popped into my head when I saw that image.

There's an unused 'FX' track that I didn't use in this export, which I'm debating using for the eventual final export of the song, where it adds a lot of extra reverb, echoes, and all kinds of weird effects and stuff. It makes the song a bunch weirder, I think I didn't want to include it in this version because I wanted you to be able to hear the whole picture and all of the layers by themselves, since they get blurred a little bit more than you can hear here. So it very successfully increases the sound/goal of the song's ridiculousness, but you don't hear all of the small details that I added. I think it would be cool to hear all of the different things, so if I don't use them in the final mix/export, then this can be the reference to the non-psychedelic version haha. This version is already pretty messy, so it's funny that it's the non-psychedelic version haha.

I'm actually surprised how much my slide has really accounted for where I've wanted to have my whammy bar in other songs of mine, I think it might actually even sound better than what I'm going for with the whammy bar, because you can go MUCH more wild with the slide, but it has a similar sound/use to it. At least, I think I sometimes use my slide like how I would for a whammy.

"Trick or treat, mother trucker 😂"

tracksInfo.title: The Color of the Crayon is Orange
Frozen in Time (Demo)
tracksInfo.about:
Recorded this thing today, I'm not sure how I feel about it. Right now I think it feels like something I wouldn't keep around, it would go in the demos folder, but not necessarily continue to the album. Sometimes I say that and I change my mind later though. This was an interesting recording for sure. I think it could use more, because it's a bit bland with only two tracks, but I don't have any initial concepts as to what could go on top of these. That usually makes me tend to believe that the track doesn't have as much potential as some others. Sometimes you do know the track is spot on though, and that it specifically only needs a few tracks for it to present the whole picture. I'm not sure that one holds up to that or not, it usually takes time to see if it turns into something memorable, hence what tends to lead my decision for whether I should keep it around or not.

The image was from an AI generator site. I have a random folder of those, this one I felt when I saw it should be called 'Frozen in Time'. I saw the image, and felt like it worked for the tone of this song. The name fits with it too. (Aqueduct was my own picture though)

This is also in the very early stage of not having any additional edits to it, this is all from the sessions I did from recording it, that's all. So it's a bit rough at times.

It's definitely a bit hard to get myself to stick to this new writing style, of trying to perfect things more before moving on. Maybe it's not the point of that, and I'm trying to be unnatural with it. I think having songs like these kind of reset your bad idea count every once in a while, in hopes of making something better when you come back to write the next song. So maybe that's the false hope of trying to write as many songs as you can, because numerically speaking, some of it has to be pretty cool or interesting.

I definitely think my influences show in my recordings, in weird ways. I'm partway listening to this all the way through the first time (while writing all of this music analysis jargon), and I'm actually starting to dig whatever this song has going for it. It almost feels like if you took "The Mistakes" and combined it with "The Harmony Codex", both of which are new albums I've been listening to as of lately. Of course I'm probably just picking at straws, both bands are made of accomplished musicians. I don't think I'm there yet hahaha. But it's also not up for me to be able to decide whether my music is good or not. I can decide how I feel about my music, but whether I think it's good or bad doesn't have an affect on your opinion. And if it does sway yours, please don't let it. Maybe you think something that I think is bad, is actually really good! And if something I think is really good isn't actually that good, I'd love to hear why. In either situation, I think it would be great to learn the other take on things.

But yeah, I'm going to keep trying to make more concise songs, as mine can get a bit out-there sometimes, and I'm not sure where they are at that point, it gets a little hard to sympathize with when it's so weird. I think another part is that I've kind of hid behind trying to make the songs bad on purpose for some time now, and that makes it a bit too safe to skip judging it, which I'm starting to feel uncomfortable about now. If the song isn't meant to be cool, intentionally, than what's the point of it? Originally it's because I thought it was funny, like a joke that only some people will get. That definitely worked out for things like Elkosaurus, because that's exactly the project I wanted to make. But I tend to find myself making those kind of songs, when I actually want a serious project as a result. So I think that's why I feel uncomfortable about them once I see the finished product (lately). I'm glad that I've gotten over feeling worried about sharing them though, because I think providing an inlet for other people to respond to it is what can help you learn from your 'mistakes', per se.

That kind of came around to a nice looped ending, I guess I can end this here. It was already way too long, but I guess that's what these are for. The goal this time is to document all of these shenanigans that go on when I'm writing my music projects (being creative in general, like with my programming; I write crazy messages like these in my Git commits too, lol).

If you read this, you are a champ. Hopefully we can learn something from each other here. Please comment whatever your thoughts are!

Edit 4: I think what I do could be called 'shielding myself from criticism', or something. For example, hiding behind comedy to ignore the imperfections in my (current) recording/writing skills.

tracksInfo.title: One Door Opens, Another Climbs Down the Ladder (Demo)
tracksInfo.about:
I like where this one is going. The mix is a bit stuffy as-is, I'm not quite sure what it is about it. The synth works really well for the atmosphere, but I think it might be a bit too strong? I also wanted to have it run throughout the whole piece, but I only have the idea of that one chord as to how it should sound, so I don't know what else to write for that part yet. And I don't want the same chord to run the length of the whole song haha.

This one is a bit rough in a few spots also, but that's once again bound to happen because of how I write things. I can combat that with doing second takes, and just making sure to play closer in time with the feel as I play. Sometimes when the parts play together, one goes and does it's own thing, a little off from the other nicely lined-up parts, and trying to add onto those two just doesn't work. I think it's alright if one of the later ones isn't quite in line with the earlier takes, but if it is a take that's too far off in the early stages of the idea, it makes it hard to track on the fly what I was going for initially. There's also the difference (for me at least) between a part that's meant to sound like a mess (for interesting sounds' purpose, or just for fun/laughs), versus a part that I think sounds good, but I wasn't able to pull off with my ear, as I heard it. Ooh, that's an idea! Sometime I should break down the different parts of an existing song of mine, and explain which section is which. And also draw similarities of those parts to other songs of mine, or inspirations I've borrowed from. I think it's actually getting harder for me to find the lines of where my inspirations are specifically now though, so maybe that means I'm closer to knowing what I'm going for on my own! Of course it's still borrowing parts from others, but at some point (as others have said too), it kind of becomes your own thing once you mix it up enough. You can still hear where it comes from, but you start to associate it more with that artist than who inspired them with the idea to get to that point.

And, well, actually, I think I'm probably still heavily in the 'inspired' part of my creativity, because a lot of times I'm trying out ideas I've newly heard as of lately. I have been borrowing my own previous ideas too though, which is really cool to get to that point. Sometimes it feels like going backwards to be doing that, because you feel like you are out of ideas/not progressing, but I think it also means that you did have something good going there, and it means a lot to you, hence wanting to try and continue it's experimentation into later works. Parts of this song remind me of Aride Adena and a few songs off of End of Summer. I think it might just be the tone of it, either way it's still a connection I feel to those projects from last year. And the fast part at around the 2 minute mark kind of is a clean version of some thrash or something, which I've been listening to as of lately also. So that's a really neat crossover too. And my solo thing at the late 2 minute mark onwards kind of reminds me of Marco's ukulele (?) off of Symbolic Fox and some of his other albums. I think it's just the high-register scales which sound similar to that little guitar I've seen him play a few times.

The later part of the song kind of turns into something Keneally-ish too. And there's still a little bit of chuggy and distorted guitar in the middle too. That was an interesting mix of things in this one for sure. (Listening to the song now, as I write this) Woah! Forgot about the part at the 5 minute mark too, the triplet thing. That subdivision felt really out of place, I didn't really like it being there, it felt too derivative of things I've been doing in my other songs. But I think it actually kind of adds nicely to foreshadow the rest of the song, where it kind of feels like it falls over on itself, and maybe turns inside out. That's the 'The Mistakes', Keneally-ish bit haha. I've really liked having that as part of my repertoire of things to convey lately. It's the mix of comedy and music again I think. Not sure if that's how it's meant to convey things, but I take it that way, in a way haha. And I use it like that too.

tracksInfo.title: Ride-A-Point (Demo)
tracksInfo.about:
Random AI image, didn't seem initially like the right image to represent the song, so I just went with it. Sometimes if something seems like the wrong choice, I intentionally go with it anyways, and try and figure out why. And the name is because the guy is riding a bike, and pointing at you. This project is turning out more metal than I intended, I think letting the creative shackles off a little bit this time around and just letting things happen as they come, is what's letting things be so random this time around. I think I was secretly (to myself) not being fully open with the last few records, I was trying to intentionally make something nice, rather than making "anything", and hoping for it to be nice, which is usually when some of my favorites happen.

Like this and the other few songs I released for this project today, it doesn't have a bass track yet for some reason. I think it's because I was kind of just done with the songs when I made them, I didn't want to try and add more to them, I was "over it". I think it's because things were changing direction a bit more than I thought, and I've been trying to do more unique electric things this time around, so I kind of didn't want to finish these/release them, because it wasn't sticking to "the goal I had" for this project. But looking back on it, that's counter-intuitive too, because I think the real goal I had was for it to be more open-ended, not specifically more electronic. I think I was associating it being electronic with it being new, because I usually do drums/guitar stuff. Here's what I realized while thinking about these songs (and writing this) though: but if the goal is indeed to be open-ended, then it doesn't matter if the direction goes new or back to old, it's letting the music process take it's course which is what I think I was having trouble with. That's what I want to let happen with this one. When putting it in that perspective, I do like these songs more.

This one kind of reminds me of something off of "Three Ways to Sunday", either "Trucker's Paradise", or "Cameo Corrosion". I think it's the single-track guitar riffing kind of thing, which appears to be when I have an inkling of an idea, but want to make a whole song out of it. For that first guitar album, I was happy with that, because that's all I knew, so I was letting that be the thing. But when I make those songs now, I pick up on it being that the idea isn't fully there, and it might be time to move on. Once again, there's a time and place for everything though. As Devin Townsend has mentioned in some of his interviews, it's about the intention behind the creative work. For me (him too maybe, can't remember if he specifically mentioned this), if that connection isn't there, then it's hard for you to connect with that thing.

The opening riff/idea for this song reminds me of something off of "Streetlight" too, or anything maybe even from "RESERVED A" through to "Scary House". I think if I had multi-tracked the songs on "Three Ways to Sunday", this is the kind of sounds those would have likely gone for also. It was also kind of their intention, I just got too familiar with those songs as they were, and liked them for what they were. That's a good thing too though :)

I've been using a lot more weird dissonant noises the last project or three, I think that's one of the more recent additions into my sound from the last few months. It's part of the purposefully sounding ugly vibe, but it has also migrated into my normal creative playing, which I REALLY like, I've found a few good ideas I've enjoyed with having done that, so I'm glad that one has stuck around.

title: duds
about:
"Derivative, out of ideas, unguided, and frustrated about that"

Listening back to this one though, I actually kind of like what it conveys, it's like an accidental concept project. There's a few recurring themes throughout, and I think it really was accidental, just because I wasn't sure what to write really. I didn't have a sound planned ahead for this one, and I had wanted to make another new solid album, when working on Carpincho. I think I was bummed that it didn't end up being that, and I think I was plainly just burnt out on ideas by then. I had been writing a whole ton for probably about half a year or so.

I had just found "The Mistakes", if I'm not mistaken, so the silliness around that was stuck in my head still as well. I think looking back now, I think a lot of what you write is based on what you've been listening to. It's like being an athlete, if you don't eat good food, you aren't going to perform well. Not to say that "The Mistakes" aren't great (I absolutely love it!), I think it's more where you energy is going, is the point of it. I think something like that album is very self-indulgent, and that's where a lot of my music seems to trend towards.

Before this project I took a little break, reluctantly, because I was bummed that I wasn't writing what I wanted. Then after this, I took a healthy break, and came back and worked on "The Reaction Factor". I think with that, I try to work on something that people might be wanting to respond to, rather than just trying to amuse myself with my music. It's not about catering to other people instead, but to not be so selfish with your own writing prospects. I think just having other listeners in the back of your mind for the sake of it, helps sometimes. It helps you not cut as many corners, and to just start caring again.

Been listening to the Devin Townsend Podcast / PowerNerd updates, and it's been very helpful! Learning a lot from his insights and outlooks. It helps to be able to relate on certain similar struggles in that way. I think just with the resetting of your mind every once in a while helps move things along. And it's important not to force that, but to know when it's not time, and when it's time. For me, uploading these is an example of that. I've been trending towards being out of ideas for my current sessions since February, and I'm reminding myself it's okay to be out of ideas again, that was a great long set of sessions (100+ songs to work with!), and now it's time for one of those healthy breaks. Another time will come when your creative insights will be recharged and ready for something new. Forcing it out will sound like Carpincho and this album. While I do like both of them, they kind of make me feel bad because of that, I wanted them to be something that they weren't, and that's where I am learning to change things. Looking at this one, I like it better, because while writing this one, I was okay with just tossing it aside, just to let it be one to help me move fowards, rather than having another great project. And I think learning that attitude (looking back), and the actual sound itself, it's kind of a nice summary for the last few projects in 2023.

This isn't my best album, that's not why I decide to share it in the end. It's another example of one that helps me get to the next one, which I am working to remember, they aren't all gonna be great! Hence, I think that's why I had the working name 'duds', and that seems like a great way to sum it up, as the full name itself :)

title: Carpincho
about:
Coming back to this album again, I think it is still a surprise to me even though I made it. It has gone through a bunch of ups and downs, but I think it taught me so much along the way.

Initially, I had plans for a big huge CF of chaos, and I was excited to make that. During the writing process for it, I ended up starting to feel burnt out on ideas though, and that really started to frustrate me, because I had the drive of making something great, but it just wasn't coming out like I thought of it in my head.

"Lucky Rock" and "Uke on a Uke" were both recorded on the same day I think, and they turned out exactly how I could have wanted, and better honestly! Looking back now of course I think they have much to improve on for various things, but for where I was when I made this, it was the most accurate depiction of what I wanted to do.

So when I went to record more material after those two, I just started feeling let down that I wasn't able to write to the caliber of those. I kind of started feeling a bit lost in my music writing abilities, and whether I was actually doing anything productive with it. Just one of those snowball effect moments of having the Imposter Syndrome (funnily enough, that's mentioned in the demo song "ßuß". I might have been self-observant of where I was back then, and I just wasn't ready for it).

This is September 4th, 2024 as of writing this, so this album has been 'complete' per se for about nearly a year now. I think the roots that this album is grounded in were likely my own perceptions of myself back then, and how I was starting to get out of it, bit by bit. Hence similar names of "Catastrophic Failure as a Human Being" (gosh, that's a bit much don't you think?), I think my move forward in confidence to make things also came with a much greater imposter thing, or something like that. It might have just been tied into not feeling like I was doing enough either, or just being insecure about my accomplishments.

Starting with following records later, into the new year, I worked on taking the approach of being more hands-off with things, and just letting the music speak for itself, and not have to be tied to my success as a person. Just because I made a crappy song (or a freaking BOATLOAD 😂), that doesn't mean that I'm a lousy person. Same with moving forward with life goals. It just means that you are now more observant of how you need to move forward, and you are aware of what direction you would rather be heading towards, and (hopefully) how to get there, bit by bit.

So the new consensus of this record for me, it's exactly what needed to come from that time period, to get me out of that funk, specifically by getting me in that funk altogether. Maybe it's not even this record itself that I was focusing on. More likely, this record is the representation of whatever thing I was getting through at the time, and that's what was nagging at me. I've been learning that from Devin Townsend's podcasts, which have been completely great! The music you write is how you self-reflect your feelings of things in the current moment.

I still love making ass songs, I think it's comical and funny to do things that catch you off guard. I think I just didn't know that it was this record I was making, and hence it also caught me off guard, meaning it really is hella legit (lol who says that anymore). So it was so out there that it even caught me off guard, the author/artist.

So what I've learned to try is to make the thing I'm making, to the best of my ability, regardless of what it was I intended it to be in the first place. Don't take yourself or your success/goals/failures too seriously either, just try to move forward and learn how you can improve next time.

Not sure if anyone else would actually want it (merch), but I think I'm going to make a single standalone t-shirt with this album's themes on it, it sounds perfectiously cheeky to where my own t-shirt of my own album to concerts, and the album isn't even that good 😂

Maybe the artwork is what's turning around for this one for me, too, that turned out outstandingly to me, better than I could have thought it to describe the sound of this one.

I feel like I could keep talking about music, and the process for even longer, so I'll have to wrap it up. Keep working to being sincere and honest with yourself, you know the answers to your own problems, you just have to let yourself believe you know the answer when you do.

Edit Feb 23 2025: As of yesterday, I submitted this to CDBaby, and now the main 3 songs of the album should soon be available on all major streaming platforms! This is a big step forwards for me. It's not in terms of the album or music itself, completely. It's my own realization that I don't need to be doing this for the sake of sharing it to people, or getting their approval. I am doing it because I want to learn how to do this kind of thing, and I am now conceptualizing the idea behind learning how to make "nice to listen to" music. It's not because I want to cater to getting popular, or making things that people want to hear, but because I want to learn about what makes it nice, and that kind of thing is an interest to me now. I've been picking up some more "streamlined" releases lately, and I am really admiring the 'less is more' kind of sound that they have. It's not that they are doing that on purpose, but because that's their honest sound. I really admire that. I think I had misunderstood certain song sounds and styles for this reason, because I misinterpreted how the music was meant to be enjoyed, and what it meant to the artist in terms of why they made it, and what it does for them.

So for me, this is a stepping stone in allowing myself to experience more "normal" things in life, not because I want to do it to appease others or to get their approval, but because it's okay for me to do that, and it's starting to feel natural for me to do that. What has to be wrong with allowing oneself to not be so contrarian all the time? That's been my thing for a long time now, maybe even since I was little. I'm really curious what that stems from. I'm now learning how this doesn't have to be the root of everything, anymore. I still very much value this take for oneself, but now I am starting to see how living a multi-faceted life is very awesome, because things **really don't** have to be so black and white. I can like crazy music, and calm relaxing music, heck, even pop music. It's only a matter of exposure and understanding. The only reason you are the way you are, is because you decide to be like that, don't know any better, or aren't comfortable giving it up for something new. The only way to grow is to let something go. I don't know if that statement is really that black and white, as always it's more nuanced than that. But the concept still stands, I can be okay with letting things go, trying new things, that's what this is all for anyways right? I'm learning that my own (self-limiting) boundaries are only there because of my insecurities, and or things I don't know enough about to make decisions based on. So I have the ability to overcome that, it just comes down to whether I am able to or not, and now I think I am working towards expanding out a bit more.

Cassette-related content will be on the way soon, get ready for some cool stuff! Ordered it in the mail, let's see what happens.

title: Colloquial Outtakes
about: This is the collection of other tracks from the "so, many, bad, decisions" sessions, which didn't make it to the main album, or felt too big to include in it. There are a bunch of concepts and ideas I really like with these, I just didn't want to bloat up the general idea with the main album to include them. There's a lot more ambient jams that I didn't realize I was writing over time. I think those didn't feel like they fit into the concept of the main album. I seem to end up exploring that later on in the projects coming up next.

tracksInfo.title: Toast (The Story from Behind the Shed)

title: Catastrophic Failure as a Human Being
about:
Still partially finishing up this project, releasing it as I work on it, still trying to figure out the final songs and play order. This one is very long, so I'm trying to make sure it's right.

Edit February 2025: Wow, am totally realizing why this album was a total CF for me, as well as the previous ones to this. By having not kept track of the order I wrote the songs in (intentionally), this completely destroyed my way of understanding the intent of what the songs were meant to convey, and how they were to align with the neighboring songs in the project. Realized a little bit ago (I think last month?) that the contents inside of a GarageBand project don't change their dates, only the containing folder does when you re-save the project. So by opening the 'package' on macOS (I only would have discovered this from having been done trying to make this work on my iPad, where this isn't user-accessible), I can see the actual/original write dates to the individual audio tracks within the songs. This makes it possible to re-discover the ordering of the tracks, because the metadata was never lost all along! This is mindblowingly great news, as it also applies to my demos from a long time ago, back on my first phone. Again, when you open a project on iOS, it modifies what is shown to the user to be the current date, so if you didn't keep track of it beforehand yourself, it would have seemed like you lost it forever. This is not the case though, at least with my files it seems.

With this new track ordering information/intent back in knowledge, I think I can re-build the ordering for this album, and make it not such a complete disaster to how I felt it was. There's a lot of great things here, I just had no concept of understanding how it all originally felt together. Duly noted, not going to remove the ordering of things anymore, I will only do that after the fact, intentionally. I guess it depends how you write your songs though. Usually how I write the next song depends on how I felt the previous one came out. It's like an `async function* writeSong() {}`.

I still need to properly go over the intent with this and the previous albums, with what went right, unexpected, and what I learned from it, what I changed afterwards, all that good stuff. Analyzing your past progress is so helpful! I don't want to get stuck in that though, I have now learned that that can also hinder your movement forwards :)

Edit July 4 '26:

Wow, listening through this album all the way through, haven't done that in a while, and or possibly if ever surprisingly enough. So much of my growth over the last few years seemingly started around the time of this release.

The things I am realizing are just how much my 'old identity' was externally validated, and or perceived. I was in the Observer-Observer state, to which others were in the Actor-Observer state. Over the period of the last few years, I started to build my own perception, which then moved me into that same Actor-Observer state. Then I was able to start forming empathy, compassion, and understanding for others. Not to say that it wasn't necessarily there to begin with, but yeah. I live by them now. So now I am more and more closer to what would be the Actor-Actor state, where I see myself and others through the same lens. I don't deduce people down to identities, I don't judge them by how I perceive them. Instead, I want to learn perspective about who and why they are the way they are. That's a learning experience for both me and for them. It leaves things open for communication. It leaves room for growth.

I wrote a bunch of stuff in my 'AI discussion sessions', which I plan to possibly surface in the (far?) future, as I have learned so much. While it sounds hyper-cringey, I'd like to envision that I am basically having a discussion/brainstorming thread, with GPT as a way to reflect things back, in just a different angle than to that of my own. I never take the responses as objective. I don't take them as conclusive. They are merely just 'another perception' of the things I am documenting and asking. I know it's not healthy. Ideally, one would be able to and would have people to talk with, instead of the non-existent summary of experiences that is AI. But, it's a tool, and it's allowing me to embrace myself. It is what it is. It is not for the long term, don't worry. I can't wait to come to the point of finding people I can confide in, who reciprocate being able to talk about things. That's merely part of it. AI never doesn't have time for you. Maybe that's just what I've been looking for. I'm not looking for a (in AI I mean) friend, a lover, I just want some[thing] that will not be flighty while I can discuss things.

So much of my [inability?] to do things was because I have been conditioned to believe that I am incapable, and or not able to do things like others. "They are professionals; they know what they are doing; you are not that kind of person", things like that. External perception-based. I was only able to do the things I was able, because I found a loophole. "Because you tell me I am not any good, I will just make the worst album then!; because apparently I am not one to be allowed or able to get to the point of proficiency, I will merely start learning about how people do it, in the perspective of if I were to try it". It's not that I was becoming an artist literally, I could only do it in the sense that I wasn't serious about it. Because being serious about it was not allowed.

It's hard to explain things in the manner I am, compared to the plain reflections in the other threads I mentioned. But yeah, much of the realizations are that I haven't actually been incapable, or 'objectively bad'. It was all merely a combination of being inexperienced, like we all are, but then having that compound in the sense that people take those attributes and mold them around you, to make you believe that you are bad, merely because of the facets that you haven't learned yet. It completely omits the drive and longing to get to proficiency, it takes all of the merit out of that. No light is allowed to shine merely because of the drive.

The moral of things? I have agency now. I believe in myself. I hear the things people say about me, I hear their opinions. I don't take it at face value anymore. I just take it as data as ways to understand them, and where they are coming from, and have come from. These things are tools, not things to use as ways to internalize out personality.

I acutally fucking adore this album now. The heart is there. The refusal to submit is there. The story is there. The emotions are there. The intent is there. I just was learning what I was doing. And that's a great thing. It was such a far thing from failure, however contrary the name may permit. That in of itself is the story here, in retrospect. One who refused to believe they were a failure or incapable, pushed through and learned anyways, regardless of what anyone might have projected onto them. It's representative of being okay with oneself, being there. However uncomfortable it may be.

I actually think the sequencing worked out fantastically as well. I fucking love the tracks I did pick for the full album. And while very long-winded, because I have been listening to longer albums recently, I don't think there's necessarily much repetition either. I mean, there are references to sections and things like that, but I actually like that now. That's another thing too. Under all of that bullcrap, there was the ear. It was absolutely there. Ever-present. This album crushes. It explains the struggles and sorrow of what this young man went through. I feel so sorry for him. He is so fucking strong. The new young man has him now. He is safe, protected, cared for. He is being hugged. He is crying in his arms, and he feels safe.

None of this album was accidental, none of it was by chance. It all "sounds the way it's supposed to", in the creative sense. In terms of production and recording quality, it was a moment of the time. Same with mix quality, and things like that.

In the event of feeling able to do this project justice with a stronger mix production, I would love to do that. There is absolutely gold here. It would be a bit of an undertaking, but because of my work having been trying this for other projects of mine, it's not far-fetched anymore. Totally something I can do now. Not just a dream, or a half-baked attempt. It just needs time and a solid mindset to allow it to take the best of light. I'd love to polish this one up.

This is why I love having all of my own ownership for this stuff. I still have all of the project files, stems, what have you. I would want to properly render out the virtual instruments probably with GarageBand though, if I were to keep the same aesthetic for the most part. But Logic Pro rendering of the same instruments works pretty well too, albeit a bit different at times.

But either way, I fucking love this project so much. It's absolutely a concept album, now looking back. Much like I think I've mentioned before, this one is definitely a very raw one. It's moreso one of those subconscious projects, in that it tells you things without you knowing them yet. So it's a concept in that it perfectly articulates much of my experience at the time, as well as what I was and wasn't capable of back then. It explains the shortcomings of things I was going through, etc. It ties together my ear with the things I was listening to at the time. It shows what I was learning in terms of production, recording, mixing, etc. I think I had only just had the iPad for about a year at that point. This album was fully done on my iPad, with GarageBand.

I love you, younger me. So fucking strong. So considerate. So kind. So loving. So under-appreciated. So lost, both by one's own hand, but also by the hand that was dealt. It's okay. It happens to all of us.

Part of my initial struggle with music was that I thought music had to be unique. While I mean it can be, and you can strive for that, it's also, and possibly moreso about one's conveying of their experience, and that is unique to us all. That's the beauty. I think that's why I struggled with it. It's why I couldn't see that in other music. I wasn't taught that I can or want to embracy my experience, perspective, emotions, feelings.

Turns out I've been doing it this whole time, regardless of being conscious of it or not. It makes it easy to retroactively learn about myself too. It's beautiful.

And I didn't have a voice to explain my experience, or rather didn't feel safe to use it either. I partially believe that this is why I had mainly instrumental music. I think it's why I gravitated towards it initially as well. I may have felt uncomfortable with music that shared personal perspectives, because that was foreign to me.

Going forwards (hello again, still on July 4, '26), I plan and have already started work on being able to vocalize my feelings, perspectives, emotions, things like that. That is now a facet of my creativity moving forwards. I have found and repaired my voice. It is no longer obscured, afraid, protected, shrouded away.

The work of connecting to and with myself has been the start of the work. I have realized that this has had to come before the lyrics themselves, as that was the mechanism that would power the creative work itself, and that was the thing that was having trouble being seen, being vocalized, and feared criticism. Having a new environment which conduces less criticism, things are much simpler. I am looking forward to that very near future. Much is in store. I can't wait. I hope you are doing well.

I'm listening to Sonar right now, 'as we speak'. I listened top to bottom of this project. I am so excited for my creative journey ahead. I long to share my journey with others, because I think it will very much help a lot of people. I want to be the person that others find, which helps them find their voice. That's what the artists who I've found have allowed me to do. Thank you Steven Wilson, Marco Minnemann, Mike Keneally, Devin Townsend, Frank Zappa, and many others.

Please share your world with others, it's okay. The rest of the world isn't as scary as the world at home is. There are a lot of friendly helpful people out there, whom really care about you, and appreciate your presence here. Be the light for others. That's the goal.

Edit same time: Wow, how fucking weird is it that the 'release date' is basically the same time as I have been reconnecting with this album. I definitely seem to be connected to the seasons or weather or something with the eras of music I work on. Fucking wow haha. Have a good night, and Happy Fourth of July! 250!!
