title: Orange paradox
about:
This one is an interesting thing for me as well. I think it might be one of my most messy albums unintentionally as of the ones I've made so far.

I wasn't completely sure what the goal for this one was, and I think that showed. I didn't know where I was going next in terms of my writing. I think it's one of the low points of mine, in a good amount of areas. It's not fully something I like to listen to, other than a few parts, but I think that's also what I like about it. The fact it was not what I hoped it would turn out to be is also what led me forward in projects to follow onwards.

So yet again, as mentioned somewhere in the album itself, as well as the nature of the whole album, this is yet another paradox. Had this album been what I wanted to make, I would be happy with it. But then I wouldn't have moved onto new sounds, ideas, and concepts that I tried out later on.

The name itself came about randomly if I remember right, it was another one of those random things I came up with, and it somehow also ended up being the perfect way to describe the album and what it means to me.

I actually do like the creativity behind "Sizzelippe", and "Horse Scream (Ice Cream)". Both of which were made on the Mojave Trail, as well as all of the others, except the title track, "Toe Funk", and "Tumbleweed Scandal", which were recorded at home.

I think I also partially knew I had to have a stopgap project to figure things out. My writing and ideas were still a bit messy from "Sienna", and I still liked the absurdity from "You Singleton!!!". Honestly, I still really like that song hahaha (Hi! From Dec. 26, 2023). I think I managed to blend that one back into my songs again later on, which I think moved to a heavier sound in some aspects.

Like most of my projects still, I hold the bad parts near and dear to my heart still I think, and leaving behind the whole picture feels like a disservice to the point of what I'm doing here, so that's why I still finish these ones out. I'm not sure what I'm doing here, and I don't really get my goal completely, but not including them also feels wrong. Yet another paradox, look at that!

"Horse Scream (Ice Cream)" was another step forward for me, even for a silly song like that. I think it was the sonic quality of it. It started with the synth parts on my phone, then when I was back at home and could record with the song, I added the guitars in hopes of making the song "worse-ish", by making it unexpectedly heavy, since it didn't sound like it needed to be initially. I thought that contrast was funnily cool. Having experimented a little more on double-tracking with that, and some more panning/improved mixing, I really liked how much more filled-out it sounded, and I think that concept moved forward in inspiration for writing future songs, which is something I really do try and handle properly for more fleshed-out feeling songs. If I think a song is going somewhere, now I have been trying expand it with a little more wind in it's sails, make it something broader to listen to. I had done this with previous songs in the past as well, but not so as much with the more improvised works. Usually it was something shorter and riff-based. I realized I should try to do this with my longer songs as well, and to not have only a few single tracks for the final thing. Just having a better fleshed out mix and panning can do wonders to a song when it's only in the "potential" stage.

After having written the title song, I wasn't sure it was anything meaningful. Listening to it again now while writing this, it does point to the future a little bit, as well as back to the past in some spots.

I think while I don't fully like this project in a few different ways, I really found what I wanted to do next from it, because it showed me what I didn't like what I was doing. It's like how learning to do things the wrong way teaches you to do things the right way, that's an example of this lol.

Sure a fun journey!

I guess another thing I can mention is I think this was partially inspired by the craziness from Mike Keneally's work, but I feel like I didn't do it justice. I'm not sure. His goes all kind of different places, but you can tell of his confidence and charisma in making it. For this one, I don't think I was fully committed to the sound, or rather I wasn't sure if it was what I was going for.

So maybe it's not the work itself I'm criticizing here, but rather my own reflection of whether I felt confident in what I was making. It's a combination of that, as well as knowing what you wanted to make. It's the ability to make the work you do make, and to be able to stand behind it and say it's yours, and not be afraid of it. It also spurs down to my early projects like Elkosaurus where I intentionally wanted it to be bad. I think I wasn't confident in making something to my 100% at the time, so I didn't feel ready in being able to pull that off. I'm really glad that project happened as well, because I learned that not everything has to be perfect and just right. I think that's also part of why I didn't want to try my "100%" at a project, because I was going to work it to death in making it perfect, and I didn't yet know how to "just let things go". So I'm glad that I stepped over that boundary, because it has allowed me to do so much over the last few years (2 years now???).

I think this also comes back around to this project. I had become so used to accepting anything came my way in terms of quality and sound of my creativity, that I was starting to feel sick of hearing the "garbage" parts being left in. For the next project after this one, I wanted to continue writing a lot, but to allow me to have a much larger queue of great songs to choose from. I didn't want to keep the bad ones if they were just "alright". Throw out some of that picture of the whole thing, it's ok! Rather than having 3 albums/EPs with marginal songs mixed in with some gems, why not just work on the concept for a bit longer, and only keep the songs you really love? That's what I'm looking forward to show you over the next remaining projects from this year. I am actually looking forward to listening to those normally in the car!

Lots to say for this one, I can probably keep going. Gotta post this so I can move onto the next one though! My goal last year was to hopefully finish and upload all of my music up to what I had been writing, I'm almost there! These final projects are much bigger than this and the ones before it, so I think I am proud to say I moved a heck of a lot forward on that. It's okay if these last few go over after New Years, because I would rather ensure they are the great albums I hope they can be (hence recording more songs to pick better ones from), than to have it up in time, for the sake of completing my "resolution". I mainly had the resolution to get started on this anyways, since it was getting heavily worse with each new album I did. Adding more music to work on over time was getting both stressful to keep track of, as well as it being something I needed to come back and recount later. Going into 2024, I will be caught up on all of my projects again, since about 2020-21. I plan on releasing things in a timely fashion in relation to when I actually complete them, one at a time like a sane person would likely do. I will like to keep trying to make as many as I need to (need? this is a great outlet for me!) throughout the year, so I don't plan on trying to slow down on the concepts and releases or anything, but rather to complete and properly release things as they are finished, than leaving it to be handled by future me later. After these are all caught up, it may be fun to draw a chart of how messy this whole shebang was, to see where the projects were released in contrast to when they were made and or completed.

For reference, just last year, I was finishing up "Corruption Junction". That makes this the *20th* thing I've released/completed this year. I don't like number things like that, I'm not looking for a status with that. It's more a metric for myself to remind me to chillax a bit, because that's just ridiculous. I stress out about things being one way or another, I work on reminding myself it's alright.

title: Sienna
about:
This one was a bit of a mess honestly. I think I tried to let loose a bit again with this one, trying to make new kinds of sounds. Some parts really shine through, and I really like them. But others are just a bit sloppy I think. I kind of had a love-hate for this one, because when I started working on it, I wanted it to be a nice and clean album, but it's actually really gritty and dirty I think haha. But looking back on it as I post it, I think it's actually a very solid set of songs.

'Frogdad' wasn't going to be as experimental initially, it kind of just evolved into that. I think that kind of disappointed me initially once I finished it, because I thought I had taken the 'easy road' out again, by just goofing off rather than trying to make something tangibly nice. I think that's part of my love-hate relationship with my goofy sound, having made a lot more music since starting it. Now I think I know how to accept it, I just have to do it in combination with other songs with a more conceptual take. This album actually does that really well, thanks to songs like 'Carnigee Mellón', 'Spaghetti Nightmare' to some extent (it's a bit wild in some ways too hehe, I think it's a nice cross between the two, in a single song), and 'Fading Off Into Silence'. The last two songs were really one, and I had already planned on having them be two sections. Bandcamp didn't let that big of a single song to upload, so I ended up properly making them into two, rather than having a double-name. 'You Singleton!!!' is absolutely one of my favorites, that turned out miles better than I intended. I think I like what's going on there. I come back again to expand on that concept in future projects up. 'Loveland' turned out nice, but I was hoping it would've been more than it was. I think I didn't quite know the plan for that one when I made it, so it was a bit messy unintentionally, and I think that's what bugs me. I wish 'Trailerpark Lingerie' was a bit more also, the concept for that one was good haha. I wanted to make just a revolting song, hence the name. I didn't really know how to expand on it, I may come back to it again later on to finish that concept out. I think it relates to the absurdity of 'Farm Animal Gore' and songs like that, where they are essentially just meant to be putrid in nature. Oh yeah, and I know how lingerie is pronounced, but I kind of internally pronounce it 'linguree' just for the sake of it. Oh yeah and 'Carnigee Mellón' is another one of my broken analogies of some sort. Same with 'Frogdad' and 'Spaghetti Nightmare'. 'Ghost's Revival' is a reference to what I thought Opeth's Ghost Reveries was called. I think I had just found and been listening to Blackwater Park around this album and the previous one.

There were also a few other entertaining demos from these sessions, but the small bits that I do like aren't worth adding another 10 or 20 minutes of fluff just to get to those parts. I'm trying to limit the amount of fluff I keep through to the final result of my projects. It's still happening a bit for me I think, it just depends on the nature of the project I feel. If there's a concept I like, even if I didn't execute it fully, I'll usually try to keep it around if it isn't too burdensome to the listening experience. I had a few of those which I feel I should have probably trimmed out from projects like 'A Sight to Behold' and 'Scary House', which I think could've been much shorter and more streamlined without those in there. But since it was getting time-wise further away from when I actually made the project, I didn't want to filter everything out that made the project what it was. That's less of a problem as I finally catch up on my music, because I am trying to plan for not including fluff from the start, and I am getting a better idea as to what might be fluff before recording it. Or rather, if it isn't going anywhere, then I don't want to keep it around, even if it might be a good concept. I'm trying to focus on execution and completeness going forward. I also started (in projects coming up) just trying to make more, hence allowing me to drop more cruft, and have a bigger collection of better things, so it can still be a big project, but not have filler for the sake of it. I try to notice if it's a song I just want to skip. If it is, then it probably shouldn't be included in the final project.

title: Sponge, Assert, Expunge
about:
This one was a fun mix of songs, maybe almost a little too much. It also felt less unguided, similar to the last two projects. I wanted to improve my writing practices/creative decisions quality, but there wasn't a specific direction for the album. I think that sometimes can make things a challenge, when you want something new, but you aren't (initially) happy with what you've done. Coming back to it later, these songs are a continued step up in focus compared to my previous projects I think, and I'm really happy with that. It's okay that I wasn't completely sold on it at first, or that it didn't have an initial plan to start things off, sometimes that's exactly what you need. I ran into this again about a month ago (this is Nov. 2023 me writing here), and that let me start working on this 'The Reaction Factor' project, which I didn't have a direct plan for initially. So that break in a creative vision helped me try something new!

Coming back to these songs, I also find how much they really do mean to me, no matter how strong or not they are on their own. They really communicate things I don't know how to show, and they also greatly sum up my challenges and emotions throughout time as I go. I think if you can do that with music, then it really is working. The fact that I've done these makes me really happy, this is so much to get done, it's kind of crazy. Anyone can make songs like these, but they haven't, so that's saying something. <- someone has said this and I'm quoting them, I can't remember who it was unfortunately.

The name of this project was actually planned though. It was after the song itself (I'm not sure whether the rest of the songs work towards the meaning specifically though). But the concept is that I throughout my life's experiences, I sponge up information and learn things along the way. Be it, emotions, learning from misunderstandings, new skills, challenging situations or decisions, what have you. Then I write a project to represent that (assert it, 'speak' it), and somehow it conveys those things and gets them out of my system. Then I can expunge them from my backpack of things to deal with.

This seems to be very similar of a path that Devin Townsend takes with what his music means to him. It's actually mindblowing to me that I discovered this kind of way to deal with things, and then I later discovered Devin and his music after that. So I hadn't learned that from him, I hadn't dived into his work yet. I first *heard about* him around the time of working on 'Transcend', on a trip to Mammoth, but I didn't look into him yet. It's almost like finding him wasn't supposed to happen yet, because I needed to figure it out on my own first. Then his music has absolutely clicked for me the last few months, crazy how that works out. Weird things like that seem to happen without you knowing, it's funny when it happens when you keep your eye out for it. I don't know if it means anything, but it is a bit conspicuous for life to provide that to you, it is amazing.

tracksInfo.title: TragneTrake Hartbeet
tracksInfo.about:
Another name randomly derived from random thoughts, or 'Broken Analogies' if you'd prefer (That's the meaning behind that song name by the way, it's the method I use to make these weird names, I correlate more than one thing together which doesn't have a plainly visible correlation).

So for some reason it was a random name 'Train Track Heart Beat', then I spelt it wrong on purpose 'TragneTrake', and make 'Hart' like you hear 'Hartland' used sometimes (for random town names and such), and 'Beet' instead of 'Beat', like the vegetable 'beetroot'. I don't know either, man.

Didn't know what 'Hart' meant, looked into it with Google, turns out it's a male deer or stag. Who knew! Now 'Hartland' makes more sense, it's like 'the land of the deer'. Now I want to write that down as a song name. That might be reference to things write up here, if you end up seeing that name later, haha. That would make this broken analogy the spur for a new iteration of the naming vortex. That sounds cool too.

I was thinking of redoing this song again, while finalizing the trimming of this for this project, maybe that deer name can be used for the new version.

So the rule of thumb is to come up with a random set of words or sentence/analogy that doesn't really make sense, then add your own new layers of inside jokes to it, which don't have any real meaning other than that they are the joke themselves. I feel like this is why I find doghouse jokes funny. I think I've brought that up before too.

tracksInfo.title: Donkey Otay
tracksInfo.about:
A play on words for Don Quixote.

This was another interesting case of life kind of waving at me. I wrote this song, then gave it that goofy name. I didn't know what Don Quixote was about or what it was. Then I looked into the meaning, it was a book, and I think part of it happened to connect with the theme behind 'Sponge, Assert, Expunge' somehow. I can't find where it mentions how I noticed the connection between the two, but somehow it was also interestingly lining up together.

The song itself kind of feels a little derivative to me, but I think it actually might be an improvement over earlier material of mine that it comes from. So I think it's actually a good take on being derivative this time around. I think it also has some nice emotion behind it.

tracksInfo.title: Ughzaustæd
tracksInfo.about: This song kind of happened pretty much like an 'Elkosaurus' song, I just goofed around a bunch on my phone, made a bunch of ugly noises. It's a good ol' fun time hehe.

tracksInfo.title: Idle Chat
tracksInfo.about: I think this was kind of a reference back to 'Insensitive' in a way. I kind of wanted to write a dark song like that again. Maybe not necessarily heavy (it is heavy), but more dark in terms of what kind of feeling it exudes. It might actually hark back to 'RESERVED A' a bit also. I think this one in combination with 'Farm Animal Gore' is a slight hint as to where I started taking my writing here in the next few projects you will see soon too.

tracksInfo.about: I can't remember how I thought of it, but somehow this is based on a domino with 10 dots. There was some reason behind it. I think I thought of it during a run.

title: Nosebleed
about:
This is going great! I'm very relieved to be finally working on projects of mine from within the same year I made them. This one was also from the start of the year, around my birthday (two of the songs were made at the desert, 'Over the Ridge' was specifically on my birthday). I had a little idea that I mostly just tried on this album. The concept was to try making songs with non-instrumental things out in the world, and making music from them. It went interesting for sure, and it was a fun idea. I want to continue to expand on it, I think I just need to choose better sound sources. I really like how 'Sandy Suskatoon' turned out. We were walking around exploring some things around camp, and found an abandoned bunker thing, which had lots of old things there, I think people just left it there over time to kind of mess up the place. Kind of unfortunate and rude since it's just in the middle of the desert, but it looks cool so eeh haha. There was an old rusty metal spring mattress, and some sticks from a bush I found. That's what I was playing 'Sandy Suskatoon' on, it actually sounded really neat. 'Over the Ridge' was a stick too I think, on a metal post next to a dropdown in the canal. It didn't audibly sound that good to me, coming back to listen to that one, but it's key to the point of the project, and it sets the vibe accordingly, so I think it's a keeper. This was kind of an in-between projects project, and it was meant to be lighthearted and just a little simple. I think it works well for that.

The heavier songs were recorded just before the trip, as well as 'ROOOOaggh'. I was continuing to experiment on yet again more properly working on making a song-song, one that's memorable, and that actually sounds nice. I think my favorite is probably 'Pizza Carl'. I didn't want to push these smaller changes of ideas into the next new project just because this was small, I wanted that next one to have it's own feel, whenever it were to start fleshing out. That's part of what I've been learning with this. Sometimes your writing comes in waves. Posting these last three or four projects the last few days has come out of not having written too much the last few days, this is my choice instead of writing something new.

I also want to (realistically, it's ok if I don't fully complete everything) continue with the goal of maybe getting all of my projects up before the end of the year. That was my goal at the start of the new year, at least a glimmer of a thought. At that point, I didn't even have Bandcamp set up yet! So the mark of putting this project up, is where I was at the beginning of the year, when I made my Bandcamp at the first place. So, in Feburary, this was my newest project, and I was just posting 'Flatlands' on Bandcamp I'm pretty sure. It's hard to keep track of the timelines, since things are behind still. Looking through the pictures and screenshots on my phone, it I was working on 'Centerland' when I was posting 'Elkosaurus' to Bandcamp. So yeah, that's how that lines up.

I think my writing has definitely started to progress this year, I'm really happy I've continued just pumping out all of these projects. After these next few smaller ones, I have two more extra big ones (like 40 or 50 song ones 🤯), then I'm at what I've been writing the last few weeks lately. So I'm almost there! It's mid November too, so I have more time than I think. Not to say it's a lot, but it's not down to an unrealistic timeframe to be able to complete it. That's why I'm kind of pushing myself to get it out.

I think my goal for 2024 will likely be to release projects that I'm actively working on, to not be behind on it anymore. I think that will be another driving factor as to help bring the quality assurance and second-takes up a bit more. I will be more okay with taking time on things like album art and improved mixing because I don't need to catch up on getting things released. I still want to go back and make the best album art for the last 6 projects or so, they aren't completely done I feel. I really like how ones like 'Streetlight' and 'Elkosaurus' turned out. I think 'Elkosaurus' took the most time out of all of the album art, and 'Streetlight' actually didn't take too long. I think the instinct came really fast for how that one should look. I really like 'Emotional Literacy', I almost feel like the art looks too good to represent the music of the actual project haha.

Wow this went way too long.

One more thing I forgot to mention, the desert spot is actually not very far away from the cover art for Mike Keneally and Marco Minnemann's 'Evidence of Humanity' album, pretty neat. We didn't specifically go to where the people live out there, it's just that it's the same desert in general.

title: Centerland
about:
I think I've kind of forgotten how much this album was a big step forward for me, I think it really bring up the quality of things a bit compared to previous projects. This is the first time in all of my projects where I didn't keep track of the order I wrote the songs in, since I have always up until this point ordered the tracks on the albums as they happened when writing them. So this is the first time I made a purposeful run list as to what I think sounds good together. That was a new thing, and as well as the goal of the project to be on making something more streamlined/listenable. I think it still has my style all over it, maybe just a bit less of the weird/abstract parts. It still goes in a lot of different directions across the duration of the album, but I think it was purposefully a bit more contained this time. I'm really happy with how this turned out, as sometimes when I try to go for a specific goal, I end up veering of course, and it turns into something a bit less streamlined.

Things are still a little rough in that I don't really go back and perfect things later, like quantizing, or second takes for instruments, things like that. I still have liked that raw sound. As of writing this (Nov. 2023), I'm trying to work on those things a bit more, but this project wasn't too much with a concern for that yet still. The goal was instead for improving the listenability of the writing, to where it's something a bit better as to what you can follow.

tracksInfo.title: World Dominion (Guitar Radio)
tracksInfo.about: My guitar/amp/cable can partially pick up (AM?) radio channels on clear nights if I unplug it a little bit. This album was a big part to trying this little thing out again. I think I started doing it on the demos for Streetlight, but the song with that in it was a little long-winded, so it didn't make the cut for that album. This is when I thought it might be fun to try it out again.

tracksInfo.title: You Get What You Get (Take That!)
tracksInfo.about: A car past me on the way to work, going like 80 or 90 in a 60 mph zone, what a jerk. About 2 miles down the road, I saw him pulled over on the side of the road by a cop, heck yeah! That's what inspired this song, I wrote it when I got home after the shift, later that day.

tracksInfo.title: Doglin
tracksInfo.about: I think this might have been around the time I discovered a little bit of Opeth, and that kind of stuff, so the intro was kind of a mix of Steven Wilson-ish acoustic stuff, but with Opeth vibes, but not really because the tone doesn't really match that. But, yeah. This one is one of my favorites from the album. It kind of feels like it goes back to reference previous ideas, I think I hear some of RESERVED A in there somehow. And I think it foreshadows upcoming projects a little bit too; this one was a nice middle-ground of ideas in a way. At least it kind of feels like it's that way.

tracksInfo.title: Green Introspective Beings
tracksInfo.about:
This is such a great track in my opinion, it might be one of my favorite songs of mine/this album. I think I found Incubus - Science around the time of writing this one, so I think that inspired the oddness a little bit. The second half of the song is just something else, I don't really know how to describe it.

The story behind the song itself was not too much actually. It was extremely late at night, and I was literally about to go to bed. Then for some reason, I just thought of the phrase "We're like green, introspective beings", with that weird time signature and everything. I felt I had to record it exactly right then, because I definitely wasn't going to remember it or play it accordingly if I waited until later. That's usually how things go. Once the initial motif for the opening of the song was done, I pretty much just went all over the place with the song, didn't really have any idea where it was going or what it meant. Then it kind of found itself, and I just fully committed to the vibe. It's very dark. But it's kind of revitalizing too, it's really interesting. I think I had already started listening to Mike Keneally - Dog just a few months before that, to which I think this kind of also drew inspiration from "This Tastes Like A Hotel". I think I felt like I wanted to make a song that conveyed that kind of thing. I can't figure out how it links to it specifically, but a heavy amount of inspiration has come from the Porcupine Tree - Yellow Hedgerow Dreamscape album, so I think this kind of relates to my learnings from that too.

Come to think of it, it also kind of might spur inspiration from C418's soundtrack for The End in Minecraft. I wasn't intentionally going for that, but only that song is the other one which makes me feel like how this one does.

tracksInfo.title: Tyler
tracksInfo.about: Dedicated to my dear friend Tyler. You were the strongest, man. We all miss you.

title: Ooble? Yeah!
about:
The artwork for this is so bad I may have to keep it just because of that. I made it in like 5 minutes, and it was a goofy picture I took around the time I recorded this one.

This song was a one-off in addition with a few others, which was between the album cycles of the previous project, and the next one, which this one felt like it should be it's own thing. I didn't know what direction the next album was going to go in, so I didn't want to group this one with that once I started to work on it. I really like the quality of it, considering how quickly it came together, and since it's a little shorter of a song.

I think it felt like a new direction also because I didn't want to go with the all-in impromptu nature of the previous album, so I tried going for a (still) improvised sound and style, but with more of a goal of making it song-oriented, something that's less consuming to listen to. Sometimes some of my songs/projects are very big, in a sense, and they are very abstract. The nature of their incompleteness is almost like the feature of what it represents. From this time and onwards, I wanted to continue to try making more listenable songs, something that you might like to listen to again, rather than it being something of a musical challenge. I guess I was doing that with Lordsmith and a few of the other previous works, but I think I kind of felt like I went back to the abstract writing with Emotional Literacy. One example being that the concept for that album was intentionally to write an album all in one setting. It was less about the art first, and more about the exercise it seemed like. The sounds and ideas on that album I really like, but it kind of runs out of depth in some spots I think.

title: Streetlight
about:
Lol I've been putting no time into good album art recently.
This was the picture I took [for the artwork] which had the vibe for the title song of the album, and I recorded the song after seeing the lone streetlight out there in the distance.
It was a feeling I had coming home from work late at night, which I then tried writing a song for.

tracksInfo.title: TV World (Cover)
tracksInfo.about: Found this song from the 'Progressive Metal Compilation' playlist on YouTube, and it became one of my favorites from those songs. I decided it would be fun trying to cover it. I didn't go a great job at all though, so it didn't turn out really good (at all). But, since I want to share my music writing process as much as I can, I'm gonna keep it in the album anyways. I think the biggest holdup was that I couldn't find the actual lyrics for the song anywhere, so I didn't really know what to sing. I'm also not a singer (yet, hopefully! lol), so you can definitely hear that in the recording too. I recommend skipping this track if you don't at minimum find it amusing, it's definitely a bloody-ear listen haha.

title: A Sight to Behold
about:
Ok it's getting a lot easier to release these later albums, most of the songs were already leveled and everything, aaah! Not quite sure if it's the final artwork yet. I'm also not sure about the selected tracks yet, but I'm gonna try all of them because why not. Some of them make the length of the album a bit long-winded, but their vibe is really something else. And some of the ideas were incomplete too, but I'm gonna see how they fit in terms of making it an album.

The key tracks are
- A Sight to Behold
- Sunlight / Content
- Cheddar
- Some Kind of Potatoes
- Meridian

I'm not sure if I like/will keep 'Pug' or 'E', but I kind of just want to leave them because why not 🙂

The writing for the album started with 'Meridian', then 'A Sight to Behold' right after that. Those were on the same night! I didn't want to open the album with a dark song like 'Meridian' though, it doesn't quite fit the vibe for the rest of the album. But I might change that back around later, not sure. It sure as heck helped inspired a new writing kind for me though, so it's absolutely a keeper track as a whole, just not sure how to package it up.

Edit Sept 4 '26

Hello! Thinking about attempting a new version of the title track, merely a remix. Excited to see what comes of it. Realizing that when I do mixes, bouncing stems are crucial, it makes it much much much more deterministic. I didn't understand, nor have the setup to manage that amount of storage before. Thank goodness for *the future™*! In doing so, I realized I never actually saved or shared a copy of the lossless artwork, as I had made it. The project now uses the PNG from the PSD, rather than a PNG with *extra* banding. There's still some banding, that's because I did the gradient weird. Whatevz. Changing it would change how it was originally, so I am leaving it. Nowadays, I would do the gradient as a separate layer, rather than a fill on top of the base color. Now I can't change the dithering, that's what I'd want to fix.

I am doing all of this because I thought I might as well bounce stems *just in case* for Recreational Outrage 1. I love that album. I am content with keeping it 100% as is. I mean, I have *no choice*. But I might as well also make archives just in case in case in case, you know? I already burnt the bridges of my old GarageBand projects, I don't want to break my modern projects too.

Listening to some of my other stuff, it seems like my heavy-handed mastering seems to be the culprit more than anything. So, might have somewhat less work on my hands, in the concept of going back to adjust things later. Again, all up in the air. Just exploring my inclinations, not trying to do it from a place of "fixing", or "doing it right".

May end up just remastering the 2025 mix of Elkosaurus too, turns out that's essentially the only mishap from that project, I mastered it a bit fucked. I intentionally wanted to keep the OG mixes anyways, for the edginess of it. The songs which are different are seemingly already handled, if I remember right. So maybe it sounds different because it was rendered in Logic. Hey, not that big of a deal. At least it's lossless now, that's a good thing.

Note that I was okay with updating the art for this, because it was a distribution issue on my part, not intentional. I hadn't discerned nor was able to see the difference between lossy JPG back then. Say like for the revised Elkosaurus art, that was a total re-tooling of the original sources, so it was kind of significant. This is the same dimensions, same sources, no edits. Just a re-export at full quality. That's what I may just go and do for 2025 Elkosaurus, using the lossless mixes instead. Should I master it? What do you think? I mean, I will use limiting of course, but what about compression/EQ? Maybe just TDR Nova for dynamic EQ, maybe that's the only EQ I will use. Again, time will tell.

Okay, see ya soon!
Brandon

title: The Midranges
about:
Hello from Sept 2, 2026! This album has been up for much longer than that. Just stopped to say hello, as I listen to Jestershit.

Was wanting to listen to and reconnect to some of my older work, when it was 'less intentional'. I was about to get in bed for sleep, but felt like these late nights are great for the introspective, music reflection. It's cool enough out for the windows to open too, so maybe the fresh air is helping with that.

I came to talk about this album, but I think I am writing about the meta-level of my albums and how they connect and relate back to each other at times. I seemingly mentioned how part of Jestershit reminded me of this album, and I find that interesting.

I noticed that a lot of what I had described about that album, as well as this album, is how I also very much feel about Recreational Outrage: Volume Three. Not that these are non-releases, but that they are what I currently now would also describe as bridges to the things that come after.

I seemingly have felt very at peace with writing after having made and recorded Recreational Outrage: Volume Three. And interestingly enough, I can possibly see why, this time. It was because of the honesty I felt with it. I noticed in the description for Jestershit, where I described things as being a transition period, a place between places. I think that's where I am right now. It wasn't intentional, that is merely just the path I am on currently. I very much see the path forwards this time, and I am not afraid of it. I think there merely is more at play here to allow it to grow into what it will be though, so the next phase isn't concrete enough yet to be formed into something solidified. That's not good or bad, it's just how it feels. I both don't necessarily know how I would and or want to articulate what's next, and I don't have the drive to do so yet either. I want to be working on something, but this is where I actually feel heavily content with being not actively working on something right now. I keep getting inclinations of wanting to work on music, wanting to code, but I don't want to do the process. Not out of laziness or anything else, but merely just that other things are on the forefront. And if anything, that's a great thing. It's a testament to the fact that the music is helping get through this journey. This is also similar to what I mentioned on the info for Jestershit.

Plenty of these albums don't have descriptions yet. It's not because I don't have reasons for how they came about, and or what they mean to me. I think it just hasn't found it's place for me to be able to articulate it yet. so, many, bad, decisions is definitely an example of this. I have a LOT I want to say about that project, what stage of the process it was. I just haven't quite figured out the context yet.

I think what I now, in retrospect, felt about Recreational Outrage: Volume Three, is that it was meant to be a transitional release. Note that it's different in that it's 'what I wanted to make', versus what I needed to make, if that makes sense. It has elements of what I 'wanted to make', namely the more conventional songs. But also the truthful songs. I think this dilemma is also exemplary of that back and forth. This time, I was at peace with that dilemma though. And I was at peace that nothing had to come of that album. I specifically was okay with that. I now see that it was what the first album was, but now also with vulnerability, and truth. Looking back, there are parts of the recordings from the Recreational Outrage series, which didn't make the cut. Whether it was because it was (in retrospective observation) "too vulnerable", "unfinished", or merely just didn't fit the album, that was seemingly part of the parameters, to which I didn't see before. Now it is blatant. I was trying to make (and did, to the ultimate of my ability) a "no reservations album", and yet vulnerability was still reserved. Going forwards, this is a whole new avenue for me. I have mentioned things like lyrics. That is a skill in of itself, and or articulation (singing I mean, not just lyrics), but it is also a facet of my exploration of vulnerability. This is the next phase for me.

Now that shame, fear, being perceived in certain ways, or needing to 'make an album that is liked by people' is out of the window, I can also share my vulnerabilities now.

This very very interestingly connects back to "Emotional Literacy", in how I mentioned that I wanted to rename it back to the obscure title. I forgot about that. That was literally only a few months ago. Very interesting. Now I don't feel I am going to, or want to. That was a lot of growth. I specifically mentioned preferring to be obtuse/obscure with my messages, articulation, things like that. That has grown two-fold. So fucking thankful. I couldn't even fucking swear before. Cunty cunty cunty cunt. Sorry, I know that was a bit much. I just got impregnated by Ziltoid right there. Oops, wrong orifice!

But yeah. Now the next phase is both learning how to articulate using my voice, while also allowing the vulnerability itself to be a creative tool.

And, the later end goal, which I think will be more fulfilled or explored once all of the facets are present, and also able to exist together, would be the 'all emotions/all voices' album I keep talking about. I probably will try multiple variations of that, over the course of the next while. Who knows? Maybe the next thing will be the first attempt at that. That's not a hint, just an inclination I just felt. It is the 'simplest' path.

Picture how jarring Recr Vol 3 was. Picture that, but with vulnerability. I imagine like how the lyrics for SYL Shitstorm are (specifically 'I FUCKING HATE MYSELF'), yet also tied into something like DTP Grace, possibly. I am looking for internal first-person perspective stuff though, specifically (Stampys Blaster?). And the idea is that these are all of the same person, in their own mind. Not to be confused that these are different characters, and or people. This is one mind, and it's exploring all of the facets of the thoughts that go through this mind.

This is also lined up with where and why I am seemingly growing outside of music right now (not growing out of, merely just not active in currently), because coming to peace at being able to sit with these voices and or feelings or thoughts without letting them take hold, that is the goal. I have to let them be, without embodying them.

But yeah, I love Stampys Blaster so much. The intensity to which it, and Shitstorm, both push two totally different narratives, but with the same amount of force, unstoppable. Stampys Blaster was specifically when Devin's music clicked for me. We were listening to it on the way to Dreamsonic in 2023. Seemingly, the deluxe edition of Lightwork, since that was the newest release at the time. I already loved the album thus far, and the bonus Nightwork really pushed it over the edge for me. I could tell with earlier songs how this guy was so positive, yet had that 'realistic darkness' about him too. Love that. So glad I started with Lightwork. A great first reference. Not that it is 'the best', or 'definitive Devy', but in the sense that you really get the whole picture, all in one place. I feel like it's the accessible counterpart to Empath, if that makes sense. And that's a compliment, I might add. I love Empath. People unfamiliar with him might understand Lightwork a bit more though, on first gander of Devy. Then the hats for Bad Devil. I was sold, through and through. And the blatant honesty with the crowd. I think he called us boring. SOLD.

Okay, I am a bit lost now, just going to sleep now. Good talk, good talk. Love ya, see you soon.

Brandon

title: Elkosaurus Tex
about:
Alright, here we are with my seventh album! This one was recently recorded from Spring to Fall 2021. Ready for it? GOOD LUCK! This one is a wild ride, if you can hang on for 1:24 of playtime.
The main goal this time around: How bad can one make an album? Some parts shine through as pretty cool, and I like that.
This is not meant to be good, that's the point! So don't be worried if I think it's good, it's meant to be hilariously bad! I think it's amazing in the sense that it's a meme album.
The later portion of the album inspired my next direction in writing for the album after this, and I can't wait to finish the production for that one so I can show you it too! It has a much different writing purpose than this one does.

Edit Apr 13 2025:

Coming back to this later on, after listening to Larry the Silver Waterfowl (Park & Ride) from Carpincho, I had a realization. I think this counterpart to my writing is inspired heavily by Marco Minnemann's album Schattenspiel. I originally heard about it when we were getting into The Aristocrats, back when I was in middle school. I only had my own YouTube rip of the song "Sandwich" for the longest time. That song seems to be, looking back now, one of the biggest eye-openers for me to this kind of creativity. The way the song structure worked was like nothing I had ever heard before, the way he composed things around the drumset, which is the centerpiece of the song, rather than something like guitar or vocals. I had this song on repeat for the longest time, and I watched the video a lot. It wasn't until 2020 or 2021 that I remembered that I had never actually gotten into the full album. That was just after I had gotten into Marco's solo catalog too, so things were starting to click for me in that regard. Marco's catalog was the music theme of the pandemic for me, hands down. I think reintroducing myself with Schattenspiel at around that time resurfaced my interest in that kind of structure, and my realization that I had never tried that out before, even though I had loved it so much when I first found it. I think this album, and the style I ended up making out of it, I'd like to think could be a nod back to that. It did morph with my own style though, with the concept of making a "bad" album. It's like the song structure from that and the way the song is constructed is what I used to drive the process for this and the other albums early on. I think that video and song was fairly tongue-and-cheek driven to start with, but I feel I also added a little more of that into the mix. I was trying to paint a friendly omage to that, but with the concept of something like Eeps as well, where it intentionally sounded "bad", I think I heard Marco say at some point. So it's like if Eeps was constructed with the way Sandwich was, but also on a very low budget, aka just with GarageBand synth samples. That in and of itself is part of the joke for me too though, at least for Elkosaurus. Part of the initial joke that didn't get fully fleshed out (sadly) would also have been if I exported this album as full lossless, my thought for that being funny would be because the nerve of making the worst album ever, but then also having it be very high quality, now that's freaking hilarious. I think I still have that in the back of my mind actually, now that I'm more focused on lossless, mixing, and mastering, I definitely want to try making another horrible album sometime. Balls to the wall, yet high quality haha. Maybe it could be explicitly a double-album too. An unrelated realization right now too actually, Elkosaurus is meant to be light-hearted. Some of my work is a bit of a downer, at least sometimes it comes from a place of what might be despair, stress, or sadness. The pandemic likely was a driving factor in that regard, but Elkosaurus is meant to be humorous, not sickly self-indulgent, or self-harmful. Ah, that's the word, masochistic. I didn't want to be that. If I included something like Infinitrack, it would have raised the bar on that metric. Hence, that's why it wasn't included. This album still has it's lower parts, like around Hazy Light and Wobble Fog, but it doesn't get dark really.

I think the biggest struggle with making another ridiculous album, is it will be challenging not to make it intense. Say for example the parts on HARRY and Carpincho, it gets a bit dark and masochistic, not as light-hearted as Elkosaurus. I think maybe that's part of what I was bummed about with Carpincho, now that I think about it. But for HARRY, I was in some regard, embracing it/allowing it to flow. I wasn't trying to inflate it intentionally though, which Devin mentioned he did for SYL Alien. I was fine if it went there at times, but I didn't want it to get too crazy, and destroy itself (talking about HARRY). HARRY is probably the closest thing to Elkosaurus since the original, with a few other having some aspects borrowed too. Carpincho was like Elkosaurus unhinged. If anything, Carpincho is so short because I couldn't handle the extent it was getting to, so it had to be shorter. I just ran out of writing fuel to continue at that level of energy. It also would just not be fun to listen to if it kept going. It's like you feel sick or something. Now I can look back at it and stay separate from it, and I admire the honesty in what it conveys. It is very strong though. I do want to explore something like that again, it comes from a very specific place though, and you can't force it. That's the biggest thing I've been learning and have been making note of. What I write currently is what I write currently. I can't influence the style it is, I can only curate it to reflect it better to represent myself. That's okay. The time will come when the types of albums I want to make, can be made. It just involves a set of circumstances that will lead to that happening.

Love you!

Edit again today:

HARRY is also a bit more honest with how I was feeling at the time, mixed with that creative funness too. Maybe that's why I am really fond hearing it after the fact. It's very open, yet also light-hearted in that it doesn't worry about itself being open. Elkosaurus kind of lacks a vulnerability. It kind of is a very surface-level thing. It's great in what it is, but it has less for you to grab onto I feel. It does have it's honest parts though, I think nearing the end of the album it get's more open about feelings, almost like an inverse to HARRY, interestingly enough. I wonder if Elkosaurus is the beginning of an era, and HARRY is the end. I feel like Snake Oil is really the conclusion though, now that I'm seeing how things like that are. It depends on what aspect one looks at. It's a positive lookback though, none of these projects could have happened without the one before it. I wouldn't have them any other way ❤️

Edit 3 lol:

Listening to Carpincho, it was almost like a joke about myself at the time. I felt lost in my writing, be it life things, having been burnt out from writing a lot, or wanting to try something new but not having many other tools to use in that regard. So it's like I started to get self-conscious about my silly writing, because I was sad that "that's all I had" in my toolset. Once again, I really love Carpincho now, it's very strong in what it is and where it came from. Very transparent. It is just an analysis where it comes from internally though. Elkosaurus was interested in making that aesthetic intentionally, while Carpincho was like that because it was frustrated that it was the only thing I knew how to do. So it was more of a criticism of it itself. It was also with HARRY where I had been okay again with that style, and the style itself was interesting again in a light-hearted way. It was almost like a turning point of no longer being insecure about it, and embracing it in that regard. It wasn't the specific intent to be balls-to-the-wall for HARRY though, it was more about overcoming that insecurity itself, and allowing it to be all there too. Sometime in the future, I want to use my own self-confidence to make that bold statement, probably a heavy album, as well as a silly album. I'm not sure yet whether this will be the same project or not. Ideally it would be both, but I feel like having it combined could be new to me as well. I want to make something like Elkosaurus but also like "Maggot Twat", "clowncore", and "Time of Orchids - Melonwhisper".

title: Classic Projects
about:
If I were only including songs I think are "good for an album" by my current standards, this album probably wouldn't be a thing.

This is meant more for a look back to ideas and concepts that weren't part of an album goal, and were moreso just one-offs in concept, and showed what was coming up next in my writing. It's also kind of just an archive of the past in a way too, crazy that's the case now. I'm old haha!

These were all done with GarageBand on my iPhone, and I am only properly exporting them now as of recently, after having gone back and archived the .band files themselves. It's from early 2015 through to the start of 2020. Each of the dates is listed under each song individually if you are curious.

You can tell from how the writing here goes, and from the styles in general, it really does foreshadow into how my writing usually goes, and it sonically points into distant horizons that I cover later on. "Odd Ambient" for example was a fair ways before Septem Numero started, and looking back it sounds kind of like it would fit on that project in a way. The Guitar Improv projects were one of those too, I still tend to write in that fashion now sometimes, I just have improved my ability to listen and improvise with multitracking. I'd like to think my playing and concepts are a bit better nowadays haha. Some parts aren't too far off from how this sounds still though, so I am still feeling like I have a lot to improve on going forwards. I've felt like this for a while now, but now I am starting to notice more and more how my concepts aren't as fleshed out as I picture them to be. Now I am starting to have a stronger feeling that I want to ensure the final result is better aligned with how it's supposed to sound, execution wise and editing wise as well. I'm okay and still interested with experimenting and improvising, I just want to see if I can better hold the listener interested in that end result. If I'm writing my songs myself, and I can keep my own attention at times, then I can only imagine what other people feel. It's not wanting to cater to other's feelings, it's my own feelings that I'm not content with anymore. I guess that is a big step forward! It all starts there at least. You have to first confront yourself with your goals before you are able to change your output.

Might come up with a better name for this "album"/"release", right now it's just called Classic Projects. That does seem like a simple name for this though, it just makes sense at the same time.

title: Raise to Conflict
about:
One could call this my sixth album, recorded back in mid 2019! This was a project Justin and I started working on together, which just ended up being this song. I think it turned out great, so I thought I'd make it into its own album also.

Edit Sep. 9, 2025:

Going back through some files, organizing things into better archived folders. Had a thought that I might not have encoded the original file as nicely as it could have been. There is only merely a 320k MP3 file of this song which exists. I had converted it to M4A back when adding it to my library. Looking back now, my not too deep knowledge of audio formats means I probably took the MP3, reencoded it to AAC for my own use (M4A), then simply to upload to Bandcamp, just converted that to a WAV. Not necessary to have done that. Since there is only a source MP3 to my knowledge, today I reencoded that directly to a WAV file, omitting the extra compression step which had likely removed data making the lack of lossless even more apparent. Albeit probably not very noticeable, at least now the quality is partially better here. I now see that the recording itself isn't constructed fully enough to where it would "matter" too much, it really was just a fun demo, glad we recorded it. Still, even then, all the bytes we can muster, why not? :D
credits:
Guitar parts written by Brandon Bennett
Drum parts written by Justin Bedore

title: Distant Utopia
about: My fifth album, written back in late 2018! I felt like this project was a sequel/spin off of the last story, but in new waters (pun not intended). This has a dark and mysterious vibe of a successful utopia, which hides a greater evil underneath. This "take place under water", I guess, haha. I was going to continue this story, but I didn't do anything else with it since 2018. It was just on my computer until late 2021, when I decided to make it into its own album.

title: Spectrum
about: My fourth album, also released back in mid 2017! I wanted to extend my ideas from Septem Numero onwards, going to a new section of the story. This is a less-sad, yet still mysterious outlook from the last section. This is the last part of that story.

title: Septem Numero
about: My third album, released back in mid 2017! I started taking a new approach with this one. It's a space-themed kind of sound, and it's fairly mysterious...

title: LIVE @ MEDINA BLOCK
about:
Teenage Supremacy was a band a few of us from school were in together. We only played one live show, and there's not much to document it's existence, other than a few hard to find social media pages. I thought I'd bring this to light with a remaster from the video of the show, to hopefully make the audio a little easier to listen to. This is the only audio we have from our sessions for the most part, so there's only so much one can do to make the audio sound a little tidier. I tried my best with my limited knowledge in mastering, hope you enjoy!

- Brandon

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R_n7dfBztDw

Edit 6/4/26: Meant to do this for the past few months, ended up making a remaster remaster, essentially a 2nd remaster I mean. The one that I posted here from almost a year ago, it wasn't as nice as I intended it to be. I was doing it with un-EQ-ed headphones too, so that made it a bit more tinny than I intended (intinded? lol). This one adds a slight more low end, omits the stereo fix (keeps the OG feel, even if it is odd that the source was more on the right), and fixes some rumble in the upper bass. The sharpness of the original remaster was a bit taxing too, so that's addressed. And this one applies a bit more compression, now the peaks aren't as taxing either. Again, this was done with headphones, and the mix is set in stone, so probably still not 'perfect', whatever that might mean.
